10.16.e: Cool, Agni, and again refresh the spot which thou hast scorched and burnt.  Here let the water-lily grow, and tender grass and leafy herb.

10.16.d: शीतिके शीतिकावति हलादिके हलादिकावति | मण्डूक्या सुसं गम इमं सवग्निं हर्षय ||
10.16.e: O full of coolness, thou cool Plant, full of fresh moisture, freshening Herb,  Come hither with the female frog: fill with delight this Agni here.

10.17.d: तवष्टा दुहित्रे वहतुं कर्णोतीतीदं विश्वं भुवनंसमेति | यमस्य माता पर्युह्यमाना महो जाया विवस्वतोननाश ||
10.17.e: TVASTAR prepares the bridal of his Daughter: all the world hears the tidings and assembles.  But Yama's Mother, Spouse of great Vivasvān, vanished as she was carried to her dwelling.

10.17.d: अपागूहन्नम्र्तां मर्त्येभ्यः कर्त्वी सवर्णामददुर्विवस्वते | उताश्विनावभरद यत तदसीदजहादु दवामिथुना सरण्यूः ||
10.17.e: From mortal men they hid the Immortal Lady, made one like her and gave her to Vivasvān.  Saranyu brought to him the Aśvin brothers, and then deserted both twinned pairs of children.

10.17.d: पूषा तवेतश्च्यावयतु पर विद्वाननष्टपशुर्भुवनस्य गोपाः | स तवैतेभ्यः परि ददत पित्र्भ्यो.अग्निर्देवेभ्यः सुविदत्रियेभ्यः ||
10.17.e: Guard of the world, whose cattle ne’er are injured, may Pūṣan bear thee hence, for he hath knowledge.  May he consign thee to these Fathers' keeping, and to the gracious Gods let Agni give thee.

10.17.d: आयुर्विश्वायुः परि पासति तवा पूषा तवा पातु परपथेपुरस्तात | यत्रसते सुक्र्तो यत्र ते ययुस्तत्र तवादेवः सविता दधातु ||
10.17.e: May Āyu, giver of all life, protect thee, and bear thee forward on the distant pathway.  Thither let Savitar the God transport thee, where dwell the pious who have passed-before thee.

10.17.d: पूषेमा आशा अनु वेद सर्वाः सो अस्मानभयतमेननेषत | सवस्तिदा आघ्र्णिः सर्ववीरो.अप्रयुछन पुर एतुप्रजानन ||
10.17.e: Pūṣan knows all these realms: may he conduct us by ways that are most free from fear and danger.  Giver of blessings, glowing, all-heroic, may he, thewise and watchful, go before us.

10.17.d: परपथे पथमजनिष्ट पूषा परपथे दिवः परपथेप्र्थिव्याः | उभे अभि परियतमे सधस्थे आ च परा चचरति परजानन ||
10.17.e: Pūṣan was born to move on distant pathways, on the road far from earth and far from heaven.  To both most wonted places of assembly he travels and returns with perfect knowledge.

10.17.d: सरस्वतीं देवयन्तो हवन्ते सरस्वतीमध्वरे तायमाने | सरस्वतीं सुक्र्तो अह्वयन्त सरस्वती दाशुषे वार्यं दात ||
10.17.e: The pious call Sarasvatī, they worship Sarasvatī while sacrifice proceedeth.  The pious called Sarasvatī aforetime. Sarasvatī send bliss to him who giveth.

10.17.d: सरस्वति या सरथं ययथ सवधाभिर्देवि पित्र्भिर्मदन्ती | आसद्यास्मिन बर्हिषि मादयस्वानमीवा इष आधेह्यस्मे ||
10.17.e: Sarasvatī, who camest with the Fathers, with them rejoicing thee in our oblations,  Seated upon this sacred grass be joyful, and give us strengthening food that brings no sickness.

10.17.d: सरस्वतीं यां पितरो हवन्ते दक्षिणा यज्ञमभिनक्षमाणाः | सहस्रार्घमिळो अत्र भागं रायस्पोषं यजमानेषु धेहि ||
10.17.e: Thou, called on as Sarasvatī by Fathers who come right forward to our solemn service,  Give food and wealth to present sacrificers, a portion, worth a thousand, of refreshment.

10.17.d: अपो अस्मान मातरः शुन्धयन्तु घर्तेन नो घर्तप्वः पुनन्तु | विश्वं हि रिप्रं परवहन्ति देविरुदिदाभ्यः शुचिरापूत एमि ||
10.17.e: The Mother Floods shall make us bright and shining, cleansers of holy oil, with oil shall cleanse us:  For, Goddesses, they bear off all defilement: I, rise up from them purified and brightened.

10.17.d: दरप्सश्चस्कन्द परथमाननु दयूनिमं च योनिमनु यश्च पुर्वः | समानं योनिमनु संचरन्तं दरप्सं जुहोम्यनु सप्त होत्राः ||
10.17.e: Through days of earliest date the Drop descended on this place and on that which was before it.  I offer up, throughout the seven oblations, the Drop which still to one same place is moving.

10.17.d: यस्ते दरप्स सकन्दति यस्ते अंशुर्बाहुच्युतो धिषणायाुपस्थात | अध्वर्योर्वा परि वा यः पवित्रात तं ते जुहोमिमनसा वषट्क्र्तम ||
10.17.e: The Drop that falls, thy stalk which arms have shaken, which from the bosom of the press hath fallen,  Or from the Adhvaryu's purifying filter, I offer thee with heart and cry of Vaṣaṭ!

10.17.d: यस्ते दरप्स सकन्नो यस्ते अंशुरवश्च यः परःस्रुचा | अयं देवो बर्हस्पतिः सं तं सिञ्चतु राधसे ||
10.17.e: That fallen Drop of thine, the stalk which from the ladle fell away,  This present God Bṛhaspati shall pour it forth to make us rich.

10.17.d: पयस्वतीरोषधयः पयस्वन मामकं वचः | अपाम्पयस्वदित पयस्तेन मा सह शुन्धत ||
10.17.e: The plants of earth are rich in milk, and rich in milk is this my speech;  And rich in milk the essence of the Waters: make me pure therewith.

10.18.d: परं मर्त्यो अनु परेहि पन्थां यस्ते सव इतरो देवयानात | चक्षुष्मते शर्ण्वते ते बरवीमि मा नः परजां रीरिषोमोत वीरान ||
10.18.e: Go hence, O Death, pursue thy special pathway apart from that which Gods are wont to travel.  To thee I say it who hast eyes and hearest: Touch not our offspring, injure not our heroes.

10.18.d: मर्त्योः पदं योपयन्तो यदैत दराघीय आयुः परतरन्दधानाः | आप्यायमानाः परजया धनेन शुद्धाःपूता भवत यज्ञियासः ||
10.18.e: As ye have come effacing Mrtyu's footstep, to further times prolonging your existence,  May ye be rich in children and possessions. cleansed, purified, and meet for sacrificing.

10.18.d: इमे जीवा वि मर्तैरावव्र्त्रन्नभूद भद्रा देवहूतिर्नोद्य | पराञ्चो अगाम नर्तये हसाय दराघीय आयुःप्रतरं दधानाः ||
10.18.e: Divided from the dead are these, the living: now be our calling on the Gods successful.  We have gone forth for dancing and for laughter, tofurther times prolonging our existence.

10.18.d: इमं जीवेभ्यः परिधिं दधामि मैषां नु गादपरोर्थमेतम | शतं जीवन्तु शरदः पुरूचीरन्तर्म्र्त्युं दधतां पर्वतेन ||
10.18.e: Here I erect this rampart for the living; let none of these, none other, reach this limit.  May they survive a hundred lengthened autumns, and may they bury Death beneath this mountain.

10.18.d: यथाहान्यनुपूर्वं भवन्ति यथ रतव रतुभिर्यन्तिसाधु | यथा न पूर्वमपरो जहात्येवा धातरायूंषि कल्पयैषाम ||
10.18.e: As the days follow days in close succession, as with the seasons duly come the seasons,  As each successor fails not his foregoer, so form the lives of these, O great Ordainer.

10.18.d: आ रोहतायुर्जरसं वर्णाना अनुपूर्वं यतमाना यतिष्ठ | इह तवष्टा सुजनिमा सजोषा दीर्घमायुःकरति जीवसे वः ||
10.18.e: Live your full lives ap! find old age delightful, all of you striving one behind the other.  May Tvaṣṭar, maker of fair things, be gracious and lengthen out the days of your existence.

10.18.d: इमा नारीरविधवाः सुपत्नीराञ्जनेन सर्पिषा संविशन्तु | अनश्रवो.अनमीवाः सुरत्ना आ रोहन्तु जनयोयोनिमग्रे ||
10.18.e: Let these unwidowed dames with noble husbands adorn themselves with fragrant balm and unguent.  Decked with fair jewels, tearless, free from sorrow, first let the dames go up to where he lieth.

10.18.d: उदीर्ष्व नार्यभि जीवलोकं गतासुमेतमुप शेष एहि | हस्तग्राभस्य दिधिषोस्तवेदं पत्युर्जनित्वमभि सम्बभूथ ||
10.18.e: Rise, come unto the world of life, O woman: come, he is lifeless by whose side thou liest.  Wifehood with this thy husband was thy portion, who took thy hand and wooed thee as a lover.

10.18.d: धनुर्हस्तादाददानो मर्तस्यास्मे कषत्राय वर्चसेबलाय | अत्रैव तवमिह वयं सुवीरा विश्वा सप्र्धोभिमातीर्जयेम ||
10.18.e: From his dead hand I take the bow be carried, that it may be our power and might and glory.  There art thou, there; and here with noble heroes may we o’ercome all hosts that fight against us.

10.18.d: उप सर्प मातरं भूमिमेतामुरुव्यचसं पर्थिवींसुशेवाम | ऊर्णम्रदा युवतिर्दक्षिणावत एषा तवा पातुनिरतेरुपस्थात ||
10.18.e: Betake thee to the Iap of Earth the Mother, of Earth far-spreading, very kind and gracious.  Young Dame, wool-soft unto the guerdongiver, may she preserve thee from Destruction's bosom.

10.18.d: उच्छ्वञ्चस्व पर्थिवि मा नि बाधथाः सूपायनास्मै भवसूपवञ्चना | माता पुत्रं यथा सिचाभ्येनं भूमूर्णुहि ||
10.18.e: Heave thyself, Earth, nor press thee downward heavily: afford him easy access, gently tending him.  Cover him, as a mother wraps her skirt about her child, O Earth.

10.18.d: उच्छ्वञ्चमाना पर्थिवी सु तिष्ठतु सहस्रं मित उप हिश्रयन्ताम | ते गर्हासो घर्तश्चुतो भवन्तु विश्वाहास्मैशरणाः सन्त्वत्र ||
10.18.e: Now let the heaving earth be free from motion: yea,—let a thousand clods remain above him.  Be they to him a home distilling fatness, here let them ever be his place of refuge.

10.18.d: उत ते सतभ्नामि पर्थिवीं तवत परीमं लोगं निदधन मोहं रिषम | एतां सथूणां पितरो धारयन्तु ते.अत्रायमः सादना ते मिनोतु ||
10.18.e: I stay the earth from thee, while over thee I place this piece of earth. May I be free from injury.  Here let the Fathers keep this pillar firm for thee, and there let Yama make thee an abiding-place.

10.18.d: परतीचीने मामहनीष्वाः पर्णमिवा दधुः | परतीचीं जग्रभा वाचमश्वं रशनया यथा ||
10.18.e: Even as an arrow's feathers, they have set me on a fitting day.  The fit word have I caught and held as ’twere a courser with the rein.

10.19.d: नि वर्तध्वं मानु गातास्मान सिषक्त रेवतीः | अग्नीषोमापुनर्वसू अस्मे धारयतं रयिम ||
10.19.e: TURN, go not farther on your way: visit us, O ye Wealthy Ones.  Agni and Soma, ye who bring riches again, secure us wealth.

10.19.d: पुनरेना नि वर्तय पुनरेना नया कुरु | इन्द्र एणा नियछत्वग्निरेना उपाजतु ||
10.19.e: Make these return to us again, bring them beside us once again.  May. Indra give them back to us, and Agni drive them hither-ward.

10.19.d: पुनरेता नि वर्तन्तामस्मिन पुष्यन्तु गोपतौ | इहैवाग्नेनि धारयेह तिष्ठतु या रयिः ||
10.19.e: Let them return to us again: under this herdsman let them feed.  Do thou, O Agni, keep them here, and let the wealth we have remain.

10.19.d: यन नियानं नययनं संज्ञानं यत परायणम | आवर्तनं निवर्तनं यो गोपा अपि तं हुवे ||
10.19.e: 1 call upon their herdsman, him who knoweth well their coming nigh,  Their parting and their home-return, and watcheth their approach and rest.

10.19.d: य उदानड वययनं य उदानट परायणम | आवर्तनंनिवर्तनमपि गोपा नि वर्तताम ||
10.19.e: Yea, let the herdsman, too, return, who marketh well their driving-forth;  Marketh their wandering away, their turning back and coming home.

10.19.d: आ निवर्त नि वर्तय पुनर्न इन्द्र गा देहि | जीवाभिर्भुनजामहै ||
10.19.e: Home-leader, lead them home to us; Indra, restore to us our kine:  We will rejoice in them alive.

10.19.d: परि वो विश्वतो दध ऊर्जा घर्तेन पयसा | ये देवाः केच यज्ञियास्ते रय्या सं सर्जन्तु नः ||
10.19.e: 1 offer you on every side butter and milk and strengthening food.  May all the Holy Deities pour down on us a flood of wealth.

10.19.d: आ निवर्तन वर्तय नि निवर्तन वर्तय | भूम्याश्चतस्रःप्रदिशस्ताभ्य एना नि वर्तय ||
10.19.e: O thou Home-leader, lead them home, restore them thou who bringest home.  Four are the quarters of the earth; from these bring back to us our kine,

10.20.e: SEND unto us a good and happy mind.

10.20.d: अग्निमीळे भुजां यविष्ठं शासा मित्रं दुर्धरीतुम | यस्य धर्मन सवरेनीः सपर्यन्ति मातुरूधः ||
10.20.e: 1 worship Agni, Youthfullest of Gods, resistless, Friend of laws;  Under whose guard and heavenly light the Spotted seek the Mother's breast:
Whom with their mouth they magnify, bannered with flame and homed in light.  He glitters with his row of teeth.

10.20.d: अर्यो विशां गातुरेति पर यदानड दिवो अन्तान | कविरभ्रं दिद्यानः ||
10.20.e: Kind, Furtherer of men, he comes, when he hath reached the ends of heaven,  Sage, giving splendour to the clouds.

10.20.d: जुषद धव्या मानुषस्योर्ध्वस्तस्थाव रभ्वा यज्ञे | मिन्वन सद्म पुर एति ||
10.20.e: To taste man's offerings, he, the Strong, hath risen erect at sacrifice:  Fixing his dwelling he proceeds.

10.20.d: स हि कषेमो हविर्यज्ञः शरुष्टीदस्य गातुरेति | अग्निं देवा वाशीमन्तम ||
10.20.e: Here are oblation, worship, rest: rapidly comes his furtherance.  To sword-armed Agni come the Gods.

10.20.d: यज्ञासाहं दुव इषे.अग्निं पूर्वस्य शेवस्य | अद्रेःसूनुमायुमाहुः ||
10.20.e: With service for chief bliss I seek the Lord of Sacrifice, Agni, whom  They call the Living, Son of Cloud.

10.20.d: नरो ये के चास्मदा विश्वेत ते वाम आ सयुः | अग्निंहविषा वर्धन्तः ||
10.20.e: Blest evermore be all the men who come from us, who magnify  Agni with sacrificial gifts.

10.20.d: कर्ष्णः शवेतो.अरुषो यामो अस्य बरध्न रज्र उत शोणोयशस्वान | हिरण्यरूपं जनिता जजान ||
10.20.e: The path he treads is black and white and red, and striped, and brown, crimson, and glorious.  His sire begat him bright with hues of gold.

10.20.d: एवा ते अग्ने विमदो मनीषामूर्जो नपादम्र्तेभिःसजोषाः | गिर आ वक्षत सुमतीरियान इषमूर्जंसुक्षितिं विश्वमाभाः ||
10.20.e: Thus with his thoughts, O Son of Strength, O Agni, hath Vimada, accordant with the Immortals,  Offered thee hymns, soliciting thy favour. Thou hast brought all food, strength, a prosperous dwelling.

10.21.d: आग्निं न सवव्र्क्तिभिर्होतारं तवा वर्णीमहे | यज्ञायस्तीर्णबर्हिषे वि वो मदे शीरं पावकशोचिषंविवक्षसे ||
10.21.e: WITH offerings of our own we choose thee, Agni, as Invoking Priest,  For sacrifice with trimmed grass,—at your glad carouse-piercing and brightly shining. Thou art waxing great.

10.21.d: तवामु ते सवाभुवः शुम्भन्त्यश्वराधसः | वेति तवामुपसेचनी वि वो मद रजीतिरग्न आहुतिर्विवक्षसे ||
10.21.e: The wealthy ones adorn thee, they who bring us horses as their gift:  The sprinkling ladle, Agni,—at your glad carouse -and glowing offering taste thee. Thou art waxing great.

10.21.d: तवे धर्माण आसते जुहूभिः सिञ्चतीरिव | कर्ष्णारूपाण्यर्जुना वि वो मदे विश्वा अधि शरियो धिषेविवक्षसे ||
10.21.e: The holy statutes rest by thee, as ’twere with ladles that o’erflow.  Black and white-gleaming colours,—at your glad carouse-all glories thou assurnest. Thou art waxing great.

10.21.d: यमग्ने मन्यसे रयिं सहसावन्नमर्त्य | तमा नोवाजसातये वि वो मदे यज्ञेषु चित्रमा भरा विवक्षसे ||
10.21.e: O Agni, what thou deemest wealth, Victorious and Immortal One!  Bring thou to give us vigour,—at your glad carouse -splendid at sacrifices. Thou art waxing great.

10.21.d: अग्निर्जातो अथर्वणा विदद विश्वानि काव्या | भुवद दूतोविवस्वतो वि वो मदे परियो यमस्य काम्यो विवक्षसे ||
10.21.e: Skilled in all lore is Agni, he whom erst Atharvan brought to life.  He was Vivasvān's envoy, at your glad carouse-the weIl-loved friend of Yama, Thou art waxing great.

10.21.d: तवां यज्ञेष्वीळते.अग्ने परयत्यध्वरे | तवं वसूनिकाम्या वि वो मदे विश्वा दधासि दाशुषे विवक्षसे ||
10.21.e: At sacrifices they adore thee, Agni, when the rite proceeds.  All fair and lovely treasures-at your glad carouse-thou givest him who offers. Thou art waxing great.

10.21.d: तवां यज्ञेष्व रत्विजं चारुमग्ने नि षेदिरे | घर्तप्रतीकं मनुषो वि वो मदे शुक्रं चेतिष्ठमक्षभिर्विवक्षसे ||
10.21.e: Men, Agni, have established thee as welcome Priest at holy rites,  Thee whose face shines with butter,—at your glad carouse-bright, with eyes most observant. Thou art waxing great.

10.21.d: अग्ने शुक्रेण शोचिषोरु परथयसे बर्हत | अभिक्रन्दन्व्र्षायसे वि वो मदे गर्भं दधासि जामिषु विवक्षसे ||
10.21.e: Wide and aloft thou spreadest thee, O Agni, with thy brilliant flame.  A Bull art thou when bellowing,—at your glad carouse-thou dost impregn the Sisters. Thou art waxing great.

10.22.d: कुह शरुत इन्द्रः कस्मिन्नद्य जने मित्रो न शरुयते | रषीणां वा यः कषये गुहा व चर्क्र्षे गिर ||
10.22.e: WHERE is famed Indra heard of? With what folk is he renowned to-day as Mitra is,—  Who in the home of Ṛṣis and in secret is extolled with song?

10.22.d: इह शरुत इन्द्रो अस्मे अद्य सतवे वज्र्य रचीषमः | मित्रो नयो जनेष्वा यशश्चक्रे असाम्या ||
10.22.e: Even here is Indra famed, and among us this day the glorious Thunderer is praised,  He who like Mitra mid the folk hath won complete and full renown.

10.22.d: महो यस पतिः शवसो असाम्या महो नर्म्णस्य तूतुजिः | भर्ता वज्रस्य धर्ष्णोः पिता पुत्रमिव परियम ||
10.22.e: He who is Sovran Lord of great and perfect strength, exerter of heroic might,  Who bears the fearless thunder as a father bears his darling son.

10.22.d: युजानो अश्व वातस्य धुनी देवो देवस्य वज्रिवः | सयन्तपथा विरुक्मता सर्जान सतोष्यध्वनः ||
10.22.e: Harnessing to thy car, as God, two blustering Steeds Of the Wind-God, O Thunderer,  That speed along the shining path, thou making ways art glorified.

10.22.d: तवं तया चिद वातस्याश्वागा रज्रा तमना वहध्यै | ययोर्देवो न मर्त्यो यन्ता नकिर्विदाय्यः ||
10.22.e: Even to these dark Steeds of Wind thou of thyself hast come to ride,  Of which no driver may be found, none, be he God or mortal man.

10.22.d: अध गमन्तोशना पर्छते वां कदर्था न आ गर्हम | आजग्मथुः पराकाद दिवश्च गमश्च मर्त्यम ||
10.22.e: When ye approach, men ask you, thee and Uśanā: Why come ye to our dwelling-place?  Why are ye come to mortal man from distant realms of eapth and heaven?

10.22.d: आ न इन्द्र पर्क्षसे.अस्माकं बरह्मोद्यतम | तत तवायाचामहे.अवः शुष्णं यद धन्नमानुषम ||
10.22.e: O Indra, thou shalt speak us fair: our holy prayer is offered up.  We pray to thee for help as thou didst strike the monster Śuṣṇa dead.

10.22.d: अकर्मा दस्युरभि नो अमन्तुरन्यव्रतो अमानुषः | तवन्तस्यामित्रहन वधर्दासस्य दम्भय ||
10.22.e: Around us is the Dasyu, riteless, void of sense, inhuman, keeping alien laws.  Baffle, thou Slayer of the foe, the weapon which this Dāsa wields.

10.22.d: तवं न इन्द्र शूर शूरैरुत तवोतासो बर्हणा | पुरुत्राते वि पूर्तयो नवन्त कषोणयो यथा ||
10.22.e: Hero with Heroes, thou art ours: yea, strong are they whom thou dost help.  In many a place are thy full gifts, and men, like vassals, sing thy praise.

10.22.d: तवं तान वर्त्रहत्ये चोदयो नॄन कार्पाणे शूर वज्रिवः | गुहा यदी कवीनां विशां नक्षत्रशवसाम ||
10.22.e: Urge thou these heroes on to slay the enemy, brave Thunderer! in the fight with swords.  Even when hid among the tribes of Sages numerous as stars.

10.22.d: मक्षू ता त इन्द्र दानाप्नस आक्षाणे शूर वज्रिवः | यद ध शुष्णस्य दम्भयो जातं विश्वं सयावभिः ||
10.22.e: Swift come those gifts of thine whose hand is prompt to rend and burn, O Hero Thunder-armed:  As thou with thy Companions didst destroy the whole of SuSnia's brood.

10.22.d: माकुध्र्यगिन्द्र शूर वस्वीरस्मे भूवन्नभिष्टयः | वयं-वयं त आसां सुम्ने सयाम वज्रिवः ||
10.22.e: Let not thine excellent assistance come to us, O Hero Indra, profitless.  May we, may we enjoy the bliss of these thy favours, Thunderer!

10.22.d: अस्मे ता त इन्द्र सन्तु सत्याहिंसन्तीरुपस्प्र्शः | विद्यामयासां भुजो धेनूनां न वज्रिवः ||
10.22.e: May those soft impulses of thine, O Indra, be fruitful and innocent to us.  May we know these whose treasures are like those of milch-kine, Thunderer!

10.22.d: अहस्ता यदपदी वर्धत कषाः शचीभिर्वेद्यानाम | शुष्णं परि परदक्षिणिद विश्वायवे नि शिश्नथः ||
10.22.e: That Earth, through power of knowing things that may be known, handless and footless yet might thrive,  Thou slewest, turning to the right, gu;na for every living man.

10.22.d: पिबा-पिबेदिन्द्र शूर सोमं मा रिषण्यो वसवान वसुःसन | उत तरायस्व गर्णतो मघोनो महश्च रायो रेवतस्क्र्धी नः ||
10.22.e: Drink, drink the Soma, Hero Indra; be not withheld as thou art good, O Treasure-giver.  Preserve the singers and our liberal princes, and make us wealthy with abundant riches.

10.23.d: यजामह इन्द्रं वज्रदक्षिणं हरीणां रथ्यंविव्रतानाम | पर शमश्रु दोधुवदूर्ध्वथा भूद विसेनाभिर्दयमानो वि राधसा ||
10.23.e: INDRA, whose right hand wields the bolt, we worship, driver of Bay Steeds seeking sundered courses.  Shaking his beard with might he hath arisen, casting his weapons forth and dealing bounties.

10.23.d: हरी नवस्य या वने विदे वस्विन्द्रो मघैर्मघवाव्र्त्रहा भुवत | रभुर्वाज रभुक्षाः पत्यते शवो.अवक्ष्णौमि दासस्य नाम चित ||
10.23.e: The treasure which his Bay Steeds found at sacrifice,—this wealth made opulent Indra slayer of the foe.  Ṛbhu, Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja-he is Lord of Might. The Dāsa's very name I utterly destroy.

10.23.d: यदा वज्रं हिरण्यमिदथा रथं हरी यमस्यवहतो वि सूरिभिः | आ तिष्ठति मघवा सनश्रुत इन्द्रोवाजस्य दीर्घश्रवसस पतिः ||
10.23.e: When, with the Princes, Maghavari, famed of old, comes nigh the thunderbolt of gold, and the Controller's car  Which his two Tawny Coursers draw, then Indra is the Sovran Lord of power whose glory spreads afar.

10.23.d: सो चिन नु वर्ष्टिर्यूथ्या सवा सचानिन्द्रः शमश्रूणिहरिताभि परुष्णुते | अव वेति सुक्षयं सुते मधूदिद्धूनोति वातो यथा वनम ||
10.23.e: With him too is this rain of his that comes like herds: Indra throws drops of moisture on his yellow beard.  When the sweet juice is shed he seeks the pleasant place, and stirs the worshipper as wind disturbs the wood.

10.23.d: यो वाचा विवाचो मर्ध्रवाचः पुरू सहस्राशिवा जघान | तत-तदिदस्य पौंस्यं गर्णीमसि पितेव यस्तविषींवाव्र्धे शवः ||
10.23.e: We laud and praise his several deeds of valour who, fatherlike, with power hath made us stronger;  Who with his voice slew many thousand wicked ones who spake in varied manners with contemptuous cries.

10.23.d: सतोमं त इन्द्र विमदा अजीजनन्नपूर्व्यं पुरुतमंसुदानवे | विद्मा हयस्य भोजनमिनस्य यदा पशुं नगोपाः करामहे ||
10.23.e: Indra, the Vimadas have formed for thee a laud, copious, unparalleled, for thee Most Bountiful.  We know the good we gain from him the Mighty One when we attract him as a herdsman calls the kine.

10.23.d: माकिर्न एना सख्या वि यौशुस्तव चेन्द्र विमदस्य चर्शेः | विद्मा हि ते परमतिं देव जामिवदस्मे ते सन्तुसख्या शिवानि ||
10.23.e: Ne’er may this bond of friendship be dissevered, the Ṛṣi Vimada's and thine, O Indra.  We know thou carest for us as a brother with us, O God, be thine auspicious friendship.

10.24.d: इन्द्र सोममिमं पिब मधुमन्तं चमू सुतम | अस्मे रयिंनि धारय वि वो मदे सहस्रिणं पुरूवसो विवक्षसे ||
10.24.e: O INDRA, drink this Soma, pressed out in the mortar, full of sweets.  Send down to us great riches,—at your glad carouse-in thousands, O Most healthy. Thou art waxing great.

10.24.d: तवां यज्ञेभिरुक्थैरुप हव्येभिरीमहे | शचीपतेशचीनां वि वो मदे शरेष्ठं नो धेहि वार्यं विवक्षसे ||
10.24.e: To thee with sacrifices, with oblations, and with lauds we come.  Lord of all strength and power, grant-at your glad carouse-the best choiceworthy treasure. Thou art waxing great.

10.24.d: यस पतिर्वार्याणामसि रध्रस्य चोदिता | इन्द्रस्तोतॄणामविता वि वो मदे दविषो नः पाह्यंहसोविवक्षसे ||
10.24.e: Thou who art Lord of precious boons, inciter even of the churl.  Guardian of singers, Indra,—at your glad carouse-save us from woe and hatred. Thou art waxing great.

10.24.d: युवं शक्रा मायाविना समीची नीरमन्थतम | विमदेनयदिळित नसत्य निरमन्थतम ||
10.24.e: Strong, Lords of Magic power, ye Twain churned the united worlds apart,  When ye, implored by Vimada, Nāsatyas, forced apart the pair.

10.24.d: विश्वे देवा अक्र्पन्त समिच्योर्निष्पतन्त्योः | नसत्यवब्रुवन्देवः पुनरा वहतदिति ||
10.24.e: When the united pair were rent asunder all the Gods complained.  The Gods to the Nāsatyas cried, Bring these together once again.

10.24.d: मधुमन मे परायणं मधुमत पुनरयनम | त नो देवदेवतय युवं मधुमतस कर्तम ||
10.24.e: Sweet be my going forth, and rich in sweets be my approach to home.  So, through your Deity, both Gods, enrich us with all pleasantness.

10.25.d: भद्रं नो अपि वातय मनो दक्षमुत करतुम | अधा तेसख्ये अन्धसो वि वो मदे रणन गवो न यवसे विवक्षसे ||
10.25.e: SEND us a good and happy mind, send energy and mental power.  Then-at your glad carouse-let men joy in thy love, Sweet juice! as kine in pasture. Thou. art waxing great.

10.25.d: हर्दिस्प्र्शस्त असते विश्वेषु सोम ध मसु | अधा कामा इमेमम वि वो मदे वि तिष्ठन्ते वसूयवो विवक्षसे ||
10.25.e: rn all thy forms, O Soma, rest thy powers that influence the heart.  So also these my longings-at your glad carouse-spread themselves seeking riches. Thou art waxing great.

10.25.d: उत वरतनि सोम ते परहं मिनामि पाक्या | अधा पितेवसूनवे वि वो मदे मर्ळ नो अभि चिद वधाद विवक्षसे ||
10.25.e: Even if, O Soma, I neglect thy laws through my simplicity,  Be gracious-at your glad carouse-as sire to son. Preserve us even from slaughter. T'hou. art waxing great.

10.25.d: समु पर यन्ति धीतयः सर्गासो.अवतानिव | करतुं नःसोम जिवसे वि वो मदे धरया चमसानिव विवक्षसे ||
10.25.e: Our songs in concert go to thee as streams of water to the wells.  Soma, that we may live, grant-at your glad carouse-full powers of mind, like beakers. Thou art waxing great.

10.25.d: तव तये सोम शक्तिभिर्निकामासो वय रण्विरे | गर्त्सस्यधिरस्तवसो वि वो मदे वरजं गोमन्तमश्विनं विवक्षसे ||
10.25.e: O Soma, through thy might who art skilful and strong, these longing men,  These sages, have thrown open-at your glad carouse-the stall of kine and horses. Thou art waxing great

10.25.d: पशुं नः सोम रक्षसि पुरुत्र विष्ठितं जगत | समाक्र्णोषि जीवसे वि वो मदे विश्वा सम्पश्यन भुवनविवक्षसे ||
10.25.e: Our herds thou guardest, Soma, and the moving world spread far and wide.  Thou fittest them for living,—at your glad carouse-looking upon all beings. Thou art waxing great.

10.25.d: तवं नः सोम विश्वतो गोप अदभ्यो भव | सेध राजन्नपस्रिधो वि वो मदे म नो दुः शंस ईशता विवक्षसे ||
10.25.e: On all sides, Soma, be to us a Guardian ne’er to be deceived.  King, drive away our foemen-at your glad carouse:—let not the wicked rule us. Thou art waxing great.

10.25.d: तवं नः सोम सुक्रतुर्व योधेयाय जाग्र्हि | कषेत्रवित्तरोमनुषो वि वो मदे दरुहो नः पाह्यंहसो विवक्षसे ||
10.25.e: Be watchful, Soma, passing wise, to give us store of vital strength.  More skilled than man to guide us,—at your glad carouse-save us from harm and sorrow. Thou art waxing great.

10.25.d: तवं नो वर्त्र हन्तमेन्द्रस्येन्दो शिवः सखा | यत सिंहवन्ते समिथे वि वो मदे युध्यमनस्तोकसातौविवक्षसे ||
10.25.e: Chief slayer of our foemen, thou, Indu, art Indra's gracious Friend,  When warriors invoke him-at your glad carouse -in fight, to win them offspring. Thou art waxing great.

10.25.d: अयं घ स तुरो मद इन्द्रस्य वर्धत परियः | अयंकक्षीवतो महो वि वो मदे मतिं विप्रस्य वर्धयद्विवक्षसे ||
10.25.e: Victorious is this gladdening drink: to Indra dear it grows in strength.  This-at your glad carouse -enhanced the mighty hymn of the great sage Kakṣīvān. Thou art waxing great.

10.25.d: अयं विप्रय दशुषे वजनियर्ति गोमतः | अयंसप्तभ्य आ वरं वि वो मदे परन्धं शरोणं चतरिषद विवक्षसे ||
10.25.e: This to the sage who offers gifts brings power that comes from wealth in kine.  This, better than the seven, hath-at your glad carouse-furthered the blind, the cripple. Thou art waxing great.

10.26.d: पर हयछा मनीषा सपार्ह यन्ति नियुतः | पर दस्रानियुद्रथः पूषा अविष्टु माहिनः ||
10.26.e: FORWARD upon their way proceed the ready teams, the lovely songs.  Further them glorious Pūṣan with yoked chariot, and the Mighty Twain!

10.26.d: यस्य तयन महित्वं वताप्यमयं जनः | विप्र आ वंसद्धीतिभिश्चिकेत सुष्टुतीनाम ||
10.26.e: With sacred hymns let this man here, this singer, win the God to whom  Belong this majesty and might. He hath observed our eulogies.

10.26.d: स वेद सुष्टुतीनामिन्दुर्न पूष वर्षा | अभि पसुरःप्रुषायति वरजं न आ परुषायति ||
10.26.e: Pūṣan the Strong hath knowledge of sweet praises even as Indu hath.  He dews our corn with moisture, he bedews the pasture of our kine.

10.26.d: मंसीमहि तवा वयमस्माकं देव पूषन | मत्मां चसाधनं विप्राणां चाधवम ||
10.26.e: We will bethink ourselves of thee, O Pūṣan, O thou God, as One.  Who brings fulfilment of our hymns, and stirs the singer and the sage.

10.26.d: परत्यर्धिर्यज्ञनामश्वहयो रथानाम | रषिः स योमनुर्हितो विप्रस्य यावयत्सखः ||
10.26.e: joint-sharer of each sacrifice, the driver of the chariot steeds;  The Ṛṣi who is good to man, the singer's Friend and faithful Guard.

10.26.d: अधीषमाणायाः पतिः शुचायाश्च शुचस्य च | वासोवयो.अवीनामा वासांसि मर्म्र्जत ||
10.26.e: One who is Lord of Suca, Lord of Suca caring for herself:  Weaving the raiment of the sheep and making raiment beautiful.

10.26.d: इनो वाजानां पतिरिनः पुष्टीनं सख | पर शमश्रुहर्यतो दूधोद वि वर्थ यो अदाभ्यः ||
10.26.e: The mighty Lord of spoil and wealth, Strong Friend of all prosperity;  He with light movement shakes his beard, lovely and ne’er to be deceived.

10.26.d: आ ते रथस्य पूषन्नजा धुरं वव्र्त्युः | विश्वस्यार्थिनः सखा सनोजा अनपच्युतः ||
10.26.e: O Pūṣan, may those goats of thine turn hitherward thy chariot-pole.  Friend of all suppliants; art thou, born in old time, and arm and sure.

10.26.d: अस्मकमुर्जा रथं पूषा अविष्टु माहिनः | भुवद्वजनां वर्ध इमं नः शर्णवद धवम ||
10.26.e: May the majestic Pūṣan speed our chariot with his power and might.  May he increase our store of wealth and listen to this call of ours.

10.27.d: असत सु मे जरितः साभिवेगो यत सुन्वते यजमनय शिक्षम | अनाशीर्दामहमस्मि परहन्ता सत्यध्व्र्तं वर्जिनायन्तमाभुम ||
10.27.e: THIS, singer, is my firm determination, to aid the worshipper who pours the Soma.  I slay the man who brings no milkoblation, unrighteous, powerful, the truth's perverter.

10.27.d: यदीदहं युधये संनयान्यदेवयून तन्वाशूशुजानान | अमा ते तुम्रं वर्षभं पचानि तीव्रंसुतं पञ्चदशं नि षिञ्चम ||
10.27.e: Then Will I, when I lead my friends to battle against the radiant persons of the godless,  Prepare for thee at home a vigorous bullock, and pour for thee the fifteen-fold strong juices.

10.27.d: नाहं तं वेद य इति बरवीत्यदेवयून समरणेजघन्वान | यदावाख्यत समरणं रघावदादिद ध मेव्र्षभा पर बरुवन्ति ||
10.27.e: I know not him who sayeth and declareth that he hath slain the godless in the battle.  Soon as they see the furious combat raging, men speak forth praises of my vigorous horses.

10.27.d: यदज्ञातेषु वर्जनेष्वासं विश्वे सतो मघवानो मासन | जिनामि वेत कषेम आ सन्तमाभुं पर तंक्षिणां पर्वते पादग्र्ह्य ||
10.27.e: While yet my deeds of might were unrecorded, all passed for Maghavans though I existed.  The potent one who dwelt in peace I conquered, grasped by the foot and slew him on the mountain.

10.27.d: न वा उ मां वर्जने वारयन्ते न पर्वतासो यदहम्मनस्ये | मम सवनात कर्धुकर्णो भयात एवेदनु दयून्किरणः समेजात ||
10.27.e: None hinder me in mine heroic exploits, no, not the mountains when I will and purpose.  Even the deaf will tremble at my roaring, and every day will dust be agitated.

10.27.d: दर्शन नवत्र शर्तपाननिन्द्रान बाहुक्षदः शरवेपत्यमानान | घर्षुं वा ये निनिदुः सखायमध्यू नवेषु पवयो वव्र्त्युः ||
10.27.e: To see the Indraless oblation-drinkers, mean offerers, o’ertaken by destruction!  Then shall the fellies of my car pass over those who have blamed my joyous Friend and scorned him.

10.27.d: अभूर्वौक्षीर्व्यु आयुरानड दर्षन नु पूर्वो अपरोनु दर्षत | दवे पवस्ते परि तं न भूतो यो अस्य पारेरजसो विवेष ||
10.27.e: Thou wast, thou grewest to full vital vigour: an earlier saw, a later one shall see thee.  Two canopies, as ’twere, are round about him who reacheth to the limit of this region.

10.27.d: गावो यवं परयुता अर्यो अक्षन ता अपश्यं सहगोपाश्चरन्तीः | हवा इदर्यो अभितः समायन कियदासुस्वपतिश्छन्दयाते ||
10.27.e: The freed kine eat the barley of the pious. 1 saw them as they wandered with the herdsman.  The calling of the pious rang around them. What portion will these kine afford their owner?

10.27.d: सं यद वयं यवसादो जनानामहं यवाद उर्वज्रेन्तः | अत्रा युक्तो.अवसातारमिछादथो अयुक्तं युनजद्ववन्वान ||
10.27.e: When we who cat the grass of men are gathered I am with barley-eaters in the corn-land.  There shall the captor yoke the yokeless bullock, and he who hath been yoked seek one to loose him.

10.27.d: अत्रेदु मे मंससे सत्यमुक्तं दविपाच्च यच्चतुष्पात्संस्र्जानि | सत्रीभिर्यो अत्र वर्षणं पर्तन्यादयुद्धोस्य वि भजानि वेदः ||
10.27.e: There wilt thou hold as true my spoken purpose, to bring together quadrupeds. and bipeds.  I will divide, without a fight, his riches who warreth here, against the Bull, with women.

10.27.d: यस्यानक्षा दुहिता जात्वास कस्तां विद्वानभिमन्याते अन्धाम | कतरो मेनिं परति तं मुचाते य ईंवहाते य ईं वा वरेयात ||
10.27.e: When a man's daughter hath been ever eyeless, who, knowing, will be wroth with her for blindness?  Which of the two will loose on him his anger-the man who leads her home or he who woos her?

10.27.d: कियती योषा मर्यतो वधूयोः परिप्रीता पन्यसावार्येण | भद्रा वधूर्भवति यत सुपेशाः सवयं सामित्रं वनुते जने चित ||
10.27.e: How many a maid is pleasing to the suitor who fain would marry for her splendid riches?  If the girl be both good and fair of feature, she finds, herself, a friend among the people.

10.27.d: पत्तो जगार परत्यञ्चमत्ति शीर्ष्णा शिरः परति दधौवरूथम | आसीन ऊर्ध्वामुपसि कषिणाति नयंं उत्तानामन्वेति भूमिम ||
10.27.e: His feet have grasped: he eats the man who meets him. Around his head he sets the head for shelter.  Sitting anear and right above he smites us, and follows earth that lies spread out beneath him.

10.27.d: बर्हन्नछायो अपलाशो अर्वा तस्थौ माता विषितो अत्तिगर्भः | अन्यस्या वत्सं रिहती मिमाय कया भुवा निदधे धेनुरूधः ||
10.27.e: High, leafless, shadowless, and swift is Heaven: the Mother stands, the Youngling, loosed, is feeding.  Loud hath she lowed, licking Another's offspring. In what world hath the Cow laid down her udder?

10.27.d: सप्त वीरासो अधरादुदायन्नष्टोत्तरात्तात समजग्मिरन ते | नव पश्चातात सथिविमन्त आयन दश पराक्सानु वि तिरन्त्यश्नः ||
10.27.e: Seven heroes from the nether part ascended, and from the upper part came eight together.  Nine from behind came armed with winnowing-baskets: ten from the front pressed o’er the rock's high ridges.

10.27.d: दशानामेकं कपिलं समानं तं हिन्वन्ति करतवेपार्याय | गर्भं माता सुधितं वक्षणास्ववेनन्तन्तुषयन्ती बिभर्ति ||
10.27.e: One of the ten, the tawny, shared in common, they send to execute their final purpose.  The Mother carries on her breast the Infant of noble form and soothes it while it knows not.

10.27.d: पीवानं मेषमपचन्त वीरा नयुप्ता अक्षा अनु दीवासन | दवा धनुं बर्हतीमप्स्वन्तः पवित्रवन्ता चरतःपुनन्ता ||
10.27.e: The Heroes dressed with fire the fatted wether: the dice were thrown by way of sport and gaming.  Two reach the plain amid the heavenly waters, hallowing and with means of purifying.

10.27.d: वि करोशनासो विष्वञ्च आयन पचाति नेमो नहि पक्षदर्धः | अयं मे देवः सविता तदाह दर्वन्न इद वनवत्सर्पिरन्नः ||
10.27.e: Crying aloud they ran in all directions: One half of them will cook, and not the other.  To me hath Savitar, this God, declared it: He will perform, whose food is wood and butter.

10.27.d: अपश्यं गरामं वहमानमारादचक्रया सवधयावर्तमानम | सिषक्त्यर्यः पर युगा जनानां सद्यःशिश्ना परमिनानो नवीयान ||
10.27.e: I saw a troop advancing from the distance moved, not by wheels but their own God-like nature.  The Friendly One seeks human generations, destroying, still new bands of evil beings.

10.27.d: एतौ मे गावौ परमरस्य युक्तौ मो षु पर सेधीर्मुहुरिन्ममन्धि | आपश्चिदस्य वि नशन्त्यर्थं सूरश्च मर्कौपरो बभूवान ||
10.27.e: These my two Bulls, even Pramara's, are harnessed: drive them not far; here let them often linger.  The waters even shall aid him to his object, and the all-cleansing Sun who is above us.

10.27.d: अयं यो वज्रः पुरुधा विव्र्त्तो.अवः सूर्यस्य बर्हतःपुरीषात | शरव इदेना परो अन्यदस्ति तदव्यथीजरिमाणस्तरन्ति ||
10.27.e: This is the thunderbolt which often whirleth down from the lofty misty realm of Sūrya.  Beyond this realm there is another glory so through old age they pass and feel no sorrow.

10.27.d: वर्क्षे-वर्क्षे नियता मीमयद गौस्ततो वयः पर पतान्पुरुषादः | अथेदं विश्वं भुवनं भयात इद्रायसुन्वद रषये च शिक्षत ||
10.27.e: Bound fast to,every tree the cow is lowing, and thence the man-consuming birds are flying,  Then all this world, though pressing juice for Indra and strengthening the Ṛṣi, is affrighted.

10.27.d: देवानां माने परथमा अतिष्ठन कर्न्तत्रदेषमुपर उदायन | तरयस्तपन्ति पर्थिविमनूप दव बर्बूकं वहतःपुरीषम ||
10.27.e: In the Gods’ mansion stood the first-created, and from their separation came the later.  Three warm the Earth while holding stores of water, and Two of these convey the murmuring moisture.

10.27.d: सा ते जीवातुरुत तस्य विद्धि म समैताद्र्गप गूहःसमर्ये | अविः सवः कर्णुते गूहते बुसं स पादुरस्यनिर्णिजो न मुच्यते ||
10.27.e: This is thy life: and do thou mark and know it. As such, hide not thyself in time of battle.  He manifests the light and hides the vapour: his foot is never free from robes that veil it.

10.28.d: विश्वो हयन्यो अरिराजगाम ममेदह शवशुरो न जगाम | जक्षीयाद धना उत सोमं पपीयात सवाशितः पुनरस्तं जगायात ||
10.28.e: Now all my other friends are here assembled: my Sire-in-law alone hath not come hither.  So might he eat the grain and drink the Soma, and, satisfied, return unto; his dwelling.

10.28.d: स रोरुवद वर्षभस्तिग्मश्र्न्गो वर्ष्मन तस्थाु वरिमन्नाप्र्थिव्याः | विश्वेष्वेनं वर्जनेषु पामि यो मे कुक्षिसुतसोमः पर्णाति ||
10.28.e: Loud belloweth the Bull whose horns are sharpened: upon the height above earth's breadth he standeth.  That man I guard and save in all his troubles who fills my flanks when he hath shed the Soma.

10.28.d: अद्रिणा ते मन्दिन इन्द्र तूयान सुन्वन्ति सोमान पिबसि तवमेशाम | पचन्ति ते वर्षभानत्सि तेषां पर्क्षेण यन्मघवन हूयमानः ||
10.28.e: Men with the stone press out for thee, O Indra, strong, gladdening Soma, and thereof thou drinkest.  Bulls they dress for thee, and of these thou eatest when, Maghavan, with food thou art invited.

10.28.d: इदं सु मे जरितरा चिकिद्धि परतीपं शापं नद्योवहन्ति | लोपाशः सिंहं परत्यञ्चमत्साः करोष्टावराहं निरतक्त कक्षात ||
10.28.e: Resolve for me, O singer, this my riddle: The rivers send their swelling water backward:  The fox steals up to the approaching lion: the jackal drives the wild-boar from the brushwood.

10.28.d: कथ त एतदहमा चिकेतं गर्त्सस्य पाकस्तवसोमनीषाम | तवं नो विद्वान रतुथा वि वोचो यमर्धं तेमघवन कषेम्या धूः ||
10.28.e: How shall I solve this riddle, I, the simple, declare the thought of thee the Wise and Mighty?  Tell us, well knowing, as befits the season: Whitherward is thy prosperous car advancing?

10.28.d: एवा हि मां तवसं वर्धयन्ति दिवश्चिन मे बर्हतौत्तरा धुः | पुरू सहस्रा नि शिशामि साकमशत्रुंहि म जनिता जजान ||
10.28.e: Thus do they magnify me, me the mighty higher than even high heaven is my car-pole.  I all at once demolish many thousands: my Sire begot me with no foe to match me.

10.28.d: एवा हि मां तवसं जज्ञुरुग्रं कर्मन-कर्मन वर्षणमिन्द्र देवाः | वधीं वर्त्रं वज्रेण मन्दसनो.अप वरजम्महिना दाशुषे वम ||
10.28.e: Yea, and the Gods have known me also, Indra, as mighty, fierce and strong in every exploit.  Exulting with the bolt I slaughtered Vṛtra, and for the offerer oped with might the cow-stall.

10.28.d: देवास आयन परशून्रबिभ्रन वना वर्श्चन्तो अभि विड्भिरायन | नि सुद्र्वं दधतो वक्षणासु यत्रा कर्पीटमनुतद दहन्ति ||
10.28.e: The Deities approached, they carried axes; splitting the wood they came with their attendants.  They laid good timber in the fire-receivers, and burnt the grass up where they found it growing.

10.28.d: शशः कषुरं परत्यञ्चं जगाराद्रिं लोगेन वयभेदमारात | बर्हन्तं चिद रहते रन्धयानि वयद वत्सो वर्षभंशूशुवानः ||
10.28.e: The hare hath swallowed up the opposing razor: I sundered with a clod the distant mountain.  The great will I make subject to the little: the calf shall wax in strength and cat the bullock.

10.28.d: सुपर्ण इत्था नखमा सिषायावरुद्धः परिपदं नसिंहः | निरुद्धश्चिन महिषस्तर्ष्यावान गोधा तस्मायथं कर्षदेतत ||
10.28.e: There hath the strong-winged eagle left his talon, as a snared lion leaves the trap that caught him.  Even the wild steer in his thirst is captured: the leather strap still holds his foot entangled.

10.28.d: तेभ्यो गोधा अयथं कर्षदेतद ये बरह्मणः परतिपियन्त्यन्नैः | सिम उक्ष्णो.अवस्र्ष्टानदन्ति सवयं बलानितन्वः शर्णानाः ||
10.28.e: So may the leather strap their foot entangle who fatten on the viands of the Brahman.  They all devour the bulls set free to wander, while they themselves destroy their bodies' vigour.

10.28.d: एते शमीभिः सुशमी अभूवन ये हिन्विरे तन्वः सोमौक्थैः | नर्वद वदन्नुप नो माहि वाजान दिवि शरवोदधिषे नाम वीरः ||
10.28.e: They were well occupied with holy duties who sped in person with their lauds to Soma.  Speaking like man, mete to us wealth and booty: in heaven thou hast the name and fame of Hero.

10.29.d: वने न वा यो नयधायि चाकञ्छुचिर्वां सतोमो भुरणावजीगः | यस्येदिन्द्रः पुरुदिनेषु होता नर्णां नर्योन्र्तमः कषपावान ||
10.29.e: As sits the young bird on the tree rejoicing, ye, swift Pair, have been roused by clear laudation,  Whose Herald-Priest through many days is Indra, earth's Guardian, Friend of men, the best of Heroes.

10.29.d: पर ते अस्या उषसः परापरस्या नर्तौ सयाम नर्तमस्यन्र्णाम | अनु तरिशोकः शतमावहन नॄन कुत्सेन रथो योसत ससवान ||
10.29.e: May we, when this Dawn and the next dance hither, be thy best servants, most heroic Hero!  Let the victorious car with triple splendour bring hitherward the hundred chiefs with Kutsa.

10.29.d: कस्ते मद इन्द्र रन्त्यो भूद दुरो गिरो अभ्युग्रो वि धाव | कद वाहो अर्वागुप मा मनीषा आ तवा शक्यमुपमंराधो अन्नैः ||
10.29.e: What was the gladdening draught that pleased thee, Indra? Speed through our doors to songs, for thou art mighty.  Why comest thou to me, what gift attracts thee? Fain would I bring thee food most meet to offer.

10.29.d: कदु दयुम्नमिन्द्र तवावतो नॄन कया धिया करसे कन नागन | मित्रो न सत्य उरुगाय भर्त्या अन्ने समस्य यदसन्मनीषाः ||
10.29.e: Indra, what fame hath one like thee mid heroes? With what plan wilt thou act? Why hast thou sought us?  As a true Friend, Wide-Strider! to sustain us, since food absorbs the thought of each among us.

10.29.d: परेरय सूरो अर्थं न पारं ये अस्य कामं जनिधा इवग्मन | गिरश्च ये ते तुविजात पूर्वीर्नर इन्द्रप्रतिशिक्षन्त्यन्नैः ||
10.29.e: Speed happily those, as Sūrya ends his journey, who meet his wish as bridegrooms meet their spouses;  Men who present, O Indra strong by nature, with food the many songs that tell thy praises.

10.29.d: मात्रे नु ते सुमिते इन्द्र पूर्वी दयौर्मज्मना पर्थिवीकाव्येन | वराय ते घर्तवन्तः सुतासः सवाद्मन भवन्तुपीतये मधूनि ||
10.29.e: Thine are two measures, Indra, wide-wellmeted, heaven for thy majesty, earth for thy wisdom.  Here for thy choice are Somas mixed with butter: may the sweet meath be pleasant for thy drinking.

10.29.d: आ मध्वो अस्मा असिचन्नमत्रमिन्द्राय पूर्णं स हिसत्यराधाः | स वाव्र्धे वरिमन्ना पर्थिव्या अभि करत्वानर्यः पौंस्यैश्च ||
10.29.e: They have poured out a bowl to him, to Indra, full of sweet juice, for faithful is his bounty.  O'er earth's expanse hath he grown great by wisdom, the Friend of man, and by heroic exploits.

10.29.d: वयानळ इन्द्रः पर्तनाः सवोजा आस्मै यतन्ते सख्यायपूर्वीः | आ समा रथं न पर्तनासु तिष्ठ यं भद्रयासुमत्या चोदयासे ||
10.29.e: Indra hath conquered in his wars, the Mighty: men strive in multitudes to win his friendship.  Ascend thy chariot as it were in battle, which thou shalt drive to us with gracious favour.

10.30.d: पर देवत्रा बराह्मणे गातुरेत्वपो अछा मनसो नप्रयुक्ति | महीं मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धासिं पर्थुज्रयसेरीरधा सुव्र्क्तिम ||
10.30.e: As ’twere with swift exertion of the spirit, let the priest speed to the celestial Waters,  The glorious food of Varuṇa and Mitra. To him who spreadeth far this laud I offer.

10.30.d: अध्वर्यवो हविष्मन्तो हि भूताछाप इतोशतीरुशन्तः | अव याश्चष्टे अरुणः सुपर्णस्तमास्यध्वमूर्मिमद्या सुहस्ताः ||
10.30.e: Adhvaryus, he ye ready with oblations,, and come with longing to the longing Waters,  Down on which looks the. purple-tinted Eagle. Pour ye that flowing wave this day, deft-handed.

10.30.d: अध्वर्यवो.अप इता समुद्रमपां नपातं हविषा यजध्वम | स वो दददूर्मिमद्या सुपूतं तस्मै सोमं मधुमन्तंसुनोत ||
10.30.e: Go to the reservoir, O ye Adhvaryus worship the Waters’ Child with your oblations.  A consecrated wave he now will give you, so press for him the Soma rich in sweetness.

10.30.d: यो अनिध्मो दीदयदप्स्वन्तर्यं विप्रास ईळतेध्वरेषु | अपां नपान मधुमतीरपो दा याभिरिन्द्रोवाव्र्धे वीर्याय ||
10.30.e: He who shines bright in floods, unfed with fuel, whom sages worship at their sacrifices:  Give waters rich in sweets, Child of the Waters, even those which gave heroic might to Indra:

10.30.d: याभिः सोमो मोदते हर्षते च कल्याणीभिर्युवतिभिर्नमर्यः | ता अध्वर्यो अपो अछा परेहि यदासिञ्चाोषधीभिः पुनीतात ||
10.30.e: Those in which Soma joys and is delighted, as a young man with fair and pleasant damsels.  Go thou unto those Waters, O Adhvaryu, and purify with herbs what thou infusest.

10.30.d: एवेद यूने युवतयो नमन्त यदीमुशन्नुशतीरेत्यछ | सं जानते मनसा सं चिकित्रे.अध्वर्यवो धिषणापश्चदेवीः ||
10.30.e: So maidens bow before the youthful gallant who comes with love to them who yearn to meet him.  In heart accordant and in wish one-minded are the Adhvaryus and the heavenly Waters.

10.30.d: यो वो वर्ताभ्यो अक्र्णोदु लोकं यो वो मह्या अभिशस्तेरमुञ्चत | तस्मा इन्द्राय मधुमन्तमूर्मिं देवमादनम्प्र हिणोतनापः ||
10.30.e: He who made room for you when fast imprisoned, who freed you from the mighty imprecation,—  Even to that Indra send the meath-rich current, the wave that gratifies the Gods, O Waters.

10.30.d: परास्मै हिनोत मधुमन्तमूर्मिं गर्भो यो वः सिन्धवोमध्व उत्सः | घर्तप्र्ष्ठमीड्यमध्वरेष्वापो रेवतीःश्र्णुता हवं मे ||
10.30.e: Send forth to him the meath-rich wave, O Rivers, which is your offspring and a well of sweetness,  Oil-balmed, to be implored at sacrifices. Ye wealthy Waters, hear mine invocation.

10.30.d: तं सिन्धवो मत्सरमिन्द्रपानमूर्मिं पर हेत य उभेियर्ति | मदच्युतमौशानं नभोजां परि तरितन्तुंविचरन्तमुत्सम ||
10.30.e: Send forth the rapture-giving wave, O Rivers, which Indra drinks, which sets the Twain in motion;  The well that springeth from the clouds, desirous, that wandereth triple-formed, distilling transport.

10.30.d: आवर्व्र्ततीरध नु दविधारा गोषुयुधो न नियवंचरन्तीः | रषे जनित्रीर्भुवनस्य पत्नीरपो वन्दस्वसव्र्धः सयोनीः ||
10.30.e: These winding Streams which with their double current, like cattle-raiders, seek the lower pastures,—  Waters which dwell together, thrive together, Queens, Mothers of the world, these, Ṛṣi, honour.

10.30.d: हिनोता नो अध्वरं देवयज्या हिनोत बरह्म सनयेधनानाम | रतस्य योगे वि शयध्वमूधः शरुष्टीवरीर्भूतनास्मभ्यमापः ||
10.30.e: Send forth our sacrifice with holy worship send forth the hymn and prayer for gain of riches.  For need of sacrifice disclose the udder. Give gracious hearing to our call, O Waters.

10.30.d: आपो रेवतीः कषयथा हि वस्वः करतुं च भद्रम्बिभ्र्थाम्र्तं च | रायश्च सथ सवपत्यस्य पत्नीःसरस्वती तद गर्णते वयो धात ||
10.30.e: For, wealthy Waters, ye control all treasures: ye bring auspicious intellect and Amṛta.  Ye are the Queens of independent riches Sarasvatī give full life to the singer!

10.30.d: परति यदापो अद्र्श्रमायतीर्घ्र्तं पयांसि बिभ्रतीर्मधूनि | अध्वर्युभिर्मनसा संविदाना इन्द्राय सोमंसुषुतं भरन्तीः ||
10.30.e: When I behold the Waters coming hither, carrying with them milk and mcath and butter,  Bearing the well-pressed Soma juice to Indra, they harmonize in spirit with Adhvaryus.

10.30.d: एमा अग्मन रेवतीर्जीवधन्या अध्वर्यवः सादयतासखायः | नि बर्हिषि धत्तन सोम्यासो.अपां नप्त्रासंविदानास एनाः ||
10.30.e: Rich, they are come with wealth for living beings, O friends, Adhvaryus, seat them in their places.  Seat them on holy grass, ye Soma-bringers in harmony with the Offspring of the Waters.

10.30.d: आग्मन्नाप उशतीर्बर्हिरेदं नयध्वरे असदन्देवयन्तीः | अध्वर्यवः सुनुतेन्द्राय सोममभूदु वःसुशका देवयज्या ||
10.30.e: Now to this grass are come the longing Waters: the Pious Ones are seated at our worship.  Adbvaryus, press the Soma juice for Indra so will the service of the Gods be easy.

10.31.d: आ नो देवानामुप वेतु शंसो विश्वेभिस्तुरैरवसेयजत्रः | तेभिर्वयं सुषखायो भवेम तरन्तो विश्वादुरिता सयाम ||
10.31.e: MAY benediction of the Gods approach us, holy, to aid us with all rapid succours.  Therewith may we be happily befriended, and pass triumphant over all our troubles.

10.31.d: परि चिन मर्तो दरविणं ममन्याद रतस्य पथा नमसाविवासेत | अत सवेन करतुना सं वदेत शरेयांसन्दक्षं मनसा जग्र्भ्यात ||
10.31.e: A man should think on wealth and strive to win it by adoration on the path of Order,  Counsel himself with his own mental insight, and grasp still nobler vigour with his spirit.

10.31.d: अधायि धीतिरसस्र्ग्रमंशास्तीर्थे न दस्ममुपयन्त्युमाः | अभ्यानश्म सुवितस्य शूषं नवेदसोम्र्तानामभूम ||
10.31.e: The hymn is formed, poured are the allotted portions: as to a ford friends come unto the Wondrous.  We have obtained the power of case and comfort, we haVe become acquainted, with Immortals.

10.31.d: नित्यश्चाकन्यात सवपतिर्दामूना यस्मा उ देवः सवितजजान | भगो वा गोभिरर्यमेमनज्यात सो अस्मै चरुश्छदयदुत सयात ||
10.31.e: Pleased be the Eternal Lord who loves the household with this man whom God Savitar created.  May Bhaga Aryaman grace him with cattle: may he appear to him, and be, delightful.

10.31.d: इयं सा भूया उषसामिव कष यद ध कषुमन्तःशवसा समायन | अस्य सतुतिं जरितुर्भिक्षमाणा आनः शग्मास उप यन्तु वाजाः ||
10.31.e: Like the Dawns' dwelling-place be this assembly, where in their might men rich in food have gathered.  Striving to share the praises of this singer. To us come strengthening and effectual riches!

10.31.d: अस्येदेषा सुमतिः पप्रथानाभवत पूर्व्या भुमनागौः | अस्य सनीळा असुरस्य योनौ समान आ भरणेबिभ्रमाणाः ||
10.31.e: This Bull's most gracious far-extended favour existed first of all in full abundance.  By his support they are maintained in common who in the Asura's mansion dwell together.

10.31.d: किं सविद वनं क उ स वर्क्ष आस यतो दयावाप्र्थिवीनिष्टतक्षुः | सन्तस्थाने अजरे इतूती अहानि पूर्वीरुषसो जरन्त ||
10.31.e: What was the tree, what wood, in sooth, produced it, from which they fashioned forth the Earth and Heaven?  These Twain stand fast and wax not old for ever: these have sung praise to many a day and morning.

10.31.d: नैतावदेना परो अन्यदस्त्युक्षा स दयावाप्र्थिवीबिभर्ति | तवदं पवित्रं कर्णुत सवधावान यदींसूर्यं न हरितो वहन्ति ||
10.31.e: Not only here is this: more is beyond us. He is the Bull, the Heaven's and Earth's supporter.  With power divine he makes his skin a filter, when the Bay Coursers bear him on as Sūrya.

10.31.d: सतेगो न कषामत्येति पर्थ्वीं मिहं न वातो वि हवाति भूम | मित्रो यत्र वरुणो अज्यमानो.अग्निर्वने न वयस्र्ष्ट शोकम ||
10.31.e: He passes o’er the broad earth like a Stega: he penetrates the world as Wind the mist-cloud.  He, balmed with oil, near Varuṇa and Mitra, like Agni in the wood, hath shot forth splendour.

10.31.d: सतरीर्यत सूत सद्यो अज्यमाना वयथिरव्यथिः कर्णुतस्वगोपा | पुत्रो यत पुर्वः पित्रोर्जनिष्ट शम्यां गौर्जगार यद ध पर्छान ||
10.31.e: When suddenly called the cow that erst was barren, she, self-protected, ended all her troubles.  Earth, when the first son sprang from sire and mother, cast up the gami, that which men were seeking.

10.31.d: उत कण्वं नर्षदः पुत्रमाहुरुत शयावो धनमादत्तवाजि | पर कर्ष्णाय रुशदपिन्वतोधरतमत्र नकिरस्मा अपीपेत ||
10.31.e: To Nṛṣad's son they gave the name of Kainva, and he the brown-hued courser won the treasure.  For him dark-coloured streamed the shining udder: none made it swell for him. Thus Order willed it.

10.32.d: पर सु गमन्ता धियसानस्य सक्षणि वरेभिर्वरानभिषु परसीदतः | अस्माकमिन्द्र उभयं जुजोषति यत्सोम्यस्यान्धसो बुबोधति ||
10.32.e: FORTH speed the Pair to bring the meditating God, benevolent with boons sent in return for boons.  May Indra graciously accept both gifts from us, when he hath knowledge of the flowing Soma juice.

10.32.d: वीन्द्र यासि दिव्यानि रोचना वि पार्थिवानि रजसापुरुष्टुत | ये तवा वहन्ति मुहुरध्वरानुप ते सुवन्वन्तु वग्यनानराधसः ||
10.32.e: Thou wanderest far, O Indra, through the spheres of light and realms of earth, the region, thou whom many praise!  Let those who often bring their solemn rites conquer the noisy babblers who present no gifts.

10.32.d: तदिन मे छन्त्सत वपुषो वपुष्टरं पुत्रो यज्जानम्पित्रोरधीयति | जाया पतिं वहति वग्नुना सुमत पुंसैद भद्रो वहतुः परिष्क्र्तः ||
10.32.e: More beautiful than beauty must this seem to me, when the son duly careth for his parents' line.  The wife attracts the husband: with a shout of joy the man's auspicious marriage is performed aright.

10.32.d: तदित सधस्थमभि चारु दीधय गावो यच्छासन्वहतुं न धेनवः | माता यन मन्तुर्यूथस्यपूर्व्याभि वाणस्य सप्तधातुरिज्जनः ||
10.32.e: This beauteous place of meeting have I looked upon, where, like milch-cows, the kine order the marriage train;  Where the Herd's Mother counts as first and best of all, and round her are the seven-toned people of the choir.

10.32.d: पर वो.अछा रिरिचे देवयुष पदमेको रुद्रेभिर्यातितुर्वणिः | जरा वा येष्वम्र्तेषु दावने परि वूमेभ्यः सिञ्चता मधु ||
10.32.e: The Pious One hath reached your place before the rest: One only moves victorious with the Rudras' band.  To these your helpers pour our meath, Immortal Gods, with whom your song of praise hath power to win their gifts.

10.32.d: निधीयमानमपगूळमप्सु पर मे देवानां वरतपाुवाच | इन्द्रो विद्वाननु हि तवा चचक्ष तेनाहमग्नेनुशिष्ट आगाम ||
10.32.e: He who maintains the Laws of God informed me that thou wast lying hidden in the waters.  Indra, who knoweth well, beheld and showed thee. By him instructed am I come, O Agni.

10.32.d: अक्षेत्रवित कषेत्रविदं हयप्राट स परैतिक्षेत्रविदानुशिष्टः | एतद वै भद्रमनुशासनोस्योतस्रुतिं विन्दत्यञ्जसीनाम ||
10.32.e: The stranger asks the way of him who knows it: taught by the skilful guide he travels onward.  This is, in truth, the blessing of instruction: he finds the path that leads directly forward.

10.32.d: अद्येदु पराणीदममन्निमाहापीव्र्तो अधयन मातुरूधः | एमेनमाप जरिमा युवानमहेळन वसुः सुमनाबभूव ||
10.32.e: Even now he breathed: these days hath he remembered. Concealed, he sucked the bosom of his Mother.  Yet in his youth old age hath come upon him: he hath grown gracious, good, and free from anger.

10.32.d: एतानि भद्रा कलश करियाम कुरुश्रवण ददतो मघानि | दान इद वो मघवानः सो अस्त्वयं च सोमो हर्दि यम्बिभर्मि ||
10.32.e: O Kalasa, all these blessings will we bring them, O Kurusravana, who give rich presents.  May he, O wealthy princes, and this Soma which I am bearing in my heart, reward you.

10.33.d: पर मा युयुज्रे परयुजो जनानां वहामि सम पुषणमन्तरेण | विश्वे देवासो अध मामरक्षन दुःशासुरागादिति घोष आसीत ||
10.33.e: THE urgings of the people have impelled me, and by,the nearest way I bring you Pūṣan.  The Universal Gods have brought me safely. The cry was heard, Behold, Dubsasu cometh!

10.33.d: सं मा तपन्त्यभितः सपत्नीरिव पर्शवः | नि बाधतेमतिर्नग्नता जसुर्वेर्न वेवीयते मतिः ||
10.33.e: The ribs that compass me give pain and trouble me like rival wives.  Indigence, nakedness, exhaustion press me sore: my mind is fluttering like a bird's.

10.33.d: मूषो न शिश्ना वयदन्ति माध्य सतोतारं ते शतक्रतो | सक्र्त सु नो मघवन्निन्द्र मर्ळयाधा पितेव नो भव ||
10.33.e: As rats eat weavers' threads, cares are consuming me, thy singer, gatakratu, me.  Have mercy on us once, O Indra, Bounteous Lord: be thou a Father unto us.
I the priests' Ṛṣi chose as prince most liberal Kurusravana,  The son of Trasadasyu's son,

10.33.d: यस्य मा हरितो रथे तिस्रो वहन्ति साधुया | सतवैसहस्रदक्षिणे ||
10.33.e: Whose three bays harnessed to the car bear me straight onward: I will laud  The giver of a thousand meeds,

10.33.d: यस्य परस्वादसो गिर उपमश्रवसः पितुः | कषेत्रं नरण्वमूचुषे ||
10.33.e: The sire of Upamasravas, even him whose words were passing sweet,  As a fair field is to its lord.

10.33.d: अधि पुत्रोपमश्रवो नपान मित्रातिथेरिहि | पितुष टे अस्मिवन्दिता ||
10.33.e: Mark, Upamasravas, his son, mark, grandson of Mitratithi:  I am thy father's eulogist.
If I controlled Immortal Gods, yea, even were I Lord of men,  My liberal prince were living still.

10.33.d: न देवानामति वरतं शतात्मा चन जीवति | तथायुजा वि वाव्र्ते ||
10.33.e: None lives, even had he hundred lives, beyond the statute of the Gods  So am I parted from my friend.

10.34.d: परावेपा मा बर्हतो मादयन्ति परवातेजा इरिणे वर्व्र्तानाः | सोमस्येव मौजवतस्य भक्षो विभीदको जाग्र्विर्मह्यमछान ||
10.34.e: SPRUNG from tall trees on windy heights, these rollers transport me as they turn upon the table.  Dearer to me the die that never slumbers than the deep draught of Mujavan's own Soma.

10.34.d: न मा मिमेथ न जिहीळ एषा शिवा सखिभ्य उत मह्यमासीत | अक्षस्याहमेकपरस्य हेतोरनुव्रतामप जायामरोधम ||
10.34.e: She never vexed me nor was angry with me, but to my friends and me was ever gracious.  For the die's sake, whose single point is final, mine own devoted wife I alienated.

10.34.d: दवेष्टि शवश्रूरप जाया रुणद्धि न नाथितो विन्दतेमर्डितारम | अश्वस्येव जरतो वस्न्यस्य नाहं विन्दामिकितवस्य भोगम ||
10.34.e: My wife holds me aloof, her mother hates me: the wretched man finds none to give him comfort.  As of a costly horse grown old and feeble, I find not any profit of the gamester.

10.34.d: अन्ये जायां परि मर्शन्त्यस्य यस्याग्र्धद वेदने वाज्यक्षः | पिता मता भरातर एनमाहुर्न जानीमो नयताबद्धमेतम ||
10.34.e: Others caress the wife of him whose riches the die hath coveted, that rapid courser:  Of him speak father, mother, brothers saying, We know him not: bind him and take him with you.

10.34.d: यदादीध्ये न दविषाण्येभिः परायद्भ्यो.अव हीयेसखिभ्यः | नयुप्ताश्च बभ्रवो वाचमक्रतनेमीदेषां निष्क्र्तं जारिणीव ||
10.34.e: When I resolve to play with these no longer, my friends depart from me and leave me lonely.  When the brown dice, thrown on the board, have rattled, like a fond girl I seek the place of meeting.

10.34.d: सभामेति कितवः पर्छमानो जेष्यामीति तन्वाशूशुजानः | अक्षासो अस्य वि तिरन्ति कामं परतिदीव्नेदधत आ कर्तानि ||
10.34.e: The gamester seeks the gambling-house, and wonders, his body all afire, Shall I be lucky?  Still do the dice extend his eager longing, staking his gains against his adversary.

10.34.d: अक्षास इदनकुशिनो नितोदिनो निक्र्त्वानस्तपनास्तापयिष्णवः | कुमारदेष्णा जयतः पुनर्हणो मध्वासम्प्र्क्ताः कितवस्य बर्हणा ||
10.34.e: Dice, verily, are armed with goads and driving-hooks, deceiving and tormenting, causing grievous woe.  They give frail gifts and then destroy the man who wins, thickly anointed with the player's fairest good.

10.34.d: तरिपञ्चाशः करीळति वरात एषां देव इव सवितासत्यधर्मा | उग्रस्य चिन मन्यवे ना नमन्ते राजा चिदेभ्योनम इत कर्णोति ||
10.34.e: Merrily sports their troop, the three-and-fifty, like Savitar the God whose ways are faithful.  They bend not even to the mighty's anger: the King himself pays homage and reveres them.

10.34.d: नीचा वर्तन्त उपरि सफुरन्त्यहस्तासो हस्तवन्तं सहन्ते | दिव्या अङगारा इरिणे नयुप्ताः शीताः सन्तो हर्दयंनिर्दहन्ति ||
10.34.e: Downward they roll, and then spring quickly upward, and, handless, force the man with hands to serve them.  Cast on the board, like lumps of magic charcoal, though cold themselves they burn the heart to ashes.

10.34.d: जाया तप्यते कितवस्य हीना माता पुत्रस्य चरतः कवस्वित | रणावा बिभ्यद धनमिछमानो.अन्येषामस्तमुपनक्तमेति ||
10.34.e: The gambler's wife is left forlorn and wretched: the mother mourns the son who wanders homeless.  In constant fear, in debt, and seeking riches, he goes by night unto the home of others.

10.34.d: सत्रियं दर्ष्ट्वाय कितवं ततापान्येषां जायांसुक्र्तं च योनिम | पूर्वाह्णे अश्वान युयुजे हि बभ्रून सोग्नेरन्ते वर्षलः पपाद ||
10.34.e: Sad is the gambler when he sees a matron, another's wife, and his well-ordered dwelling.  He yokes the brown steeds in the early morning, and when the fire is cold sinks down an outcast.

10.34.d: यो वः सेनानीर्महतो गणस्य राजा वरातस्य परथमोबभूव | तस्मै कर्णोमि न धना रुणध्मि दशाहम्प्राचीस्तद रतं वदामि ||
10.34.e: To the great captain of your mighty army, who hath become the host's imperial leader,  To him I show my ten extended fingers: I speak the truth. No wealth am I withholding.

10.34.d: अक्षैर्मा दीव्यः कर्षिमित कर्षस्व वित्ते रमस्व बहुमन्यमानः | तत्र गावः कितव तत्र जाया तन मे विचष्टे सवितायमर्यः ||
10.34.e: Play not with dice: no, cultivate thy corn-land. Enjoy the gain, and deem that wealth sufficient.  There are thy cattle there thy wife, O gambler. So this good Savitar himself hath told me.

10.34.d: मित्रं कर्णुध्वं खलु मर्लता नो मा नो घोरेण चरताभिध्र्ष्णु | नि वो नु मन्युर्विशतामरातिरन्यो बभ्रूणाम्प्रसितौ नवस्तु ||
10.34.e: Make me your friend: show us some little mercy. Assail us not with your terrific fierceness.  Appeased be your malignity and anger, and let the brown dice snare some other captive.

10.35.d: अबुध्रमु तय इन्द्रवन्तो अग्नयो जयोतिर्भरन्त उषसोव्युष्टिषु | मही दयावाप्र्थिवी चेततामपो.अद्यादेवानामव आ वर्णीमहे ||
10.35.e: THESE fires associate with Indra are awake, bringing their light when first the Dawn begins to shine.  May Heaven and Earth, great Pair, observe our holy work. We claim for us this day the favour of the Gods.

10.35.d: दिवस्प्र्थिव्योरव आ वर्णीमहे मातॄन सिन्धून पर्वताञ्छर्यणावतः | अनागास्त्वं सूर्यमुषासमीमहे भद्रंसोमः सुवानो अद्या कर्णोतु नः ||
10.35.e: Yea, for ourselves we claim the grace of Heaven and Earth, of Śaryaṇāvān, of the Hills and Mother Streams.  For innocence we pray to Sūrya and to Dawn. So may the flowing Soma bring us bliss to-day.

10.35.d: दयावा नो अद्य पर्थिवी अनागसो मही तरायेतां सुवितायमातरा | उषा उछन्त्यप बाधतामघं सवस्त्यग्निंसमिधानमीमहे ||
10.35.e: May the great Twain, the Mothers, Heaven and Earth, this day preserve us free from sin for peace and happiness.  May Morning sending forth her light drive sin afar. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.

10.35.d: इयं न उस्रा परथमा सुदेव्यं रेवत सनिभ्यो रेवती वयुछतु | आरे मन्युं दुर्विदत्रस्य धीमहि सवस्त्यग्निंसमिधानमीमहे ||
10.35.e: May this first Dawn bring us the host of gracious Gods: rich, may it richly shine for us who strive for wealth.  The wrath of the malignant may we keep afar. We pray to kindled Agni for feilicity.

10.35.d: पर याः सिस्रते सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिर्ज्योतिर्भरन्तीरुषसो वयुष्टिषु | भद्रा नो अद्य शरवसे वयुछत सवस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ||
10.35.e: Dawns, who come forward with the bright beams of the Sun, and at your earliest flushing bring to us the light,  Shine ye on us to-day auspicious, for renown. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.

10.35.d: अनमीवा उषस आ चरन्तु न उदग्नयो जिहतां जयोतिषाब्र्हत | आयुक्षातामश्विना तूतुजिं रथं सवस्त्यग्निंसमिधानमीमहे ||
10.35.e: Free from all sickness may the Mornings come to us, and let our fires mount upward with a lofty blaze.  The Aśvin Pair have harnessed their swift-moving car. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.

10.35.d: शरेष्ठं नो अद्य सवितर्वरेण्यं भागमा सुव स हिरत्नधा असि | रायो जनित्रीं धिषणामुप बरुवे सवस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ||
10.35.e: Send us to-day a portion choice and excellent, O Savitar, for thou art he who dealeth wealth.  I cry to Dhiṣaṇā, Mother of opulence. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.

10.35.d: पिपर्तु मा तद रतस्य परवाचनं देवानां यन मनुष्यामन्महि | विश्वा इदुस्रा सपळ उदेति सूर्यः सवस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ||
10.35.e: Further me this declaring of Eternal Law, the Law of Gods, as we mortals acknowledge it!  The Sun goes up beholding all the rays of morn. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.

10.35.d: अद्वेषो अद्य बर्हिष सतरीमणि गराव्णां योगे मन्मनःसाध ईमहे | आदित्यानां शर्मणि सथा भुरण्यसि सवस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ||
10.35.e: This day we pray with innocence in strewing grass, adjusting pressing-stones, and perfecting the hymn.  Thou in the Ādityas’ keeping movest restlessly. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.

10.35.d: आ नो बर्हिः सधमादे बर्हद दिवि देवानीळे सादयासप्त होतॄन | इन्द्रं मित्रं वरुणं सातये भगं सवस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ||
10.35.e: To our great holy grass I bid the Gods at morn to banquet, and will seat them as the seven priests,—  Varuṇa, Indra, Mitra, Bhaga for our gain. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.

10.35.d: त आदित्या आ गता सर्वतातये वर्धे नो यज्ञमवतासजोषसः | बर्हस्पतिं पूषणमश्विना भगं सवस्त्यग्निं समिधानमीमहे ||
10.35.e: Come hither, O Ādityas, for our perfect weal: accordant help our sacrifice that we may thrive.  Pūṣan, Bṛhaspati, Bhaga, both Aśvins, and enkindled Agni we implore for happiness.

10.35.d: तन नो देवा यछत सुप्रवाचनं छर्दिरादित्याः सुभरंन्र्पाय्यम | पश्वे तोकाय तनयाय जीवसे सवस्त्यग्निंसमिधानमीमहे ||
10.35.e: Ādityas, Gods, vouchsafe that this our home may be praise-worthy, prosperous, our heroes' sure defence,  For cattle, for our sons, for progeny, for life. We pray to kindled Agni for felicity.

10.35.d: विश्वे अद्य मरुतो विश्व ऊती विश्वे भवन्त्वग्नयःसमिद्धाः | विश्वे नो देवा अवसा गमन्तु विश्वमस्तुद्रविणं वाजो अस्मे ||
10.35.e: This day may all the Maruts, all he near us with aid: may all our fires be well enkindled.  May all Gods come to us with gracious favour. May spoil and wealth he ours, and all possessions.

10.35.d: यं देवासो.अवथ वाजसातौ यं तरायध्वे यं पिप्र्थात्यंहः | यो वो गोपीथे न भयस्य वेद ते सयामदेववीतये तुरासः ||
10.35.e: He whom ye aid, O Deities, in battle, whom ye protect and rescue from affliction,  Who fears no danger at your milk-libation, -such may we be to feast the Gods, ye Mighty.

10.36.d: उषासानक्ता बर्हती सुपेशसा दयावाक्षामा वरुणोमित्रो अर्यमा | इन्द्रं हुवे मरुतः पर्वतानप आदित्यान्द्यावाप्र्थिवी अपः सवः ||
10.36.e: THERE are the Dawn and Night, the grand and beauteous Pair, Earth, Heaven, and Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman.  Indra I call, the Maruts, Mountains, and the Floods, Ādityas, Heaven and Earth, the Waters, and the Sky.

10.36.d: दयौश्च नः पर्थिवी च परचेतस रतावरी रक्षतामंहसोरिषः | मा दुर्विदत्रा निरतिर्न ईशत तद देवानामवोद्या वर्णीमहे ||
10.36.e: May Dyaus and Prthivi, wise, true to Holy Law, keep us in safety from distress and injury.  Let not malignant Nirrti rule over us. We crave to-day this gracious favour of the Gods.

10.36.d: विश्वस्मान नो अदितिः पात्वंहसो माता मित्रस्य वरुणस्यरेवतः | सवर्वज्ज्योतिरव्र्कं नशीमहि तद देवानां ... ||
10.36.e: Mother of Mitra and of opulent Varuṇa, may Aditi preserve us safe from all distress.  May we obtain the light of heaven without a foe. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.

10.36.d: गरावा वदन्नप रक्षांसि सेधतु दुष्वप्न्यं निरतिंविश्वमत्रिणम | आदित्यं शर्म मरुतामशीमहि तद्देवानां ... ||
10.36.e: May ringing press-stones keep the Rākṣasas afar, ill dream, and Nirrti, and each voracious fiend.  May the Ādityas and the Maruts shelter us. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.

10.36.d: एन्द्रो बर्हिः सीदतु पिन्वतामिळा बर्हस्पतिः सामभिरकवो अर्चतु | सुप्रकेतं जीवसे मन्म धीमहि तद्देवानां ... ||
10.36.e: Full flow libations; on our grass let Indra sit; Bṛhaspati the singer laud with Sāma hymns!  Wise be our hearts' imaginings that we may live. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.

10.36.d: दिविस्प्र्शं यज्ञमस्माकमश्विना जीराध्वरं कर्णुतंसुम्नमिष्टये | पराचीनरश्मिमाहुतं घर्तेन तद्देवानां ... ||
10.36.e: Ye Aśvins, make our sacrifice ascend to heaven, and animate the rite that it may send us bliss,  Offered with holy oil, with forward-speeding rein. We crave the gracious favour of the Gods to-day.

10.36.d: उप हवये सुहवं मारुतं गणं पावकं रष्वं सख्यायशम्भुवम | रायस पोषं सौश्रवसाय धीमहि तद्देवानां ... ||
10.36.e: Hither I call the band of Maruts, swift to hear, great, purifying, bringing bliss, to he our Friends.  May we increase our wealth to glorify our name. We crave this graciousfavour of the Gods to-day.

10.36.d: अपां पेरुं जीवधन्यं भरामहे देवाव्यं सुहवमध्वरश्रियम | सुरश्मिं सोममिन्द्रियं यमीमहि तद्देवानां ... ||
10.36.e: We bring the Stay of Life, who makes the waters swell, swift-hearing, Friend of Gods, who waits on sacrifice.  May we control that Power, Soma whose rays are bright. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.

10.36.d: सनेम तत सुसनिता सनित्वभिर्वयं जीवा जीवपुत्रानागसः | बरह्मद्विषो विष्वगेनो भरेरत तद्देवानां ... ||
10.36.e: Alive ourselves, with living sons, devoid of guilt, may we win this with winners by fair means to win.  Let the prayer-haters bear our sin to every side. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.

10.36.d: ये सथा मनोर्यज्ञियास्ते शर्णोतन यद वो देवा ईमहेतद ददातन | जैत्रं करतुं रयिमद वीरवद यशस्तद्देवानां ... ||
10.36.e: Hear us, O ye who claim the worship of mankind, and give us, O ye Gods, the gift for which we pray,  Victorious wisdom, fame with heroes and with wealth. We crave to-day this gracious favour of the Gods.

10.36.d: महदद्य महतामा वर्णीमहे.अवो देवानां बर्हतामनर्वणाम | यथा वसु वीरजातं नशामहै तद्देवानां ... ||
10.36.e: We crave the gracious favour of the Gods to-day, great favour of great Gods, sublime and free from foes,  That we may gain rich treasure sprung from hero sons. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.

10.36.d: महो अग्नेः समिधानस्य शर्मण्यनागा मित्रे वरुणेस्वस्तये | शरेष्ठे सयाम सवितुः सवीमनि तद्देवानां ... ||
10.36.e: In great enkindled Agni's keeping, and, for bliss, free from all sin before Mitra and Varuṇa.  May we share Savitar's best animating help. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day.

10.36.d: ये सवितुः सत्यसवस्य विश्वे मित्रस्य वरते वरुणस्यदेवाः | ते सौभगं वीरवद गोमदप्नो दधातनद्रविणं चित्रमस्मे ||
10.36.e: All ye, the Gods whom Savitar the Father of truth, and Varuṇa and Mitra govern,  Give us prosperity with hero children, and opulence in kine and various treasure.

10.36.d: सविता पश्चातात सविता पुरस्तात सवितोत्तरात्तात्सविताधरात्तात | सविता नः सुवतु सर्वतातिं सविता नोरासतां दीर्घमयुः ||
10.36.e: Savitar, Savitar from cast and westward, Savitar, Savitar from north and southward,  Savitar send us perfect health and comfort, Savitar let our days of life be lengthened!

10.37.d: नमो मित्रस्य वरुणस्य चक्षसे महो देवाय तद रतंसपर्यत | दूरेद्र्शे देवजाताय केतवे दिवस पुत्रायसूर्याय शंसत ||
10.37.e: Do homage unto Varuṇa's and Mitra's Eye: offer this solemn worship to the Mighty God,  Who seeth far away, the Ensign, born of Gods. Sing praises unto Sūrya, to the Son of Dyaus.

10.37.d: सा मा सत्योक्तिः परि पातु विश्वतो दयावा च यत्रततनन्नहानि च | विश्वमन्यन नि विशते यदेजतिविश्वाहापो विश्वाहोदेति सूर्यः ||
10.37.e: May this my truthful speech guard me on every side wherever heaven and earth and days are spread abroad.  All else that is in motion finds a place of rest: the waters ever flow and ever mounts the Sun.

10.37.d: न ते अदेवः परदिवो नि वासते यदेतशेभिः पतरैरथर्यसि | पराचीनमन्यदनु वर्तते रज उदन्येनज्योतिषा यासि सूर्य ||
10.37.e: No godless man from time remotest draws thee down when thou art driving forth with winged dappled Steeds.  One lustre waits upon thee moving to the cast, and, Sūrya, thou arisest with a different light.

10.37.d: येन सूर्य जयोतिषा बाधसे तमो जगच्च विश्वमुदियर्षिभानुना | तेनास्मद विश्वामनिरामनाहुतिमपामीवामप दुष्वप्न्यं सुव ||
10.37.e: O Sūrya, with the light whereby thou scatterest gloom, and with thy ray impellest every moving thing,  Keep far from us all feeble, worthless sacrifice, and drive away disease and every evil dream.

10.37.d: विश्वस्य हि परेषितो रक्षसि वरतमहेळयन्नुच्चरसिस्वधा अनु | यदद्य तवा सूर्योपब्रवामहै तं नो देवानु मंसीरत करतुम ||
10.37.e: Sent forth thou guardest well the Universe's law, and in thy wonted way arisest free from wrath.  When Sūrya, we address our prayers to thee to-day, may the Gods favour this our purpose and desire.

10.37.d: तं नो दयावाप्र्थिवी तन न आप इन्द्रः शर्ण्वन्तु मरुतोहवं वचः | मा शूने भूम सूर्यस्य सन्द्र्शिभद्रं जीवन्तो जरणामशीमहि ||
10.37.e: This invocation, these our words may Heaven and Earth, and Indra and the Waters and the Maruts hear.  Ne’er may we suffer want in presence of the Sun, and, living happy lives, may we attain old age.

10.37.d: विश्वाहा तवा सुमनसः सुचक्षसः परजावन्तो अनमीवानागसः | उद्यन्तं तवा मित्रमहो दिवे-दिवे जयोग जीवाःप्रति पश्येम सूर्य ||
10.37.e: Cheerful in spirit, evermore, and keen of sight, with store of children, free from sickness and from sin,  Long-living, may we look, O Sūrya, upon thee uprising day by day, thou great as Mitra is!

10.37.d: महि जयोतिर्बिभ्रतं तवा विचक्षण भास्वन्तं चक्षुषे चक्षुषे मयः | आरोहन्तं बर्हतः पाजसस परि वयंजीवाः परति पश्येम सूर्य ||
10.37.e: Sūrya, may we live long and look upon thee still, thee, O Far-seeing One, bringing the glorious light,  The radiant God, the spring of joy to every eye, as thou art mounting up o’er the high shining flood.

10.37.d: यस्य ते विश्वा भुवनानि केतुना पर चेरते नि च विशन्तेक्तुभिः | अनागास्त्वेन हरिकेश सूर्याह्नाह्ना नोवस्यसा-वस्यसोदिहि ||
10.37.e: Thou by whose lustre all the world of life comes forth, and by thy beams again returns unto its rest,  O Sūrya with the golden hair, ascend for us day after day, still bringing purer innocence.

10.37.d: शं नो भव चक्षसा शं नो अह्ना शं भानुना शंहिमा शं घर्णेन | यथा शमध्वञ्छमसद दुरोणेतत सूर्य दरविणं धेहि चित्रम ||
10.37.e: Bless us with shine, bless us with perfect daylight, bless us with cold, with fervent heat and lustre.  Bestow on us, O Sūrya, varied riches, to bless us in our home and when we travel.

10.37.d: अस्माकं देवा उभयाय जन्मने शर्म यछत दविपदेचतुष्पदे | अदत पिबदूर्जयमानमाशितं तदस्मेशं योररपो दधातन ||
10.37.e: Gods, to our living creatures of both kinds vouchsafe protection, both to bipeds and to quadrupeds,  That they may drink and eat invigorating food. So grant us health and strength and perfect innocence.

10.37.d: यद वो देवाश्चक्र्म जिह्वया गुरु मनसो वा परयुतीदेवहेळनम | अरावा यो नो अभि दुछुनायते तस्मिन तदेनोवसवो नि धेतन ||
10.37.e: If by some grievous sin we have provoked the Gods, O Deities, with the tongue or thoughtlessness of heart,  That guilt, O Vasus, lay upon the Evil One, on him who ever leads us into deep distress.

10.38.d: अस्मिन न इन्द्र पर्त्सुतौ यशस्वति शिमीवति करन्दसि परावसातये | यत्र गोषाता धर्षितेषु खादिषु विष्वक्पतन्ति दिद्यवो नर्षाह्ये ||
10.38.e: O INDRA, in this battle great and glorious, in this loud din of war help us to victory,  Where in the strife for kine among bold ring-decked men arrows fly all around and heroes are subdued.

10.38.d: स नः कषुमन्तं सदने वयूर्णुहि गोर्णसं रयिमिन्द्रश्रवाय्यम | सयाम ते जयतः शक्र मेदिनो यथा वयमुश्मसि तद वसो कर्धि ||
10.38.e: At home disclose to us opulence rich in food, streaming with milk, O Indra, meet to be renowned.  Śakra, may we be thine, the friendly Conqueror's: even as we desire, O Vasu, so do thou.

10.38.d: यो नो दास आर्यो वा पुरुष्टुतादेव इन्द्र युधये चिकेतति | अस्माभिष टे सुषहाः सन्तु शत्रवस्त्वया वयं तान्वनुयाम संगमे ||
10.38.e: The godless man, much-lauded Indra, whether he be Dāsa or be Ārya, who would war with us,—  Easy to conquer he for thee, with us, these foes: with thee may we subdue them in the clash of fight.

10.38.d: यो दभ्रेभिर्हव्यो यश्च भूरिभिर्यो अभीके वरिवोविन्न्र्षाह्ये | तं विखादे सस्निमद्य शरुतं नरमर्वाञ्चमिन्द्रमवसे करामहे ||
10.38.e: Him who must be invoked by many and by few, who standeth nigh with comfort in the war of men,  Indra, famed Hero, winner in the deadly strife, let us bring hitherward to-day to favour us.

10.38.d: सवव्र्जं हि तवामहमिन्द्र शुश्रवानानुदं वर्षभरध्रचोदनम | पर मुञ्चस्व परि कुत्सादिहा गहि किमुत्वावान मुष्कयोर्बद्ध आसते ||
10.38.e: For, Indra, I have heard thee called Self. capturer, One, Steer! who never yields, who urges even the churl.  Release thyself from Kutsa and come hither. How shall one like thee sit still bound that he may not move?

10.39.d: यो वां परिज्मा सुव्र्दश्विना रथो दोषामुषासो हव्योहविष्मता | शश्वत्तमासस्तमु वामिदं वयं पितुर्ननाम सुहवं हवामहे ||
10.39.e: As ’twere the name of father, easy to invoke, we all assembled here invoke this Car of yours,  Aśvins, your swiftly-rolling circumambient Car which he who worships must invoke at eve and dawn.

10.39.d: चोदयतं सून्र्ताः पिन्वतं धिय उत पुरन्धीरीरयतन्तदुश्मसि | यशसं भागं कर्णुतं नो अश्विना सोमं नचारुं मघवत्सु नस कर्तम ||
10.39.e: Awake all pleasant strains and let the hymns flow forth: raise up abundant fulness: this is our desire.  Aśvins, bestow on us a glorious heritage, and give our princes treasure fair as Soma is.

10.39.d: अमाजुरश्चिद भवथो युवं भगो.अनाशोश्चिदवितारापमस्य चित | अन्धस्य चिन नासत्या कर्शस्य चिद युवामिदाहुर्भिषजा रुतस्य चित ||
10.39.e: Ye are the bliss of her who groweth old at home, and helpers of the slow although he linger last.  Men call you too, Nāsatyas, healers of the blind, the thin and feeble, and the man with broken bones.

10.39.d: युवं चयवानं सनयं यथा रथं पुनर्युवानंचरथाय तक्षथुः | निष टौग्र्यमूहथुरद्भ्यस परिविश्वेत ता वां सवनेषु परवाच्या ||
10.39.e: Ye made Cyavāna, weak and worn with length of days, young again, like a car, that he had power to move.  Ye lifted up the son of Tugra from the floods. At our libations must all these your acts be praised.

10.39.d: पुराणा वां वीर्या पर बरवा जने.अथो हासथुर्भिषजामयोभुवा | ता वां नु नव्याववसे करामहे.अयंनासत्या शरदरिर्यथा दधत ||
10.39.e: We will declare among the folk your ancient deeds heroic; yea, ye were Physicians bringing health.  You, you who must be lauded, will we bring for aid, so that this foe of ours, O Aśvins, may believe.

10.39.d: इयं वामह्वे शर्णुतं मे अश्विना पुत्रायेव पितरा मह्यंशिक्षतम | अनापिरज्ञा असजात्यामतिः पुरा तस्याभिशस्तेरव सप्र्तम ||
10.39.e: Listen to me, O Aśvins; I have cried to you. Give me-your aid as sire and mother aid their son.  Poor, without kin or friend or ties of blood am I. Save me before it be too late, from this my curse.

10.39.d: युवं रथेन विमदाय शुन्ध्युवं नयूहथुः पुरुमित्रस्ययोषणाम | युवं हवं वध्रिमत्या अगछतं युवंसुषुतिं चक्रथुः पुरन्धये ||
10.39.e: Ye, mounted on your chariot brought to Vimada the comely maid of Purumitra as a bride.  Ye, came unto the calling of the weakling's dame, and granted noble offspring to the happy wife.

10.39.d: युवं विप्रस्य जरणामुपेयुषः पुनः कलेरक्र्णुतंयुवद वयः | युवं वन्दनं रश्यदादुदूपथुर्युवंसद्यो विश्पलामेतवे कर्थः ||
10.39.e: Ye gave a ain the vigour of his youthful life to tge sage Kali when old age was coming nigh.  Ye rescued Vandana and raised him from the pit, and in a moment gave Viśpalā power to move.

10.39.d: युवं ह रेभं वर्षणा गुहा हितमुदैरयतम्मम्र्वांसमश्विना | युवं रबीसमुत तप्तमत्रयोमन्वन्तं चक्रथुः सप्तवध्रये ||
10.39.e: Ye Aśvins Twain, endowed with manly strength, brought forth Reblia when hidden in the cave and well-nigh dead,  Freed Saptavadliri, and for Atri caused the pit heated with fire to be a pleasant resting-place.

10.39.d: युवं शवेतं पेदवे.अश्विनाश्वं नवभिर्वाजैर्नवतीच वाजिनम | चर्क्र्त्यं ददथुर्द्रावयत्सखं भगं नन्र्भ्यो हव्यं मयोभुबम ||
10.39.e: On Pedu ye bestowed, Aśvins, a courser white, mighty with nine-and-ninety varied gifts of strength,  A horse to be renowned, who bore his friend at speed, joy-giving, Bhaga-like to be invoked of men.

10.39.d: न तं राजानावदिते कुतश्चन नांहो अश्नोति दुरितंनकिर्भयम | यमश्विना सुहवा रुद्रवर्तनी पुरोरथंक्र्णुथः पत्न्या सह ||
10.39.e: From no side, ye Two Kings whom none may check or stay, doth grief, distress, or danger come u on the man  Whom, Aśvins swift to hear, borne on your glowing path, ye with your Consort make the foremost in the race.

10.39.d: आ तेन यातं मनसो जवीयसा रथं यं वां रभवश्चक्रुरश्विना | यस्य योगे दुहिता जायते दिव उभे अहनीसुदिने विवस्वतः ||
10.39.e: Come on that Chariot which the Ṛbhus wrought for you, the Chariot, Aśvins, that is speedier than thought,  At harnessing whereof Heaven's Daughter springs to birth, and from Vivasvān come auspicious Night and Day.

10.39.d: ता वर्तिर्यातं जयुषा वि पर्वतमपिन्वतं शयवेधेनुमश्विना | वर्कस्य चिद वर्तिकामन्तरास्याद युवंशचीभिर्ग्रसिताममुञ्चतम ||
10.39.e: Come, Conquerors of the sundered mountain, to our home, Aśvins who made the cow stream milk for Śayu's sake,  Ye who delivered even from the wolf's deep throat and set again at liberty the swallowed quail.

10.39.d: एतं वां सतोममश्विनावकर्मातक्षाम भर्गवो न रथम | नयम्र्क्षाम योषणां न मर्ये नित्यं न सूनुन्तनयं दधानाः ||
10.39.e: We have prepared this laud for you, O Aśvins, and, like the Bhṛgus, as a car have framed it,  Have decked it as a maid to meet the bridegroom, and brought it as a son, our stay for ever.

10.40.d: रथं यान्तं कुह को ह वां नरा परति दयुमन्तंसुविताय भूषति | परातर्यावाणं विभ्वं विशे-विशेवस्तोर वस्तोर्वहमानं धिया शमि ||
10.40.e: YOUR radiant Chariot-whither goes it on its way?-who decks it for you, Heroes, for its happy course,  Starting at daybreak, visiting each morning every house, borne hitherward through prayer unto the sacrifice?

10.40.d: कुह सविद दोषा कुह वस्तोरश्विना कुहाभिपित्वं करतःकुहोषतुः | को वां शयुत्रा विधवेव देवरं मर्यं नयोषा कर्णुते सधस्थ आ ||
10.40.e: Where are ye, Aśvins, in the evening, where at morn? Where is your haltingplace, where rest ye for the night?  Who brings you homeward, as the widow bedward draws her husband's brother, as the bride attracts the groom?

10.40.d: परातर्जरेथे जरणेव कापया वस्तोर-वस्तोर्यजता गछथोग्र्हम | कस्य धवस्रा भवथः कस्य वा नरा राजपुत्रेवसवनाव गछथः ||
10.40.e: Early ye sing forth praise as with a herald's voice, and, meet for worship, go each morning to the house.  Whom do ye ever bring to ruin? Unto whose libations come ye, Heroes, like two Sons of Kings?

10.40.d: युवां मर्गेव वारणा मर्गण्यवो दोषा वस्तोर्हविषा निह्वयामहे | युवं होत्रां रतुथा जुह्वते नरेषं जनायवहथः शुभस पती ||
10.40.e: Even as hunters follow two wild elephants, we with oblations call you down at morn and eve.  To folk who pay you offierings at appointed times, Chiefs, Lords of splendour, ye bring food to strengthen them.

10.40.d: युवां ह घोषा पर्यश्विना यती राज्ञ ऊचे दुहिताप्र्छे वां नरा | भूतं मे अह्न उत भूतमक्तवेऽशवावते रथिने शक्तमर्वते ||
10.40.e: To you, O Aśvins, came the daughter of a King, Ghoṣā, and said, O Heroes, this I beg of you:  Be near me in the day, he near me in the night: help me to gain a car-borne chieftain rich in steeds.
