10.40.d: युवं कवी षठः पर्यश्विना रथं विशो न कुत्सोजरितुर्नशायथः | युवोर्ह मक्षा पर्यश्विना मध्वासा भरत निष्क्र्तं न योषणा ||
10.40.e: O Aśvins, ye are wise: as Kutsa comes to men, bring your car nigh the folk of him who sings your praise.  The bee, O Aśvins, bears your honey in her mouth, as the maid carries it purified in her hand.

10.40.d: युवं ह भुज्युं युवमश्विना वशं युवं शिञ्जारमुशनामुपारथुः | युवो ररावा परि सख्यमासते युवोरहमवसा सुम्नमा चके ||
10.40.e: To Bhujyu and to Vaśa ye come near with help, O Aśvins, to Sinjara and to Uśanā.  Your worshipper secures your friendship for himself. Through your protection I desire felicity.

10.40.d: युवं ह कर्शं युवमश्विना शयुं युवं विधन्तंविधवामुरुष्यथः | युवं सनिभ्य सतनयन्तमश्विनापव्रजमूर्णुथः सप्तास्यम ||
10.40.e: Krsa and Śayu ye protect, ye Aśvins Twain: ye Two assist the widow and the worshipper;  And ye throw open, Aśvins, unto those who win the cattle-stall that thunders with its serenfold mouth.

10.40.d: जनिष्ट योषा पतयत कनीनको वि चारुहन वीरुधोदंसना अनु | आस्मै रीयन्ते निवनेव सिन्धवो.अस्मा अह्नेभवति तत पतित्वनम ||
10.40.e: The Woman hath brought forth, the Infant hath appeared, the plants of wondrous beauty straightway have sprung up.  To him the rivers run as down a deep descent, and he this day becomes their master and their lord.

10.40.d: जीवं रुदन्ति वि मयन्ते अध्वरे दीर्घामनु परसितिन्दीधियुर्नरः | वामं पित्र्भ्यो य इदं समेरिरे मयःपतिभ्यो जनयः परिष्वजे ||
10.40.e: They mourn the living, cry aloud, at sacrifice: the men have set their thoughts upon a distant cast.  A lovely thing for fathers who have gathered here,—a joy to husbands,—are the wives their arms shall clasp

10.40.d: न तस्य विद्म तदु षु पर वोचत युवा ह यद युवत्याःक्षेति योनिषु | परियोस्रियस्य वर्षभस्य रेतिनो गर्हंगमेमाश्विना तदुश्मसि ||
10.40.e: Of this we have no knowledge. Tall it forth to us, now the youth rests within the chambers of the bride.  Fain would we reach the dwelling of the vigorous Steer who loves the kine, O Aśvins: this is our desire.

10.40.d: आ वामगन सुमतिर्वाजिनीवसू नयश्विना हर्त्सु कामायंसत | अभूतं गोपा मिथुना शुभस पती परियार्यम्णो दुर्यानशीमहि ||
10.40.e: Your favouring grace hath come, ye Lords of ample wealth: Aśvins, our longings are stored up within your hearts.  Ye, Lords of splendour, have become our twofold guard: may we as welcome friends reach Aryaman's abode.

10.40.d: ता मन्दसाना मनुषो दुरोण आ धत्तं रयिं सहवीरंवचस्यवे | कर्तं तीर्थं सुप्रपाणं शुभस पतीस्थाणुं पथेष्ठामप दुर्मतिं हतम ||
10.40.e: Even so, rejoicing in the dwelling-place of man, give hero sons and riches to the eloquent.  Make a ford, Lords of splendour, where men well may drink: remove the spiteful tree-stump standing in the path.

10.40.d: कव सविदद्य कतमास्वश्विना विक्षु दस्रा मादयेतेशुभस पती | क ईं नि येमे कतमस्य जग्मतुर्विप्रस्य वायजमानस्य वा गर्हम ||
10.40.e: O Aśvins, Wonder-Workers, Lords of lustre, where and with what folk do ye delight yourselves to-day?  Who hath detained them with him? Whither are they gone? Unto what sage's or what worshipper's abode?

10.41.d: समानमु तयं पुरुहूतमुक्थ्यं रथं तरिचक्रं सवनागनिग्मतम | परिज्मानं विदथ्यं सुव्र्क्तिभिर्वयंव्युष्टा उषसो हवामहे ||
10.41.e: THAT general Car of yours, invoked by many a man, that comes to our libations, three-wheeled, meet for lauds,  That circumambient Car, worthy of sacrifice, we call with our pure hymns at earliest flush of dawn.

10.41.d: परातर्युजं नासत्याधि तिष्ठथः परातर्यावाणम्मधुवाहनं रथम | विशो येन गछथो यज्वरीर्नराकीरेश्चिद यज्ञं होत्र्मन्तमश्विना ||
10.41.e: Ye, O Nāsatyas, mount that early-harnessed Car, that travels early, laden with its freight of balm,  Wherewith ye, Heroes, visit clans who sacrifice, even the poor man's worship where the priest attends.

10.41.d: अध्वर्युं वा मधुपाणिं सुहस्त्यमग्निधं वाध्र्तदक्षं दमूनसम | विप्रस्य वा यत सवननि गछथोऽत आ यातं मधुपेयमश्विना ||
10.41.e: If to the deft Adhvaryu with the meath in hand, or to the Kindler firm in strength, the household friend,  Or to the sage's poured libations ye approach, come thence, O Aśvins, now to drink the offered meath.

10.42.d: अस्तेव सु परतरं लायमस्यन भूषन्निव पर भरास्तोममस्मै | वाचा विप्रास्तरत वाचमर्यो नि रामयजरितः सोम इन्द्रम ||
10.42.e: EVEN as an archer shoots afar his arrow, offer the laud to him with meet adornment.  Quell with your voice the wicked's voice, O sages. Singer, make Indra rest beside the Soma.

10.42.d: दोहेन गामुप शिक्षा सखायं पर बोधय जरितर्जारमिन्द्रम | कोशं न पूर्णं वसुना नय्र्ष्टमा चयावयमघदेयाय शूरम ||
10.42.e: Draw thy Friend to thee like a cow at milking: O Singer, wake up Indra as a lover.  Make thou the Hero haste to give us riches even as a vessel filled brimful with treasure.

10.42.d: किमङग तवा मघवन भोजमाहुः शिशीहि मा शिशयन्त्वा शर्णोमि | अप्नस्वती मम धीरस्तु शक्र वसुविदम्भगमिन्द्रा भरा नः ||
10.42.e: Why, Maghavan, do they call thee Bounteous; Giver? Quicken me: thou, I hear, art he who quickens.  Śakra, let my intelligence be active, and bring us luck that finds great wealth, O Indra.

10.42.d: तवां जना ममसत्येष्विन्द्र सन्तस्थाना वि हवयन्तेसमीके | अत्रा युजं कर्णुते यो हविष्मान नासुन्वतासख्यं वष्टि शूरः ||
10.42.e: Standing, in battle for their rights, together, the people, Indra, in the fray invoke thee.  Him who brings gifts the Hero makes his comrade: with him who pours no juice he seeks not friendship.

10.42.d: धनं न सयन्द्रं बहुलं यो अस्मै तीव्रान सोमानासुनोतिप्रयस्वान | तस्मै शत्रून सुतुकान परातरह्नो निस्वष्ट्रान युवति हन्ति वर्त्रम ||
10.42.e: Whoso with plenteous food for him expresses strong Somas as much quickly-coming treasure,  For him he overthrows in early morning his swift well-weaponed foes, and slays the tyrant.

10.42.d: यस्मिन वयं दधिमा शंसमिन्द्रे यः शिश्राय मघवाकाममस्मे | आराच्चित सन भयतामस्य शत्रुर्न्यस्मैद्युम्ना जन्या नमन्ताम ||
10.42.e: He unto whom we offer praises, Indra, Maghavan, who hath joined to ours his wishes,—  Before him even afar the foe must tremble: low before him must bow all human glories.

10.42.d: आराच्छत्रुमप बाधस्व दूरमुग्रो यः शम्बःपुरुहूत तेन | अस्मे धेहि यवमद गोमदिन्द्र कर्धी धियंजरित्रे वाजरत्नाम ||
10.42.e: With thy fierce bolt, O God invoked of many, drive to a distance from afar the foeman.  O Indra, give us wealth in corn and cattle, and make thy singer's prayer gain strength and riches.

10.42.d: पर यमन्तर्व्र्षसवासो अग्मन तीव्राः सोमा बहुलान्तासैन्द्रम | नाह दामानं मघवा नि यंसन नि सुन्वते वहतिभूरि वामम ||
10.42.e: Indra, the swallower of strong libations rich in the boons they bring, the potent Somas,  He, Maghavan, will not restrict his bounty he brings much wealth unto the Soma-presser.

10.42.d: उत परहामतिदीव्या जयाति कर्तं यच्छ्वघ्नी विचिनोतिकाले | यो देवकामो न धना रुणद्धि समित तं रायास्र्जति सवधावान ||
10.42.e: Yea, by superior play he wins advantage, when he, a gambler, piles his gains in season.  Celestial-natured, he o’erwhelms with riches the devotee who keeps not back his treasure.

10.42.d: गोभिष टरेमामतिं दुरेवां यवेन कषुधं पुरुहूतविश्वाम | वयं राजभिः परथमा धनान्यस्माकेनव्र्जनेना जयेम ||
10.42.e: O Much-invoked, may we subdue all famine and evil want with store of grain and cattle.  May we allied, as first in rank, with princes obtain possessions by our own exertion.

10.42.d: बर्हस्पतिर्नः परि पातु पश्चादुतोत्तरस्मादधरादघायोः | इद्रः पुरस्तादुत मध्यतो नः सखा सखिभ्योवरिवः कर्णोतु ||
10.42.e: Bṛhaspati protect us from the rearward, and from above, and from below, from sinners!  May Indra from the front, and from the centre, as Friend to friends, vouchsafe us room and freedom.

10.43.d: अछा म इन्द्रं मतयः सवर्विदः सध्रीचीर्विश्वाुशतीरनूषत | परि षवजन्ते जनयो यथा पतिं मर्यंन शुन्ध्युं मघवानमूतये ||
10.43.e: IN perfect unison all yearning hymns of mine that find the light of heaven have sung forth Indra's praise.  As wives embrace their lord, the comely bridegroom, so they compass Maghavan about that he may help.

10.43.d: न घा तवद्रिगप वेति मे मनस्त्वे इत कामं पुरुहूतशिश्रय | राजेव दस्म नि षदो.अधि बर्हिष्यस्मिन सु सोमेऽवपानमस्तु ते ||
10.43.e: Directed unto thee my spirit never strays, for I have set my hopes on thee, O Much-invoked!  Sit, Wonderful! as King upon the sacred grass, and let thy drinking-place be by the Soma juice.

10.43.d: विषूव्र्दिन्द्रो अमतेरुत कषुधः स इद रायो मघवावस्व ईशते | तस्येदिमे परवणे सप्त सिन्धवो वयोवर्धन्ति वर्षभस्य शुष्मिणः ||
10.43.e: From indigence and hunger Indra turns away: Maghavan hath dominion over precious wealth.  These the Seven Rivers flowing on their downward path increase the vital vigour of the potent Steer.

10.43.d: वयो न वर्क्षं सुपलाशमासदन सोमास इन्द्रं मन्दिनश्चमूषदः | परैषामनीकं शवसा दविद्युतद विदत्स्वर्मनवे जयोतिरार्यम ||
10.43.e: As on the fair-leafed tree rest birds, to Indra flow the gladdening Soma juices that the bowls contain.  Their face that glows with splendour through their mighty power hath found the shine of heaven for man, the Āryas' light.

10.43.d: कर्तं न शवघ्नी वि चिनोति देवने संवर्गं यन मघवासूर्यं जयत | न तत ते अन्यो अनु वीर्यं शकन नपुराणो मघवन नोत नूतनः ||
10.43.e: As in the game a gambler piles his winnings, so Maghavan, sweeping all together, gained the Sun  This mighty deed of thine none other could achieve, none, Maghavan, before thee, none in recent time.

10.43.d: विशं-विशं मघवा पर्यशायत जनानां धेनावचाकशद वर्षा | यस्याह शक्रः सवनेषु रण्यति सतीव्रैः सोमैः सहते पर्तन्यतः ||
10.43.e: Maghavan came by turns to all the tribes of men: the Steer took notice of the people's songs of praise.  The man in whose libations Śakra hath delight by means of potent Somas vanquisheth his foes.

10.43.d: आपो न सिन्धुमभि यत समक्षरन सोमास इन्द्रं कुल्यािव हरदम | वर्धन्ति विप्रा महो अस्य सादने यवं नव्र्ष्टिर्दिव्येन दानुना ||
10.43.e: When Soma streams together unto Indra flow like waters to the river, rivulets to the lake,  In place of sacrifice sages exalt his might, as the rain swells the corn by moisture sent from heaven.

10.43.d: वर्षा न करुद्धः पतयद रजस्स्वा यो अर्यपत्नीरक्र्णोदिमा अपः | स सुन्वते मघवा जीरदानवे.अविन्दज्ज्योतिर्मनवे हविष्मते ||
10.43.e: He rushes through the region like a furious Bull, he who hath made these floods the dames of worthy lords.  This Maghavan hath found light for the man who brings oblation, sheds the juice, and promptly pours his gifts.

10.43.d: उज्जायतां परशुर्ज्योतिषा सह भूया रतस्य सुदुघापुराणवत | वि रोचतामरुषो भानुना शुचिः सवर्णशुक्रं शुशुचीत सत्पतिः ||
10.43.e: Let the keen axe come forth together with the light: here be,.as erst, the teeming cow of sacrifice.  Let the Red God shine bright with his refulgent ray, and let the Lord of heroes glow like heaven's clear sheen.
O Much-invoked, may we subdue all famine and evil want with store of grain and cattle.  May we allied, as first in rank, with princes obtain possessions by our own exertion.
Bṛhaspati protect us from the rearward, and from above, and from below, from sinners.  May Indra from the front, and from the centre, as Friend to friends, vouchsafe us room and freedom.

10.44.d: आ यात्विन्द्रः सवपतिर्मदाय यो धर्मणा तूतुजानस्तुविष्मान | परत्वक्षाणो अति विश्वा सहांस्यपारेणमहता वर्ष्ण्येन ||
10.44.e: MAY Sovran Indra come to the carousal, he who by Holy Law is strong and active,  The overcomer of all conquering forces with his great steer-like power that hath no limit.

10.44.d: सुष्ठामा रथः सुयमा हरी ते मिम्यक्ष वज्रो नर्पतेगभस्तौ | शीभं राजन सुपथा याह्यर्वां वर्धामते पपुषो वर्ष्ण्यानि ||
10.44.e: Firm-seated is thy car, thy Steeds are docile; thy hand, O King, holds, firmly grasped, the thunder.  On thy fair path, O Lord of men, come quickly: we will increase thy powers when thou hast drunken.

10.44.d: एन्द्रवाहो नर्पतिं वज्रबाहुमुग्रमुग्रासस्तविषास एनम | परत्वक्षसं वर्षभं सत्यशुष्ममेमस्मत्रा सधमादोवहन्तु ||
10.44.e: Let strong and mighty Steeds who bear this Mighty Indra, the Lord of men, whose arm wields thunder,  Bring unto us, as sharers of our banquet, the Steer of conquering might, of real vigour.

10.44.d: एवा पतिं दरोणसाचं सचेतसमूर्ज सकम्भं धरुणा वर्षायसे | ओजः कर्ष्व सं गर्भाय तवे अप्यसो यथाकेनिपानामिनो वर्धे ||
10.44.e: So like a Bull thou rushest to the Lord who loves the trough, the Sage, the prop of vigour, in the vat,  Prepare thine energies, collect them in thyself: be for our profit as the Master of the wise.

10.44.d: गमन्नस्मे वसून्या हि शंसिषं सवाशिषं भरमायाहि सोमिनः | तवमीशिषे सास्मिन्ना सत्सि बर्हिष्यनाध्र्ष्या तव पात्राणि धर्मणा ||
10.44.e: May precious treasures come to us-so will I pray. Come to the votary's gift offered with beauteous laud.  Thou art the Lord, as such sit on this holy grass: thy vessels are inviolate as Law commands.

10.44.d: पर्थक परायन परथमा देवहूतयो.अक्र्ण्वत शरवस्यानिदुष्टरा | न ये शेकुर्यज्ञियां नावमारुहमीर्मैवते नयविशन्त केपयः ||
10.44.e: Far went our earlist invocation of the Gods, and won us glories that can never be surpassed.  They who could not ascend the ship of sacrifice, sink down in desolation, trembling with alarm.

10.44.d: एवैवापागपरे सन्तु दूढ्यो.अश्वा येषां दुर्युजायुयुज्रे | इत्था ये परागुपरे सन्ति दावने पुरूणियत्र वयुनानि भोजना ||
10.44.e: So be the others, evil-hearted, far away, whose horses, difficult to harness, have been yoked.  Here in advance men stand anear to offer gifts, by whom full many a work that brings reward is done.

10.44.d: गिरीन्रज्रान रेजमानानधारयद दयौः करन्ददन्तरिक्षाणि कोपयत | समीचीने धिषणे वि षकभायतिव्र्ष्णः पीत्वा मद उक्थानि शंसति ||
10.44.e: He firmly fixed the plains and mountains as they shook. Dyaus thundered forth and made the air's mid-region quake.  He stays apart the two confronting bowls; he sings lauds in the potent Soma's joy when he hath drunk.

10.44.d: इमं बिभर्मि सुक्र्तं ते अङकुशं येनारुजासि मघवञ्छफारुजः | अस्मिन सु ते सवने अस्त्वोक्यं सुत इष्टौमघवन बोध्याभगः ||
10.44.e: I bear this deftly-fashioned goad of thine, wherewith thou, Maghavan, shalt break the strikers with the hoof.  At this libation mayst thou be well satisfied. Partake the juice, partake the worship, Maghavan.
O Much-invoked, may we subdue all famine and evil want with store of grain and cattle.  May we allied, as first in rank, with princes obtain possessions by our own exertion.
Bṛhaspati protect us from the rearward, and from above, and from below, from sinners.  May Indra from the front and from the centre, as Friend to friends, vouchsafe us room and freedom.

10.45.d: दिवस परि परथमं जज्ञे अग्निरस्मद दवितीयं परिजातवेदाः | तर्तीयमप्सु नर्मणा अजस्रमिन्धान एनंजरते सवाधीः ||
10.45.e: FIRST Agni sprang to life from out of Heaven: the second time from us came Jātavedas.  Thirdly the Manly-souled was in the waters. The pious lauds and kindles him the Eternal.

10.45.d: विद्मा ते अग्ने तरेधा तरयाणि विद्मा ते धाम विभ्र्तापुरुत्रा | विद्मा ते नाम परमं गुहा यद विद्मा तमुत्सं यत आजगन्थ ||
10.45.e: Agni, we know thy three powers in three stations, we know thy forms in many a place divided.  We know what name supreme thou hast in secret: we know the source from which thou hast proceeded.

10.45.d: समुद्रे तवा नर्मणा अप्स्वन्तर्न्र्चक्षा ईधे दिवो अग्नूधन | तर्तीये तवा रजसि तस्थिवांसमपामुपस्थेमहिषा अवर्धन ||
10.45.e: The Manly-souled lit thee in sea and waters, man's Viewer lit thee in the breast of heaven,  There as thou stoodest in the third high region the Steers increased thee in the water's bosom.

10.45.d: अक्रन्ददग्नि सतनयन्निव दयौः कषामा रेरिहद वीरुधःसमञ्जन | सद्यो जज्ञानो वि हीमिद्धो अख्यदा रोदसीभानुना भात्यन्तः ||
10.45.e: Agni roared out, like Dyaus what time he thunders: he licked the ground about the plants he flickered.  At once, when born, he looked around enkindled, and lightened heaven and earth within with splendour.

10.45.d: शरीणामुदारो धरुणो रयीणां मनीषाणाम्प्रार्पणः सोमगोपाः | वसुः सूनुः सहसो अप्सु राजावि भात्यग्र उषसामिधानः ||
10.45.e: The spring of glories and support of riches, rouser of thoughts and guardian of the Soma,  Good Son of Strength, a King amid the waters, in forefront of the Dawns he shines enkindled.

10.45.d: विश्वस्य केतुर्भुवनस्य गर्भ आ रोदसी अप्र्णाज्जायमानः | वीळुं चिदद्रिमभिनत परायञ जना यदग्निमयजन्त पञ्च ||
10.45.e: Germ of the world, ensign of all creation, be sprang to life and filled the earth and heavens.  Even the firm rock he cleft when passing over, when the Five Tribes brought sacrifice to Agni.

10.45.d: उशिक पावको अरतिः सुमेधा मर्तेष्वग्निरम्र्तो नि धायि | इयर्ति धूममरुषं भरिभ्रदुच्छुक्रेण शोचिषाद्या इनक्षन ||
10.45.e: So among mortals was Immortal Agni stablished as holy wise and willing envoy.  He waves the red smoke that he lifts above him, striving to reach the heavens with radiant lustre.

10.45.d: दर्शानो रुक्म उर्विया वयद्यौद दुर्मर्षमायुः शरियेरुचानः | अग्निरम्र्तो अभवद वयोभिर्यदेनं दयौर्जनयत सुरेताः ||
10.45.e: Like gold to look on, far he shone refulgent, beaming imperishable life for glory,  Agni by vital powers became immortal when his prolific Father Dyaus begat him.

10.45.d: यस्ते अद्य कर्णवद भद्रशोचे.अपूपं देव घर्तवन्तमग्ने | पर तं नय परतरं वस्यो अछाभि सुम्नं देवभक्तंयविष्ठ ||
10.45.e: Whoso this day, O God whose flames are lovely, prepares a cake, O Agni, mixt with butter,  Lead thou and further him to higher fortune, to bliss bestowed by Gods, O thou Most Youthful.

10.45.d: आ तं भज सौश्रवसेष्वग्न उक्थौक्थ आ भज शस्यमाने | परियः सूर्ये परियो अग्ना भवात्युज्जातेन भिनददुज्जनित्वैः ||
10.45.e: Endow him, Agni, with a share of glory, at every song of praise sung forth enrich him.  Dear let him be to Sūrya, dear to Agni, preeminent with son and children's children.

10.45.d: तवामग्ने यजमाना अनु दयून विश्वा वसु दधिरे वार्याणि | तवया सह दरविणमिछमाना वरजं गोमन्तमुशिजो विवव्रुः ||
10.45.e: While, Agni, day by day men pay thee worship they win themselves all treasures worth the wishing.  Allied with thee, eager and craving riches, they have disclosed the stable filled with cattle.

10.45.d: अस्ताव्यग्निर्नरां सुशेवो वैश्वानर रषिभिःसोमगोपाः | अद्वेषे दयावाप्र्थिवी हुवेम देवा धत्त रयिमस्मे सुवीरम ||
10.45.e: Agni, the Friend of men, the Soma's keeper, Vaiśvānara, hath been lauded by the Ṛṣis.  We will invoke benignant Earth and Heaven: ye Deities, give us wealth with hero children.

10.46.d: पर होता जातो महान नभोविन नर्षद्वा सीददपामुपस्थे | दधिर्यो धायि स ते वयांसि यन्ता वसूनि विधतेतनूपाः ||
10.46.e: STABLISHED for thee, to lend thee vital forces, Giver of wealth, Guard of his servant's body.  The Great Priest, born, who knows the clouds, Abider with men, is seated in the lap of waters.

10.46.d: इमं विधन्तो अपां सधस्थे पशुं न नष्टं पदैरनु गमन | गुहा चतन्तमुशिजो नमोभिरिछन्तो धीराभ्र्गवो.अविन्दन ||
10.46.e: Worshipping, seeking him with adoration like some lost creature followed by its footprints,  Wise Bhṛgus, yearning in their hearts, pursued him, and found him lurking where the floods are gathered.

10.46.d: इमं तरितो भूर्यविन्ददिछन वैभूवसो मूर्धन्यघ्न्यायाः | स शेव्र्धो जात आ हर्म्येषु नाभिर्युवाभवति रोचनस्य ||
10.46.e: On the Cow's forehead, with laborious searching, Trita, the offspring of Vibhiavas, found him.  Born in our houses, Youthful, joy-bestower, he now becomes the central point of brightness.

10.46.d: मन्द्रं होतारमुशिजो नमोभिः पराञ्चं यज्ञं नेतारमध्वराणाम | विशामक्र्ण्वन्नरतिं पावकं हव्यवाहन्दधतो मानुषेषु ||
10.46.e: Yearning, with homage, they have set and made him blithe Priest among mankind, oblation-bearer,  Leader of rites and Purifier, envoy of men, as sacrifice that still advances.

10.46.d: पर भूर्जयन्तं महां विपोधां मूरा अमूरं पुरान्दर्माणम | नयन्तो गर्भं वनां धियं धुर्हिरिश्मश्रुं नार्वाणं धनर्चम ||
10.46.e: The foolish brought the ne’er-bewildered forward, great, Victor, Song-inspirer, Fort-destroyer.  Leading the Youth gold-bearded, like a courser gleaming with wealth, they turned their hymn to profit.

10.46.d: नि पस्त्यासु तरित सतभूयन परिवीतो योनौ सीददन्तः | अतः संग्र्भ्या विशां दमूना विधर्मणायन्त्रैरीयतेनॄन ||
10.46.e: Holding his station firmly in the houses, Trita sat down within his home surrounded  Thence, as Law bids, departs the Tribes' Companion having collected men with no compulsion.

10.46.d: अस्याजरासो दमामरित्रा अर्चद्धूमासो अग्नयः पावकाः | शवितीचयः शवात्रासो भुरण्यवो वनर्षदो वायवो नसोमाः ||
10.46.e: His are the fires, eternal, purifying, that make the houses move, whose smoke is shining,  White, waxing in their strength, for ever stirring, and sitting in the wood; like winds are Somas.

10.46.d: पर जिह्वया भरते वेपो अग्निः पर वयुनानि चेतसाप्र्थिव्याः | तमायवः शुचयन्तं पावकं मन्द्रंहोतारं दधिरे यजिष्ठम ||
10.46.e: The tongue of Agni bears away the praisesong, and, through his care for Earth, her operations.  Him, bright and radiant, living men have stablished as their blithe Priest, the Chief of Sacrificers.

10.46.d: दयावा यमग्निं पर्थिवी जनिष्टामापस्त्वष्टा भर्गवोयं सहोभिः | ईळेन्यं परथमं मातरिश्वा देवास्ततक्षुर्मनवे यजत्रम ||
10.46.e: That Agni, him whom Heaven and Earth engendered, the Waters. Tvaṣṭar, and with might, the Bhṛgus,  Him Mātariśvan and the Gods have fashioned holy for man and first to be entreated.

10.46.d: यं तवा देवा दधिरे हव्यवाहं पुरुस्प्र्हो मानुषासोयजत्रम | स यामन्नग्ने सतुवते वयो धाः पर देवयन्यशसः सं हि पूर्वीः ||
10.46.e: Agni, whom Gods have made oblationbearer, and much-desiring men regard as holy,  Give life to him who lauds thee when he worships, and then shall glorious men in troops adore thee.

10.47.d: जग्र्भ्मा ते दक्षिणमिन्द्र हस्तं वसूयवो वसुपतेवसूनाम | विद्मा हि तवा गोपतिं शूर गोनामस्मभ्यंचित्रं वर्षणं रयिं दाः ||
10.47.e: THY right hand have we grasped in ours, O Indra, longing for treasure, Treasure-Lord of treasures!  Because we know thee, Hero, Lord of cattle: vouchsafe us mighty and resplendent riches.

10.47.d: सवायुधं सववसं सुनीथं चतुःसमुद्रं धरुनंरयीणाम | चर्क्र्त्यं शंस्यं भूरिवारमस्मभ्यंचित्रं वर्षणं रयिं दाः ||
10.47.e: Wealth, fully armed, good guard and kind protector, sprung from four seas, the prop and stay of treasures,  Fraught with great bounties, meet for praise and glory; vouchsafe us mighty and resplendent riches.

10.47.d: सुब्रह्माणं देववन्तं बर्हन्तमुरुं गभीरं पर्थुबुध्नमिन्द्र | शरुतर्षिमुग्रमभिमातिषाहमस्मभ्यं चित्रंव्र्षणं रयिं दाः ||
10.47.e: Wealth, with good Brahmans, Indra! God-attended, high, wide, and deep, arid based on broad foundations,  Strong, with famed Ṛṣis, conquering our foemen: vouchsafe us mighty and resplendent riches.

10.47.d: सनद्वाजं विप्रवीरं तरुत्रं धनस्प्र्तं शूशुवांसंसुदक्षम | दस्युहनं पूर्भिदमिन्द्र सत्यमस्मभ्यंचित्रं वर्षणं रयिं दाः ||
10.47.e: Victorious, winning strength, with hero sages, confirmed in power, most useful, wealth-attracting,  True, Indra! crushing forts and slaying Dasyus: vouchsafe us mighty and resplendent riches.

10.47.d: अश्वावन्तं रथिनं वीरवन्तं सहस्रिणं शतिनंवाजमिन्द्र | भद्रव्रातं विप्रवीरं सवर्षामस्मभ्यंचित्रं वर्षणं रयिं दाः ||
10.47.e: Wealthy in heroes and in cars and horses, strength hundredfold and thousandfold, O Indra,  With manly sages, happy troops, Iight-winning: vouchsafe us mighty and resplentdent riches.

10.47.d: पर सप्तगुं रतधीतिं सुमेधां बर्हस्पतिं मतिरछाजिगाति | य आङगिरसो नमसोपसद्यो.अस्मभ्यं चित्रंव्र्षणं रयिं दाः ||
10.47.e: To Saptagu the sage, the holy-minded, to him, Bṛhaspati, the song approaches,  Aṅgiras' Son who must be met with homage: vouchsafe us mighty and reslendent riches.

10.47.d: वनीवानो मम दूतास इन्द्रं सतोमाश्चरन्ति सुमतीरियानाः | हर्दिस्प्र्शो मनसा वच्यमाना अस्मभ्यं चित्रंव्र्षणं रयिं दाः ||
10.47.e: My lauds, like envoys, craving loving-kindness, go forth to Indra with their strong entreaty,  Moving his heart and uttered by my spirit: vouchsafe us mighty and resplendent riches.

10.47.d: यत तवा यामि दद्धि तन न इन्द्र बर्हन्तं कषयमसमंजनानाम | अभि तद दयावाप्र्थिवी गर्णीतामस्मभ्यंचित्रं वर्षणं रयिं दाः ||
10.47.e: Grant us the boon for which I pray, O Indra, a spacious home unmatched among the people.  To this may Heaven and Earth accord approval: vouchsafe us mighty and resplendent riches.

10.48.d: अहं भुवं वसुनः पूर्व्यस पतिरहं धनानि संजयामि शश्वतः | मां हवन्ते पितरं न जन्तवो.अहन्दाशुषे वि भजामि भोजनम ||
10.48.e: I WAS the first possessor of all precious gear: the wealth of every man I win and gather up.  On me as on a Father living creatures call; I deal enjoyment to tho. man who offers gifts.

10.48.d: अहमिन्द्रो रोधो वक्षो अथर्वणस्त्रिताय गा अजनयमहेरधि | अहं दस्युभ्यः परि नर्म्णमा ददे गोत्रा शिक्षन्दधीचे मातरिश्वने ||
10.48.e: I, Indra, am Atharvan's stay and firm support: I brought forth kine to Trita from the Dragon's grasp.  I stripped the Dasyus of their manly might, and gave the cattle-stalls to Matarigvan and Dadhyac.

10.48.d: मह्यं तवष्टा वज्रमतक्षदायसं मयि देवासो.अव्र्जन्नपि करतुम | ममानीकं सूर्यस्येव दुष्टरं मामार्यन्तिक्र्तेन कर्त्वेन च ||
10.48.e: For me hath Tvaṣṭar forged the iron thunderbolt: in me the Gods have centred intellectual power.  My sheen is like the Sun's insufferably bright: men honour me as Lord for past and future deeds.

10.48.d: अहमेतं गव्ययमश्व्यं पशुं पुरीषिणं सायकेनाहिरण्ययम | पुरू सहस्रा नि शिशामि दाशुषे यन मासोमास उक्थिनो अमन्दिषुः ||
10.48.e: I won myself these herdi of cattle, steeds and kine, and gold in ample store, with my destructive bolt.  I give full many a thousand to the worshipper, what time the Somas and the lauds have made me glad.

10.48.d: अहमिन्द्रो न परा जिग्य इद धनं न मर्त्यवे.अव तस्थेकदा चन | सोममिन मा सुन्वन्तो याचता वसु न मेपूरवः सख्ये रिषाथन ||
10.48.e: Indra am I none ever wins my wealth from me never at any time am I a thrall to death.  Pressing the Soma, ask riches from me alone: ye, Pūrus, in my friendship shall not suffer harm.

10.48.d: अहमेताञ्छाश्वसतो दवा-दवेन्द्रं ये वज्रं युधयेऽकर्ण्वत | आह्वयमानानव हन्मनाहनं दर्ळा वदन्ननमस्युर्नमस्विनः ||
10.48.e: These, breathing loud in fury, two and two, who caused Indra to bring his bolt of thunder to the fray,  The challengers, I struck with deadly weapon down: firm stand what words the God speaks to his worshippers.

10.48.d: अभीदमेकमेको अस्मि निष्षाळ अभी दवा किमु तरयःकरन्ति | खले न पर्षान परति हन्मि भूरि किं मा निन्दन्तिशत्रवो.अनिन्द्राः ||
10.48.e: This One by stronger might I conquered singly; yea, also two: shall three prevail against me?  Like many sheaves upon the floor I thrash them. How can my foes, the Indraless, revile me?

10.48.d: अहं गुङगुभ्यो अतिथिग्वमिष्करमिषं न वर्त्रतुरंविक्षु धारयम | यत पर्णयघ्न उत वा करञ्जहे पराहम्महे वर्त्रहत्ये अशुश्रवि ||
10.48.e: Against the Gungus I made Atithigva strong, and kept him mid the folk like Vṛtra-conquering strength,  When I won glory in the great foe-slaying fight, in battle where Karanja fell, and Parṇaya.

10.48.d: पर मे नमी साप्य इषे भुजे भूद गवामेषे सख्याक्र्णुत दविता | दिद्युं यदस्य समिथेषु मंहयमादिदेनं शंस्यमुक्थ्यं करम ||
10.48.e: With food for mine enjoyment Sapya Nami came: he joined me as a friend of old in search of kine.  As I bestowed on him an arrow for the fight I made him worthy of the song apd hymn of praise.

10.48.d: पर नेमस्मिन दद्र्शे सोमो अन्तर्गोपा नेममाविरस्थाक्र्णोति | स तिग्मश्र्ङगं वर्षभं युयुत्सन दरुहस्तस्थौबहुले बद्धो अन्तः ||
10.48.e: One of the two hath Soma, seen within it; the Herdsman with the bone shows forth the other.  He, fain to fight the Bull whose horns were sharpened, stood fettered in the demon's ample region.

10.48.d: आदित्यानां वसूनां रुद्रियाणां देवो देवानां नमिनामि धाम | ते मा भद्राय शवसे ततक्षुरपराजितमस्त्र्तमषाळम ||
10.48.e: I, as a God, ne’er violate the statutes of Gods, of Vasus, Rudriyas, Ādityas.  These Gods have formed me for auspicious vigour, unconquered and invincible for ever.

10.49.d: अहं दां गर्णते पूर्व्यं वस्वहं बरह्म कर्णवं मह्यंवर्धनम | अहं भुवं यजमानस्य चोदितायज्वनः साक्षिविश्वस्मिन भरे ||
10.49.e: I HAVE enriched the singer with surpassing wealth; I have allowed the holy hymn to strengthen me.  I, furtherer of him who offers sacrifice, have conquered in each fight the men who worship not.

10.49.d: मां धुरिन्द्रं नाम देवता दिवश्च गमश्चापां चजन्तवः | अहं हरी वर्षणा विव्रता रघू अहंवज्रं शवसे धर्ष्ण्वा ददे ||
10.49.e: The People of the heavens, the waters, and the earth have stablished me among the Gods with Indra's name.  I took unto myself the two swift vigorous Bays that speed on divers paths, and the fierce bolt for strength.

10.49.d: अहमत्कं कवये शिश्नथं हथैरहं कुत्समावमाभिरूतिभिः | अहं शुष्णस्य शनथिता वधर्यमंन यो रर आर्यं नाम दस्यवे ||
10.49.e: With deadly blows I smote Atka for Kavi's sake; I guarded Kutsa well with these saving helps.  As Śuṣṇa's slayer I brandished the dart of death: I gave not up the Āryan name to Dasyu foes.

10.49.d: अहं पितेव वेतसून्रभिष्टये तुग्रं कुत्साय समदिभंच रन्धयम | अहं भुवं यजमानस्य राजनि पर यद भरेतुजये न परियाध्र्षे ||
10.49.e: Smadibha, Tugra, and the Vetasus I gave as prey to Kutsa, father-like, to succour him.  I was a worthy King to rule the worshipper, when I gave Tuji dear inviolable gifts.

10.49.d: अहं रन्धयं मर्गयं शरुतर्वणे यन माजिहीत वयुनाचनानुषक | अहं वेशं नम्रमायवे.अकरमहंसव्याय पड्ग्र्भिमरन्धयम ||
10.49.e: I gave up Mṛgaya to Srutarvan as his prey because he ever followed me and kept my laws.  For Āyu's sake I caused Veta to bend and bow, and into Savya's hand delivered Padgrbhi.

10.49.d: अहं स यो नववास्त्वं बर्हद्रथं सं वर्त्रेव दासंव्र्त्रहारुजम | यद वर्धयन्तं परथयन्तमानुषग दूरेपारे रजसो रोचनाकरम ||
10.49.e: 1, I crushed Navavāstva of the lofty car, the Dāsa, as the Vṛtra-slayer kills the fiends;  When straightway on the region's farthest edge I brought the God who makes the lights to broaden and increase.

10.49.d: अहं सूर्यस्य परि याम्याशुभिः परैतशेभिर्वहमानोजसा | यन मा सावो मनुष आह निर्णिज रधक कर्षेदासं कर्त्व्यं हथैः ||
10.49.e: I travel round about borne onward in my might by the fleet-footed dappled Horses of the Sun.  When man's libation calls me to the robe of state I soon repel the powerful Dasyu with my blows.

10.49.d: अहं सप्तहा नहुषो नहुष्टरः पराश्राव यं शवसातुर्वशं यदुम | अहं नयन्यं सहसा सहस करं नवव्राधतो नवतिं च वक्षयम ||
10.49.e: Stronger am I than Nabus, I who slew the seven: I glorified with might Yadu and Turvaga.  I brought another low, with strength I bent his strength: I let the mighty nine-and-ninety wax in power.

10.49.d: अहं सप्त सरवतो धारयं वर्षा दरवित्न्वः पर्थिव्यांसीरा अधि | अहमर्णांसि वि तिरामि सुक्रतुर्युधा विदम्मनवे गातुमिष्टये ||
10.49.e: Bull over all the streams that flow along the earth, I took the Seven Rivers as mine own domain.  I, gifted with great wisdom, spread the floods abroad: by war I found for man the way to high success.

10.49.d: अहं तदासु धारयं यदासु न देवश्चनत्वष्टाधारयद रुशत | सपार्हं गवामूधस्सुवक्षणास्वा मधोर्मधु शवात्र्यं सोममाशिरम ||
10.49.e: I set within these cows the white milk which no God, not even Tvaṣṭar's self, had there deposited,—  Much-longed-for, in the breasts, the udders of the kine, the savoury sweets of meath, the milk and Soma juice.

10.49.d: एवा देवानिन्द्रो विव्ये नॄन पर चयौत्नेन मघवासत्यराधाः | विश्वेत ता ते हरिवः शचीवो.अभितुरासः सवयशो गर्णन्ति ||
10.49.e: Even thus hath Indra Maghavan, truly bounteous, sped Gods and men with mighty operation.  The pious glorify all these thine exploits, Lord of Bay Coursers, Strong, and Selfresplendent.

10.50.d: पर वो महे मन्दमानायान्धसो.अर्चा विश्वानरायविश्वाभुवे | इन्द्रस्य यस्य सुमखं सहो महि शरवोन्र्म्णं च रोदसी सपर्यतः ||
10.50.e: I LAUD your Mighty One who joyeth in the juice, him who is shared by all men, who created all;  Indra, whose conquering strength is powerful in war, whose fame and manly vigour Heaven and Earth revere.

10.50.d: सो चिन नु सख्या नर्य इन सतुतश्चर्क्र्त्य इन्द्रो मावतेनरे | विश्वासु धूर्षु वाजक्र्त्येषु सत्पते वर्त्रे वाप्स्वभि शूर मन्दसे ||
10.50.e: He with his friend is active, lauded, good to man, Indra who must be glorified by one like me.  Hero, Lord of the brave, all cars are thy delight, warring with Vṛtra, or for waters, or for spoil.

10.50.d: के ते नर इन्द्र ये त इषे ये ते सुम्नं सधन्यमियक्षान | के ते वाजायासुर्याय हिन्विरे के अप्सु सवासूर्वरासुपौंस्ये ||
10.50.e: Who are the men whom thou wilt further, Indra, who strive to win thy bliss allied with riches?  Who urged thee forward to exert thy power divine, to valour, in the war for waters on their fields?

10.50.d: भुवस्त्वमिन्द्र बरह्मणा महान भुवो विश्वेषु सवनेषुयज्ञियः | भुवो नॄंश्च्यौत्नो विश्वस्मिन भरेज्येष्ठश्च मन्त्रो विश्वचर्षणे ||
10.50.e: Thou, Indra, through the holy prayer art mighty, worthy of sacrifice at all libations.  In every fight thou castest heroes on the ground: thou art the noblest song, O Lord of all the folk.

10.50.d: अवा नु कं जयायान यज्ञवनसो महीं त ओमात्रांक्र्ष्टयो विदुः | असो नु कमजरो वर्धाश्च विश्वेदेतासवना तूतुमा कर्षे ||
10.50.e: Help now, as Highest, those who toil at sacrifice: well do the people know thy great protecting might.  Thou shalt be Everlasing, Giver of success yea, on all these libations thou bestowest strength.

10.50.d: एता विश्वा सवना तूतुमाक्र्षे सवयं सूनो सहसो यानिदधिषे | वराय ते पात्रं धर्मणे तना यज्ञो मन्त्रोब्रह्मोद्यतं वचः ||
10.50.e: All these libations thou makest effectual, of which thou art thyself supporter, Son of Power.  Therefore thy vessel is to be esteemed the best, sacrifice, holy text, prayer, and exalted speech.

10.50.d: ये ते विप्र बरह्मक्र्तः सुते सचा वसूनां च वसुनश्चदावने | पर ते सुम्नस्य मनसा पथा भुवन मदे सुतस्यसोम्यस्यान्धसः ||
10.50.e: They who with flowing Soma pray to thee, O Sage, to pour on them thy gifts of opulence and wealth,  May they come forward, through their spirit, on the path of bliss, in the wild joy of Soma juice effused.

10.51.d: महत तदुल्बं सथविरं तदासीद येनाविष्टितःप्रविवेशिथापः | विश्वा अपश्यद बहुधा ते अग्ने जातवेदस्तन्वो देव एकः ||
10.51.e: LARGE was that covering, and firm of texture, folded wherein thou enteredst the waters.  One Deity alone, O Jātavedas Agni, saw all thy forms in sundry places.

10.51.d: को मा ददर्श कतमः स देवो यो मे तन्वो बहुधापर्यपश्यत | कवाह मित्रावरुणा कषियन्त्यग्नेर्विस्वाःसमिधो देवयानीः ||
10.51.e: What God hath seen me? Who of all their number clearly beheld my forms in many places?  Where lie, then, all the sacred logs of Agni that lead him God-ward, Varuṇa and Mitra?

10.51.d: ऐछाम तवा बहुधा जातवेदः परविष्टमग्ने अप्स्वोषधीषु | तं तवा यमो अचिकेच्चित्रभानो दशान्तरुष्यादतिरोचमानम ||
10.51.e: In many places, Agni Jātavedas, we sought thee hidden in the plants and waters.  Then Yama marked thee, God of wondrous splendour! effulgent from thy tenfold secret dwelling,

10.51.d: होत्रादहं वरुण बिभ्यदायं नेदेव मा युनजन्नत्रदेवाः | तस्य मे तन्वो बहुधा निविष्टा एतमर्थं नचिकेताहमग्निः ||
10.51.e: I fled in fear from sacrificial worship, Varuṇa, lest the Gods should thus engage me.  Thus were my forms laid down in many places. This, as my goal, I Agni saw before me.

10.51.d: एहि मनुर्देवयुर्यज्ञकामो.अरंक्र्त्या तमसि कषेष्यग्ने | सुगान पथः कर्णुहि देवयानान वह हव्यानिसुमनस्यमानः ||
10.51.e: Come; man is pious and would fain do worship, he waits prepared: in gloom thou, Agni, dwellest.  Make pathways leading God-ward clear and easy, and bear oblations with a kindly spirit.

10.51.d: अग्नेः पूर्वे भरातरो अर्थमेतं रथीवाध्वानमन्वावरीवुः | तस्माद भिया वरुण दूरमायं गौरो नक्षेप्नोरविजे जयायाः ||
10.51.e: This goal mine elder brothers erst selected, as he who drives a car the way to travel.  So,Varuṇa, I fled afar through terror, as flies the wild-bull from an archer's bowstring.

10.51.d: कुर्मस्त आयुरजरं यदग्ने यथा युक्तो जातवेदो नरिष्याः | अथा वहासि सुमनस्यमानो भागं देवेभ्योहविषः सुजात ||
10.51.e: We give thee life unwasting, Jātavedas, so that, employed, thou never shalt be injured.  So, nobly born! shalt thou with kindly spirit bear to the Gods their share of men's oblations.

10.51.d: परयाजान मे अनुयाजांश्च केवलानूर्जस्वन्तं हविषोदत्त भागम | घर्तं चापां पुरुषं चौषधीनामग्नेश्च दीर्घमायुरस्तु देवाः ||
10.51.e: Grant me the first oblations and the latter, entire, my forceful shares of holy presents,  The soul of plants, the fatness of the waters, and let there be long life, ye Gods, to Agni.

10.51.d: तव परयाजा अनुयाजाश्च केवल ऊर्जस्वन्तो हविषः सन्तुभागाः | तवाग्ने यज्ञो.अयमस्तु सर्वस्तुभ्यं नमन्ताम्प्रदिशश्चतस्रः ||
10.51.e: Thine be the first oblations and the latter, entire, thy forceful shares of holy presents.  Let all this sacrifice be thine, O Agni, and let the world's four regions how before thee.

10.52.d: विश्वे देवाः शास्तन मा यथेह होता वर्तो मनवै यन्निषद्य | पर मे बरूत भागधेयं यथा वो येन पथाहव्यमा वो वहानि ||
10.52.e: INSTRUCT me, all ye Gods, how I, elected your Priest, must seat me here, and how address you.  Instruct me how to deal to each his portion, and by what ' path to bring you man's oblation.

10.52.d: अहं होता नयसीदं यजीयान विश्वे देवा मरुतो माजुनन्ति | अहर-अहरश्विनाध्वर्यवं वां बरह्मा समिद भवतिसाहुतिर्वाम ||
10.52.e: I sit as Priest most skilled in sacrificing: the Maruts and all Deities impel me.  Aśvins, each day yours is the Adhvaryu's duty: Brahman and wood are here: ’tis yours to offer.

10.52.d: अयं यो होता किरु स यमस्य कमप्यूहे यत समञ्जन्तिदेवाः | अहर-अहर्जायते मासि-मास्यथा देवा दधिरेहव्यवाहम ||
10.52.e: Who is the Priest? Is he the Priest of Yama? On whom is thrust this God-appointed honour?  He springs to life each month, each day that passes; so Gods have made him their oblation-bearer.

10.52.d: मां देवा दधिरे हव्यवाहमपम्लुक्तं बहु कर्छ्राचरन्तम | अग्निर्विद्वान यज्ञं नः कल्पयाति पञ्चयामन्त्रिव्र्तं सप्ततन्तुम ||
10.52.e: The Gods have made me bearer of oblations, who slipped away and passed through many troubles.  Wise Agni shall ordain for us the worship, whether five-wayed, threefold, or seven-threaded.

10.52.d: आ वो यक्ष्यम्र्तत्वं सुवीरं यथा वो देवा वरिवःकराणि | आ बाह्वोर्वज्रमिन्द्रस्य धेयामथेमाविश्वाः पर्तना जयाति ||
10.52.e: So will I win you strength and life for ever. O Gods, that I may give you room and freedom.  To Indra's arms would I consign the thunder; in all these battles shall he then be victor.

10.52.d: तरीणि शता तरी सहस्राण्यग्निं तरिंशच्च देवा नवचासपर्यन | औक्षन घर्तैरस्त्र्णन बर्हिरस्मा आदिद्धोतारं नयसादयन्त ||
10.52.e: The Deities three hundred and thirty-nine, have served and honoured Agni,  Strewn sacred grass, anointed him with butter, and seated him as Priest, the Gods’ Invoker.

10.53.d: यमैछाम मनसा सो.अयमागाद यज्ञस्य विद्वान्परुषश्चिकित्वान | स नो यक्षद देवताता यजीयान नि हिषत्सदन्तरः पूर्वो अस्मत ||
10.53.e: HE hath arrived, he whom we sought with longing, who skilled in sacrifice well knows its courses.  Let him discharge his sacrificial duties: let him sit down as Friend who was before  Us.

10.53.d: अराधि होता निषदा यजीयनभि परयांसि सुधितानि हिख्यत | यजामहै यज्ञियान हन्त देवानीळामहाीड्यानाज्येन ||
10.53.e: Best Priest, he hath been won by being seated, for he hath looked on the well-ordered viands.  Come, let usworship Gods who must be worshipped, and pouring oil, laud those who should be lauded.

10.53.d: साध्वीमकर्देववीतिं नो अद्य यज्ञस्य जिह्वामविदामगुह्याम | स आयुरागात सुरभिर्वसानो भद्रामकर्देवहूतिं नो अद्य ||
10.53.e: Now hath he made the feast of Gods effective: now have we found the secret tongue of worship.  Now hath he come, sweet, robed in vital vigour, and made our calling on the Gods effective.

10.53.d: तदद्य वाचः परथमं मसीय येनासुरानभि देवासाम | ऊर्जाद उत यज्ञियसः पञ्च जना मम होत्रंजुषध्वम ||
10.53.e: This prelude of my speech I now will utter, whereby we Gods may quell our Asura foemen.  Eaters of strengthening food who merit worship, O ye Five Tribes, be pleased with mine oblation.

10.53.d: पञ्च जना मम होत्रं जुषन्तां गोजाता उत येयज्ञियासः | पर्थिवी नः पार्थिवात पात्वंअसोऽनतरिक्षं दिव्यात पात्वस्मान ||
10.53.e: May the Five Tribes be pleased with mine oblation, and the Cow's Sons and all who merit worship.  From earthly trouble may the earth protect us, and air's mid realm from woe that comes from heaven.

10.53.d: तन्तुं तन्वन रजसो भानुमन्विहि जयोतिष्मतः पथोरक्ष धिया कर्तान | अनुल्बणं वयत जोगुवामपो मनुर्भव जनया दैव्यं जनम ||
10.53.e: Spinning the thread, follow the region's splendid light: guard thou the path ways well which wisdom hath prepared.  Weave ye the knotless labour of the bards who sing: be Manu thou, and bring the Heavenly People forth.

10.53.d: अक्षानहो नह्यतनोत सोम्या इष्क्र्णुध्वं रशना ओतपिंशत | अष्टावन्धुरं वहताभितो रथं येन देवासोनयन्नभि परियम ||
10.53.e: Lovers of Soma, bind the chariot traces fast: set ye the reins in order and embellish them.  Bring hitherward the car with seats where eight may sit, whereon the Gods have brought the treasure that we love.

10.53.d: अश्मन्वती रीयते सं रभध्वमुत तिष्ठत पर तरतासखायः | अत्रा जहाम ये असन्नशेवाः शिवान वयमुत्तरेमाभि वाजान ||
10.53.e: Here flows Asmanvati: hold fast each other, keep yourselves up, and pass, my friends, the river.  There let us leave the Powers that brought no profit, and cross the flood to Powers that are auspicious.

10.53.d: तवष्टा माया वेदपसामपस्तमो बिभ्रत पात्रादेवपानानि शन्तमा | शिशीते नूनं परशुं सवायसंयेन वर्श्चादेतशो बरह्मणस पतिः ||
10.53.e: Tvaṣṭar, most deft of workmen, knew each magic art, bringing most blessed bowls that hold the drink of Gods.  His axe, wrought of good metal, he is sharpening now, wherewith the radiant Brahmaṇaspati will cut.

10.53.d: सतो नूनं कवयः सं शिशीत वाशीभिर्याभिरम्र्ताय तक्षथ | विद्वांसः पदा गुह्यानि कर्तन येनदेवासो अम्र्तत्वमानशुः ||
10.53.e: Now, O ye Sapient Ones, make ye the axes sharp wherewith ye fashion bowls to hold the Amṛta.  Knowing the secret places make ye ready that whereby the Gods have gotten immortality.

10.53.d: गर्भे योषामदधुर्वत्समासन्यपीच्येन मनसोतजिह्वया | स विश्वाहा सुमना योग्या अभि सिषासनिर्वनतेकार इज्जितिम ||
10.53.e: Ye with a secret tongue and dark intention laid the maiden deep within, the calf within the mouth.  They evermore are near us with their gracious help: successful is the song that strives for victory.

10.54.d: तां सु ते कीर्तिं मघवन महित्वा यत तवा भीते रोदसीह्वयेताम | परावो देवानातिरो दासमोजः परजायैत्वस्यै यदशिक्ष इन्द्र ||
10.54.e: I SING thy fame that, Maghavan, through thy Greatness the heavens and earth invoked thee in their terror,  Thou, aiding Gods, didst quell the power of Dāsas, what time thou holpest many a race, O Indra.

10.54.d: यदचरस्तन्वा वाव्र्धानो बलानीन्द्र परब्रुवाणो जनेषु | मायेत सा ते यानि युद्धान्याहुर्नाद्य शत्रुं ननुपुरा विवित्से ||
10.54.e: When thou wast roaming, waxen strong in body, telling thy might, Indra, among the people,  All that men called thy battles was illusion: no foe hast thou to-day, nor erst hast found one.

10.54.d: क उ नु ते महिमनः समस्यास्मत पूर्व रषयो.अन्तमापुः | यन मातरं च पितरं च साकमजनयथास्तन्वःस्वायाः ||
10.54.e: Who are the Ṛṣis, then, who comprehended before our time the bounds of all thy greatness?  For from thy body thou hast generated at the same time the Mother and the Father.

10.54.d: चत्वारि ते असुर्याणि नामादाभ्यानि महिषस्य सन्ति | तवमङग तानि विश्वानि वित्से येभिः कर्माणि मघवञ्चकर्थ ||
10.54.e: Thou, Mighty Steer, hast four supremest natures, Asura natures that may ne’er be injured.  All these, O Maghavan, thou surely knowest, wherewith thou hast performed thy great achievements.

10.54.d: तवं विश्वा दधिषे केवलानि यान्याविर्या च गुहावसूनि | काममिन मे मघवन मा वि तारीस्त्वमाज्ञातात्वमिन्द्रासि दाता ||
10.54.e: Thou hast all treasures in thy sole possession, treasures made manifest and treasures hidden.  Defer not thou, O Maghavan, my longing: thou, art Director, Indra, thou art Giver.

10.54.d: यो अदधाज्ज्योतिषि जयोतिरन्तर्यो अस्र्जन मधुना सम्मधूनि | अध परियं शूषमिन्द्राय मन्म बरह्मक्र्तोब्र्हदुक्थादवाचि ||
10.54.e: To him who set the light in things of splendour, and with all sweetness blent essential sweetness,  To Indra hath this welcome hymn that strengthens been uttered by the votary Bṛhaduktha.

10.55.d: दूरे तन नाम गुह्यं पराचैर्यत तवा भीते अह्वयेतांवयोधै | उदस्तभ्नाः पर्थिवीं दयामभीके भरातुःपुत्रान मघवन तित्विषाणः ||
10.55.e: FAR is that secret name by which, in terror, the worlds invoked thee and thou gavest vigour  The earth and heaven thou settest near each other, and Maghavan, madest bright thy Brother's Children.

10.55.d: महत तन नाम गुह्यं पुरुस्प्र्ग येन भूतं जनयो येनभव्यम | परत्नं जातं जयोतिर्यदस्य परियं परियाः समविशन्त पञ्च ||
10.55.e: Great is that secret name and far-extending, whereby thou madest all that is and shall be.  The Five Tribes whom he loveth well have entered the light he loveth that was made aforetime.

10.55.d: आ रोदसी अप्र्णादोत मध्यं पञ्च देवान रतुशः सप्त सप्त | चतुस्त्रिंशता पुरुधा वि चष्टे सरूपेण जयोतिषाविव्रतेन ||
10.55.e: He filled the heaven and earth and all between them, Gods five times sevenfold in their proper seasons.  With four-and-thirty lights he looks around him, lights of one colour though their ways are divers.

10.55.d: यदुष औछः परथमा विभानामजनयो येन पुष्टस्यपुष्टम | यत ते जामित्वमवरं परस्या महन महत्यासुरत्वमेकम ||
10.55.e: As first among the lights, O Dawn, thou shonest, whereby thou broughtest forth the Stay of Increase,  Great art thou, matchless is thine Asura nature, who, high above, art kin to those beneath thee.

10.55.d: विधुं दद्राणं समने बहूनां युवानं सन्तं पलितोजगार | देवस्य पश्य काव्यं महित्वाद्या ममार स हयःसमान ||
10.55.e: The old hath waked the young Moon from his slumber who runs his circling course with many round him.  Behold the Gods’ high wisdom in its greatness: he who died yesterday to-day is living.

10.55.d: शाक्मना शाको अरुणः सुपर्ण आ यो महः शूरःसनादनीळः | यच्चिकेत सत्यमित तन न मोघं वसुस्पार्हमुत जेतोत दाता ||
10.55.e: Strong is the Red Bird in his strength, great Hero, who from of old hath had no nest to dwell in.  That which he knows is truth and never idle: he wins and gives the wealth desired of many.

10.55.d: ऐभिर्ददे वर्ष्ण्या पौंस्यानि येभिरौक्षद वर्त्रहत्यायवज्री | ये कर्मणः करियमाणस्य मह्न रतेकर्ममुदजायन्त देवाः ||
10.55.e: Through these the Thunderer gained strong manly vigour, through whom he waxed in power to smite down Vṛtra,—  Who through the might of Indra's operation came forth as Gods in course of Law and Order.

10.55.d: युजा कर्माणि जनयन विश्वौजा अशस्तिथा विश्वमनास्तुराषाट | पीत्वी सोमस्य दिव आ वर्धानः शूरो निर्युधाधमद दस्यून ||
10.55.e: All-strong, performing works with his companion, All-marking, rapid Victor, Curse-averter,  The Hero, waxing, after draughts of Soma, blew far from heaven the Dasyus with his weapon.

10.56.d: इदं त एकं पर ऊ त एकं तर्तीयेन जयोतिषा संविशस्व | संवेशने तन्वश्चारुरेधि परियो देवानाम्परमे जनित्रे ||
10.56.e: HERE is one light for thee, another yonder: enter the third and he therewith united.  Uniting with a body be thou welcome, dear to the Gods in their sublimest birthplace.

10.56.d: तनूष टे वाजिन तन्वं नयन्ती वाममस्मभ्यं धातुशर्म तुभ्यम | अह्रुतो महो धरुणाय देवान दिवीवज्योतिः सवमा मिमीयाः ||
10.56.e: Bearing thy body, Vajin, may thy body afford us blessing and thyself protection.  Unswerving, stablish as it were in heaven thine own light as the mighty God's supporter.

10.56.d: वाज्यसि वाजिनेना सुवेनीः सुवित सतोमं सुवितो दिवंगाः | सुवितो धर्म परथमानु सत्या सुवितो देवान सुवितोऽनु पत्म ||
10.56.e: Strong Steed art thou: go to the yearning Maidens with vigour, happily go to heaven and praises:  Fly happily to the Gods with easy passage, according to the first and faithful statutes.

10.56.d: महिम्न एषां पितरश्चनेशिरे देवा देवेष्वदधुरपिक्रतुम | समविव्यचुरुत यान्यत्विषुरैषां तनूषु निविविशुः पुनः ||
10.56.e: Part of their grandeur have the Fathers also gained: the Gods have seated mental power in them as Gods.  They have embraced within themselves all energies, which, issuing forth, again into their bodies pass.

10.56.d: सहोभिर्विश्वं परि चक्रमू रजः पूर्वा धामान्यमितामिमानाः | तनूषु विश्वा भुवना नि येमिरे परासारयन्तपुरुध परजा अनु ||
10.56.e: They strode through all the region with victorious might, establishing the old immeasurable laws.  They compassed in their bodies all existing things, and streamed forth offipring in many successive forms.

10.56.d: दविधा सूनवो.असुरं सवर्विदमास्थापयन्त तर्तीयेनकर्मणा | सवां परजां पितरः पित्र्यं सह आवरेष्वदधुस्तन्तुमाततम ||
10.56.e: In two ways have the sons established in his place the Asura who finds the light, by the third act,  As fathers, they have set their heritage on earth, their offspring, as a thread continuously spun out.

10.56.d: नावा न कषोदः परदिशः पर्थिव्याः सवस्तिभिरतिदुर्गाणि विश्वा | सवां परजां बर्हदुक्थो महित्वावरेष्वदधादा परेषु ||
10.56.e: As in a ship through billows, so through regions of air, with blessings, through toils and troubles  Hath Bṛhaduktha brought his seed with glory, and placed it here and in the realms beyond us.

10.57.d: मा पर गाम पथो वयं मा यज्ञादिन्द्र सोमिनः | मान्त सथुर्नो अरातयः ||
10.57.e: LET us not, Indra, leave the path, the Soma-presser's sacrifice:  Let no malignity dwell with us.
May we obtain, completely wrought, the thread spun out to reach the Gods,  That perfecteth the sacrifice.

10.57.d: मनो नवा हुवामहे नाराशंसेन सोमेन | पितॄणां चमन्मभिः ||
10.57.e: We call the spirit hither with the Soma of our parted sires,  Yea, with the Fathers' holy hymns.

10.57.d: आ त एतु मनः पुनः करत्वे दक्षाय जीवसे | जयोक चसूर्यं दर्शे ||
10.57.e: Thy spirit come to thee again for wisdom, energy, and lire,  That thou mayst long behold the sun!

10.57.d: पुनर्नः पितरो मनो ददातु दैव्यो जनः | जीवं वरातंसचेमहि ||
10.57.e: O Fathers, may the Heavenly Folk give us our spirit once again,  That we may be with those who live.

10.57.d: वयं सोम वरते तव मनस्तनूषु बिभ्रतः | परजावन्तः सचेमहि ||
10.57.e: O Soma with the spirit still within us, blest with progeny,  May we be busied in the law.

10.58.d: यत ते यमं वैवस्वतं मनो जगाम दूरकम | तत त आवर्तयामसीह कषयाय जीवसे ||
10.58.e: THY spirit, that went far away to Yama to Vivasvān's Son,  We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.

10.58.d: यत ते दिवं यत पर्थिवीं मनो जगाम दूरकम | तत त ... ||
10.58.e: Thy spirit, that went far away, that passed away to earth and heaven,  We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.

10.58.d: यत ते भूमिं चतुर्भ्र्ष्टिं मनो जगाम दूरकम | तत त... ||
10.58.e: Thy spirit, that went far away, away to the four-cornered earth,  We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.

10.58.d: यत ते चतस्रः परदिशो मनो जगाम दूरकम | तत त ... ||
10.58.e: Thy spirit, that went far away to the four quarters of the world,  We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.

10.58.d: यत ते समुद्रमर्णवं मनो जगाम दूरकम | तत त ... ||
10.58.e: Thy spirit, that went far away, away unto the billowy sea,  We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.

10.58.d: यत ते मरीचीः परवतो मनो जगाम दूरकम | तत त ... ||
10.58.e: Thy spirit, that went far away to beams of light that flash and flow,  We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.

10.58.d: यत ते अपो यदोषधीर्मनो जगाम दूरकम | तत त ... ||
10.58.e: Thy spirit, that went far away, went to the waters and the plants,  We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.

10.58.d: यत ते सूर्यं यदुषसं मनो जगाम दूरकम | तत त ... ||
10.58.e: Thy spirit, that went far away, that visited the Sun and Dawn.  We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.

10.58.d: यत ते पर्वतान बर्हतो मनो जगाम दूरकम | तत त ... ||
10.58.e: Thy spirit, that went far away, away to lofty mountain heights,  We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.

10.58.d: यत ते विश्वमिदं जगन मनो जगाम दूरकम | तत त ... ||
10.58.e: Thy spirit, that went far away into this All, that lives and moves,  We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.

10.58.d: यत ते पराः परावतो मनो जगाम दूरकम | तत त ... ||
10.58.e: Thy spirit, that went far away to distant realms beyond our ken,  We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn here.

10.58.d: यत ते भूतं च भव्यं च मनो जगाम दूरकम | तत त... ||
10.58.e: Thy spirit, that went far away to all that is and is to be,  We cause to come to thee again that thou mayst live and sojourn heie.

10.59.d: पर तार्यायुः परतरं नवीय सथातारेव करतुमतारथस्य | अध चयवान उत तवीत्यर्थं परातरं सग़्म ||
10.59.e: His life hath been renewed and carried forward as two men, car-borne, by the skilful driver.  One falls, then seeks the goal with quickened vigour. Let Nirrti depart to distant places.

10.59.d: सामन नु राये निधिमन नवन्नं करामहे सु पुरुधश्रवांसि | ता नो विश्वानि जरिता ममत्तु परातरं सुनिरतिर्जिहीताम ||
10.59.e: Here is the psalm for wealth, and food, in plenty: let us do many deeds to bring us glory.  All these our doings shall delight the singer. Let Nirrti depart to distant places.

10.59.d: अभी षवर्यः पौंस्यैर्भवेम दयौर्न भूमिं गिरयोनाज्रन | ता नो विश्वानि जरिता चिकेत परातरं सुनिरतिर्जिहीताम ||
10.59.e: May we o’ercome our foes with acts of valour, as heaven is over earth, hills over lowlands.  All these our deeds the singer hath considered. Let Nirrti depart to distant places.

10.59.d: मो षु णः सोम मर्त्यवे परा दाः पश्येम नु सूर्यमुच्चरन्तम | दयुभिर्हितो जरिमा सू नो अस्तु परातरं सुनिरतिर्जिहीताम ||
10.59.e: Give us not up as prey to death, O Soma still let us look upon the Sun arising.  Let our old age with passing days be kindly. Let Nirrti depart to distant places.

10.59.d: असुनीते मनो अस्मासु धारय जीवातवे सु पर तिरा नायुः | रारन्धि नः सूर्यस्य सन्द्र्शि घर्तेन तवन्तन्वं वर्धयस्व ||
10.59.e: O Asuniti, keep the soul within us, and make the days we have to live yet longer.  Grant that we still may look upon the sunlight: strengthen thy body with the oil we bring thee.

10.59.d: असुनीते पुनरस्मासु चक्षुः पुनः पराणमिह नो धेहिभोगम | जयोक पश्येम सूर्यमुच्चरन्तमनुमते मर्ळया नह्स्वस्ति ||
10.59.e: Give us our sight again, O Asuniti, give us again our breath and our enjoyment.  Long may we look upon the Sun uprising; O Anumati, favour thou and bless us.

10.59.d: पुनर्नो असुं पर्थिवी ददातु पुनर्द्यौर्देवी पुनरन्तरिक्षम | पुनर्नः सोमस्तन्वं ददातु पुनः पूषापथ्यां या सवस्तिः ||
10.59.e: May Earth restore to us our vital spirit, may Heaven the Goddess and mid-air restore it.  May Soma give us once again our body, and Pūṣan show the Path of peace and comfort.

10.59.d: शं रोदसी सुबन्धवे यह्वी रतस्य मातरा | भरतामप यद रपो दयौः पर्थिवि कषमा रपो मो षु ते किंचनाममत ||
10.59.e: May both Worlds bless Subandhu, young Mothers of everlasting Law.  May Heaven and Earth uproot and sweep iniquity and shame away: nor sin nor sorrow trouble thee.

10.59.d: अव दवके अव तरिका दिवश्चरन्ति भेषजा | कषमाचरिष्ण्वेककं भरतामप यद रपो दयौः पर्थिवि कषमारपो मो षु ते किं चनाममत ||
10.59.e: Health-giving medicines descend sent down from heaven in twos and threes,  Or wandering singly on the earth. May Heaven and Earth uproot and sweep iniquity and shame away: nor sin nor sorrow trouble thee.

10.59.d: समिन्द्रेरय गामनड्वाहं य आवहदुशीनराण्यानः | भरतामप यद रपो दयौः पर्थिवि कषमा रपो मोषु ते किं चनाममत ||
10.59.e: Drive forward thou the wagon-ox, O Indra, which brought Usinarani's wagon hither.  May Heaven and Earth uproot and sweep iniquity and shame away: nor sin nor sorrow trouble thee.

10.60.d: आ जनं तवेषसन्द्र्शं माहीनानामुपस्तुतम | अगन्मबिभ्रतो नमः ||
10.60.e: BRINGING our homage we have come to one magnificent in look.  Glorified of the mighty Gods

10.60.d: असमातिं नितोशनं तवेषं निययिनं रथम | भजेरथस्य सत्पतिम ||
10.60.e: To Asamati, spring of gifts, lord of the brave, a radiant car,  The conqueror of Bhajeratha
Who, when the spear hath armed his hand, or even weaponless o’erthrows  Men strong as buffaloes in fight;

10.60.d: यस्येक्ष्वाकुरुप वरते रेवान मराय्येधते | दिवीवपञ्च कर्ष्टयः ||
10.60.e: Him in whose service flourishes Iksvaku, rich and dazzling-bright.  As the Five Tribes that are in heaven.

10.60.d: इन्द्र कषत्रासमातिषु रथप्रोष्ठेषु धारय | दिवीवसूर्यं दर्शे ||
10.60.e: Indra, support the princely power of Rathaprosthas matched by none,  Even as the Sun for all to see.

10.60.d: अगस्त्यस्य नद्भ्यः सप्ती युनक्षि रोहिता | पणीन नयक्रमीरभि विश्वान राजन्नराधसः ||
10.60.e: Thou for Agastya's sister's sons yokest thy pair of ruddy steeds.  Thou troddest niggards under foot, all those, O King, who brought no gifts.

10.60.d: अयं मातायं पितायं जीवातुरागमत | इदं तवप्रसर्पणं सुबन्धवेहि निरिहि ||
10.60.e: This is the mother, this the sire, this one hath come to be thy life.  What brings thee forth is even this. Now come, Subandhu, get thee forth.

10.60.d: यथा युगं वरत्रया नह्यन्ति धरुणाय कम | एवादाधार ते मनो जीवातवे न मर्त्यवे.अथो अरिष्टतातये ||
10.60.e: As with the leather thong they bind the chariot yoke to hold it fast,  So have I held thy spirit fast, held it for life and not for death, held it for thy security.

10.60.d: यथेयं पर्थिवी मही दाधारेमान वनस्पतीन | एवादाधार ते मनो जीवातवे न मर्त्यवे.अथो अरिष्टतातये ||
10.60.e: Even as this earth, the mighty earth, holds fast the monarchs of the wood.  So have I held thy spirit fast, held it for life and not for death, held it for thy security.

10.60.d: यमादहं वैवस्वतात सुबन्धोर्मन आभरम | जीवातवेन मर्त्यवे.अथो अरिष्टतातये ||
10.60.e: Subandlin's spirit I have brought from Yarna, from Vivasvān's Son,  Brought it for life and not for death, yea, brought it for security.

10.60.d: नयग वातो.अव वाति नयक तपति सूर्यः | नीचीनमघ्न्यादुहे नयग भवतु ते रपः ||
10.60.e: The wind blows downward from on high, downward the Sun-God sends his heat,  Downward the milch-cow pours her milk: so downward go thy pain and grief.

10.60.d: अयं मे हस्तो भगवानयं मे भगवत्तरः | अयं मेविश्वभेषजो.अयं शिवाभिमर्शनः ||
10.60.e: Felicitous is this mine hand, yet more felicitous is this.  This hand contains all healing balms, and this makes whole with gentle touch.

10.61.d: इदमित्था रौद्रं गूर्तवचा बरह्म करत्वा शच्यामन्तराजौ | कराणा यदस्य पितरा मंहनेष्ठाः पर्षत्पक्थे अहन्ना सप्त होतॄन ||
10.61.e: THE welcome speaker in the storm of battle uttered with might this prayer to win the Aśvins,  When the most liberal God, for Paktha, rescued his parents, and assailed the seven Hotras.

10.61.d: स इद दानाय दभ्याय वन्वञ्च्यवानः सूदैरमिमीतवेदिम | तूर्वयाणो गूर्तवचस्तमः कषोदो न रेत इतूतिसिञ्चत ||
10.61.e: Cyavāna, purposing deceptive presents, with all ingredients, made the altar ready.  Most sweet-voiced Tūrvayāṇa poured oblations like floods of widely fertilizing water.

10.61.d: मनो न येषु हवनेषु तिग्मं विपः शच्या वनुथोद्रवन्ता | आ यः शर्यभिस्तुविन्र्म्णोस्याश्रीणीतादिशं गभस्तौ ||
10.61.e: To his oblations, swift as thought, ye hurried, and welcomed eagerly the prayers he offered.  With arrows in his hand the Very Mighty forced from him all obedience of a servant.

10.61.d: कर्ष्णा यद गोष्वरुणीषु सीदद दिवो नपाताश्विनाहुवे वाम | वीतं मे यज्ञमा गतं मे अन्नं ववन्वांसानेषमस्म्र्तध्रू ||
10.61.e: I call on you the Sons of Dyaus, the Aśvins, that a dark cow to my red kine be added.  Enjoy my sacrifice, come to my viands contented, not deceiving expectation. '

10.61.d: परथिष्ट यस्य वीरकर्ममिष्णदनुष्ठितं नु नर्योपौहत | पुनस्तदा वर्हति यत कनाया दुहितुरानुभ्र्तमनर्वा ||
10.61.e: Membrum suum virile, quod vrotentum fuerat, mas ille retraxit. Rursus illud quod in juvenem filiam sublatum fuerat, non aggressurus, ad se rerahit.

10.61.d: मध्या यत कर्त्वमभवदभीके कामं कर्ण्वाणेपितरि युवत्याम | मनानग रेतो जहतुर्वियन्ता सानौनिषिक्तं सुक्र्तस्य योनौ ||
10.61.e: Quum jam in medio connessu, semiperfecto opere, amorem in puellam pater impleverat, ambo discedentes seminis paulum in terrae superficiem sacrorum sede effusum emiserunt.

10.61.d: पिता यत सवां दुहितरमधिष्कन कष्मया रेतःसंजग्मानो नि षिञ्चत | सवाध्यो.अजनयन बरह्म देवावास्तोष पतिं वरतपां निरतक्षन ||
10.61.e: Quum pater suam nilam adiverat, cum eā congressus suum semen supra  viram  effudit. Tum Dii benigni precem (brahma)  progenuerunt  , et Vastoshpatim, legum sacrarum custodem, formaverunt.

10.61.d: स ईं वर्षा न फेनमस्यदाजौ समदा परैदपदभ्रचेताः | सरत पदा न दक्षिणा पराव्रं न ता नुमे पर्शन्यो जग्र्भ्रे ||
10.61.e: Ille tauro similis spumam in certamine jactavit, tunc discedens pusillaximis huc profectus est. Quasi dextro pede claudus processit, "inutiles fuerunt illi mei complexus," ita locutus.

10.61.d: मक्षू न वह्निः परजाया उपब्दिरग्निं न नग्न उपसीददूधः | सनितेध्मं सनितोत वाजं स धर्ताजज्ञे सहसा यवीयुत ||
10.61.e: 'The fire, burning the people, does not approach quickly (by day): the naked (  Rākṣasas  approach) not Agni by night; the giver of fuel, and the giver of food, he, the upholder (of the rite), is born, overcoming enemies by his might.'

10.61.d: मक्षू कनायाः सख्यं नवग्वा रतं वदन्त रतयुक्तिमग्मन | दविबर्हसो य उप गोपमागुरदक्षिणासो अच्युतादुदुक्षन ||
10.61.e: Uttering praise to suit the rite Navagvas came speedily to win the damsel's friendship.  They who approached the twice-strong stable's keeper, meedless would milk the rocks that naught had shaken.

10.61.d: मक्षू कनायाः सख्यं नवीयो राधो न रेत रतमित्तुरण्यन | शुचि यत ते रेक्ण आयजन्त सबर्दुघायाः पयौस्रियायाः ||
10.61.e: Swift was new friendship with the maid they quickly accepted it as genuine seed and bounty.  Milk which the cow Sabardughā had yielded was the bright heritage which to thee they offered.

10.61.d: पश्वा यत पश्चा वियुता बुधन्तेति बरवीति वक्तरीरराणः | वसोर्वसुत्वा कारवो.अनेहा विश्वं विवेष्टिद्रविणमुप कषु ||
10.61.e: When afterwards they woke and missed the cattle, the speaker thus in joyful mood addressed them:  Matchless are singers through the Vasu's nature; he bringeth them all food and all possessions.

10.61.d: तदिन नवस्य परिषद्वानो अग्मन पुरू सदन्तो नार्षदम्बिभित्सन | वि शुष्णस्य संग्रथितमनर्वा विदत्पुरुप्रजातस्य गुहा यत ||
10.61.e: His followers then who dwelt in sundry places came and desired too slay the son of Nṛṣad.  Resistless foe, be found the hidden treasure of Śuṣṇa multiplied in numerous offspring.

10.61.d: भर्गो ह नामोत यस्य देवाः सवर्ण ये तरिषधस्थेनिषेदुः | अग्निर्ह नामोत जातवेदाः शरुधी नो होतरतस्य होताध्रुक ||
10.61.e: Thou, called Effulgence, in whose threefold dwelling, as in the light of heaven, the Gods are sitting,  Thou who art called Agni or Jātavedas, Priest, hear us, guileless Priest of holy worship.

10.61.d: उत तया मे रौद्रावर्चिमन्ता नासत्याविन्द्र गूर्तयेयजध्यै | मनुष्वद वर्क्तबर्हिषे रराणा मन्दूहितप्रयसा विक्षु यज्यू ||
10.61.e: And, Indra, bring, that I may laud and serve them, those Two resplendent glorious Nāsatyas,  Blithe, bounteous, man-like, to the sacrificer, honoured among our men with offered viands.

10.61.d: अयं सतुतो राजा वन्दि वेधा अपश व विप्रस्तरतिस्वसेतुः | स कक्षीवन्तं रेजयत सो अग्निं नेमिं नचक्रमर्वतो रघुद्रु ||
10.61.e: This King is praised and honoured as Ordainer: himself the bridge, the Sage speeds o’er the waters.  He hath stirred up Kakṣīvān, stirred up Agni, as the steed's swift wheel drives the felly onward.

10.61.d: स दविबन्धुर्वैतरणो यष्टा सबर्धुं धेनुमस्वन्दुहध्यै | सं यन मित्रावरुणा वर्ञ्ज उक्थैर्ज्येष्ठेभिरर्यमणं वरूथैः ||
10.61.e: Vaitarana, doubly kinsman, sacrificer, shall milk the cow who ne’er hath calved, Sabardhu,  When I encompass Varuṇa and Mitra with lauds, and Aryaman in safest shelter.

10.61.d: तद्बन्धुः सूरिर्दिवि ते धियन्धा नाभानेदिष्ठो रपतिप्र वेनन | सा नो नाभिः परमास्य वा घाहं तत्पश्चा कतिथश्चिदास ||
10.61.e: Their kin, the Prince in heaven, thy nearest kinsman, turning his thought to thee thus speaks in kindness:  This is our highest bond: I am his offspring. How many others came ere I succeeded?

10.61.d: इयं मे नाभिरिह मे सधस्थमिमे मे देवा अयमस्मिसर्वः | दविजा अह परथमजा रतस्येदं धेनुरदुहज्जायमाना ||
10.61.e: Here is my kinship, here the place I dwell in: these are my Gods; I in full strength am present.  Twice-born am I, the first-born Son of Order: the Cow milked this when first she had her being.

10.61.d: अधासु मन्द्रो अरतिर्विभावाव सयति दविवर्तनिर्वनेषाट | ऊर्ध्वा यच्छ्रेणिर्न शिशुर्दन मक्षू सथिरंशेव्र्धं सूत माता ||
10.61.e: So mid these tribes he rests, the friendly envoy, borne on two paths, refulgent Lord of fuel.  When, like a line, the Babe springs up erectly, his Mother straight hath borne him strong to bless us.

10.61.d: अधा गाव उपमातिं कनाया अनु शवान्तस्य कस्य चित्परेयुः | शरुधि तवं सुद्रविणो नस्त्वं याळ आश्वघ्नस्यववर्धे सून्र्ताभिः ||
10.61.e: Then went the milch-kine forth to please the damsel, and for the good of every man that liveth.  Hear us, O wealthy Lord; begin our worship. Thou hast grown mighty through Āśvaghna's virtues.

10.61.d: अध तवमिन्द्र विद्ध्यस्मान महो राये नर्पते वज्रबाहुः | रक्षा च नो मघोनह पाहि सूरीननेहसस्ते हरिवोभिष्टौ ||
10.61.e: And take thou notice of us also, Indra, for ample riches, King whose arm wields thunder!  Protect our wealthy nobles, guard our princes unmenaced near thee, Lord of Tawny Coursers.

10.61.d: अध यद राजाना गविष्टौ सरत सरण्युः कारवेजरण्युः | विप्रः परेष्ठः स हयेषां बभूव परा चवक्षदुत पर्षदेनान ||
10.61.e: When he goes forth, ye Pair of Kings, for booty, speeding to war and praise to please the singer,—  I was the dearest sage of those about him,—let him lead these away and bring them safely.

10.61.d: अधा नवस्य जेन्यस्य पुष्टौ वर्था रेभन्त ईमहे तदूनु | सरण्युरस्य सूनुरश्वो विप्रश्चासि शरवसश्चसातौ ||
10.61.e: Now for this noble man's support and comfort, singing with easy voice we thus implore thee:  Impetuous be his son and fleet his courser: and may I be his priest to win him glory.

10.61.d: युवोर्यदि सख्यायास्मे शर्धाय सतोमं जुजुषे नमस्वान्विश्वत्र यस्मिन्ना गिरः समीचीः पूर्वीव गतूर्दाशत सून्र्तायै ||
10.61.e: If, for our strength, the priest with adoration to win your friendship made the laud accepted,  That laud shall be a branching road to virtue for every one to whom the songs are suited.

10.61.d: स गर्णानो अद्भिर्देववानिति सुबन्धुर्नमसा सूक्तैः | वर्धदुक्थैर्वचोभिरा हि नूनं वयध्वैति पयसौस्रियायाः ||
10.61.e: Glorified thus, with holy hymns and homage:—Of noble race, with Waters, God-attended—  May he enrich us for our prayers and praises: now can the cow be milked; the path is open.

10.61.d: त ऊ षु णो महो यजत्रा भूत देवास ऊतये सजोषाः | ये वाजाननयता वियन्तो ये सथा निचेतारो अमूराः ||
10.61.e: Be to us, then, ye Gods who merit worship, be ye of one accord our strong protection,  Who went on various ways and brought us vigour, ye who are undeceivable explorers.

10.62.d: ये यज्ञेन दक्षिणया समक्ता इन्द्रस्य सख्यमम्र्तत्वमानश | तेभ्यो भद्रमङगिरसो वो अस्तु परति गर्भ्णीतमानवं सुमेधसः ||
10.62.e: YE, who, adorned with guerdon through the sacrifice, have won you Indra's friendship and eternal life,  Even to you be happiness, Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise.

10.62.d: य उदाजन पितरो गोमयं वस्व रतेनाभिन्दन परिवत्सरेवलम | दीर्घायुत्वमङगिरसो वो अस्तु परति गर्भ्णीतमानवं सुमेधसः ||
10.62.e: The Fathers, who drave forth the wealth in cattle, have in the year's courses cleft Vala by Eternal Law:  A lengthened life be yours, O ye Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise.

10.62.d: य रतेन सूर्यमारोहयन दिव्यप्रथयन पर्थिवीं मातरंवि | सुप्रजास्त्वमङगिरसो वो अस्तु परति गर्भ्णीत मानवंसुमेधसः ||
10.62.e: Ye raised the Sun to heaven by everlasting Law, and spread broad earth, the Mother, out on every side.  Fair wealth of progeny be yours, Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise.

10.62.d: अयं नाभा वदति वल्गु वो गर्हे देवपुत्रा रषयस्तच्छ्र्णोतन | सुब्रह्मण्यमङगिरसो वो अस्तु परति गर्भ्णीतमानवं सुमेधसः ||
10.62.e: This kinsman in your dwellingplace speaks pleasant words: give car to this, ye Ṛṣis, children of the Gods.  High Brahman dignity be yours, Aṅgirases. Welcome the son of Manu, ye who are most wise.

10.62.d: विरूपास इद रषयस्त इद गम्भीरवेपसः | ते अङगिरसःसूनवस्ते अग्नेः परि जज्ञिरे ||
10.62.e: Distinguished by their varied form, these Ṛṣis have been deeply moved.  These are the sons of Aṅgirases: from Agni have they sprung to life.

10.62.d: ये अग्नेः परि जज्ञिरे विरूपासो दिवस परि | नवग्वो नुदशग्वो अङगिरस्तमो सचा देवेषु मंअते ||
10.62.e: Distinguished by their varied form, they sprang from Agni, from the sky.  Navagva and Daśagva, noblest Aṅgiras, he giveth bounty with the Gods.

10.62.d: इन्द्रेण युजा निः सर्जन्त वाघतो वरजं गोमन्तमश्विनम | सहस्रं मे ददतो अष्टकर्ण्यः शरवो देवेष्वक्रत ||
10.62.e: With Indra for associate the priests have cleared the stable full of steeds and kine,  Giving to me a thousand with their eightmarked cars, they gained renown among the Gods.

10.62.d: पर नूनं जायतामयं मनुस्तोक्मेव रोहतु | यः सहस्रंशताश्वं सद्यो दानाय मंहते ||
10.62.e: May this man's sons be multiplied; like springing corn may Manu grow,  Who gives at once in bounteous gift a thousand kine, a hundred steeds.

10.62.d: न तमश्नोति कश्चन दिव इव सान्वारभम | सावर्ण्यस्य दक्षिणा वि सिन्धुरिव पप्रथे ||
10.62.e: No one attains to him, as though a man would grasp the heights of heaven.  Savarnya's sacrificial meed hath broadened like an ample flood.

10.62.d: उत दासा परिविषे समद्दिष्टी गोपरीणसा | यदुस्तुर्वश्च मामहे ||
10.62.e: Yadu and Turva, too, have given two Dāsas, well-disposed, to serve,  Together with great store of kine.

10.62.d: सहस्रदा गरामणीर्मा रिषन मनुः सूर्येणास्ययतमानैतु दक्षिणा | सावर्णेर्देवाः पर तिरन्त्वायुर्यस्मिन्नश्रान्ता असनाम वाजम ||
10.62.e: Blest be the hamlet's chief, most liberal Manu, and may his bounty rival that of Sūrya.  May the God let Ssvarni's life be leng  thened, with whom, unwearied, we have lived and prospered.

10.63.d: परावतो ये दिधिषन्त आप्यं मनुप्रीतासो जनिमाविवस्वतः | ययातेर्ये नहुष्यस्य बर्हिषि देवा आसते तेधि बरुवन्तु नः ||
10.63.e: MAY they who would assume kinship from far away, Vivasvān's generations, dearly loved of men,  Even the Gods who sit upon the sacred grass of Nahuṣa's son Yayāti, bless and comfort us.

10.63.d: विश्वा हि वो नमस्यानि वन्द्या नामानि देवा उत यज्ञियानिवः | ये सथ जाता अदितेरब्ध्यस परि ये पर्थिव्यास्तेम इह शरुता हवम ||
10.63.e: For worthy of obeisance, Gods, are all your names, worthy of adoration and of sacrifice.  Ye who were born from waters, and from Aditi, and from the earth, do ye here listen to my call.

10.63.d: येभ्यो माता मधुमत पिन्वते पयः पीयूषं दयौरदितिरद्रिबर्हाः | उक्थशुष्मान वर्षभरान सवप्नसस्तानादित्याननु मदा सवस्तये ||
10.63.e: I will rejoice in these Ādityas for my weal, for whom the Mother pours forth water rich in balm,  And Dyaus the Infinite, firm as a rock, sweet milk,—Gods active, strong through lauds, whose might the Bull upholds.

10.63.d: नर्चक्षसो अनिमिषन्तो अर्हणा बर्हद देवासो अम्र्तत्वमानशुः | जयोतीरथा अहिमाया अनागसो दिवो वर्ष्माणंवसते सवस्तये ||
10.63.e: Looking on men, ne’er slumbering, they by their deserts attained as Gods to lofty immortality.  Borne on refulgent cars, sinless, with serpents' powers, they robe them, for our welfare, in the height of heaven.

10.63.d: सम्राजो ये सुव्र्धो यज्ञमाययुरपरिह्व्र्ता दधिरे दिविक्षयम | ताना विवास नमसा सुव्र्क्तिभिर्महो आदित्यानदितिं सवस्तये ||
10.63.e: Great Kings who bless us, who have come to sacrifice, who, ne’er assailed, have set their mansion in the sky,—  These I invite with adoration and with hymns, mighty Ādityas, Aditi, for happiness.

10.63.d: को व सतोमं राधति यं जुजोषथ विश्वे देवासो मनुषोयति षठन | को वो.अध्वरं तुविजाता अरं करद यो नःपर्षदत्यंहः सवस्तये ||
10.63.e: Who offereth to you the laud that ye accept, O ye All-Gods of Manu, many as ye are?  Who, Mighty Ones, will prepare for you the sacrifice to bear us over trouble to felicity?

10.63.d: येभ्यो होत्रां परथमामायेजे मनुः समिद्धाग्निर्मनसासप्त होत्र्भिः | त आदित्या अभयं शर्म यछत सुगा नःकर्त सुपथा सवस्तये ||
10.63.e: Ye to whom Manu, by seven priests, with kindled fire, offered the first oblation with his heart and soul,  Vouchsafe us, ye Ādityas, sheitcr free from fear, and make us good and easy paths to happiness.

10.63.d: य ईशिरे भुवनस्य परचेतसो विश्वस्य सथातुर्जगतश्चमन्तवः | ते नः कर्तादक्र्तादेनसस पर्यद्या देवासःपिप्र्ता सवस्तये ||
10.63.e: Wise Deities, who have dominion o’er the world, ye thinkers over all that moves not and that moves,  Save us from uncommitted and committed sin, preserve us from all sin to-day for happiness.

10.63.d: भरेष्विन्द्रं सुहवं हवामहे.अंहोमुचं सुक्र्तन्दैव्यं जनम | अग्निं मित्रं वरुणं सातये भगन्द्यावाप्र्थिवी मरुतः सवस्तये ||
10.63.e: In battles we invoke Indra still swift to hear, and all the holy Host of Heaven who banish grief,  Agni, Mitra, and Varuṇa that we may gain, Dyays, Bhaga, Maruts, Prthivi for happiness:

10.63.d: सुत्रामाणं पर्थिवीं दयामनेहसं सुशर्माणमदितिंसुप्रणीतिम | दैवीं नावं सवरित्रामनागसमस्रवन्तीमा रुहेमा सवस्तये ||
10.63.e: Mightily-saving Earth, incomparable Heaven the good guide Aditi who gives secure defence  The well-oared heavenly Ship that lets no waters in, free from defect, will we ascend for happiness.

10.63.d: विश्वे यजत्रा अधि वोचतोतये तरायध्वं नो दुरेवायाभिह्रुतः | सत्यया वो देवहूत्या हुवेम शर्ण्वतो देवावसे सवस्तये ||
10.63.e: Bless us, all Holy Ones, that we may have your help, guard and protect us from malignant injury.  With fruitful invocation may we call on you, Gods, who give ear to us for grace, for happiness.

10.63.d: अपामीवामप विश्वामनाहुतिमपारातिं दुर्विदत्रामघायतः | आरे देवा दवेषो अस्मद युयोतनोरु णः शर्मयछता सवस्तये ||
10.63.e: Keep all disease afar and sordid sacrifice, keep off the wicked man's malicious enmity.  Keep far away from us all hatred, O ye Gods, and give us ample shelter for our happiness.

10.63.d: अरिष्टः स मर्तो विश्व एधते पर परजाभिर्जायतेधर्मणस परि | यमादित्यासो नयथा सुनीतिभिरतिविश्वानि दुरिता सवस्तये ||
10.63.e: Untouched by any evil, every mortal thrives, and, following the Law, spreads in his progeny.  Whom ye with your good guidance, O Ādityas, lead safely through all his pain and grief to happiness.

10.63.d: यं देवासो.अवथ वाजसातौ यं शूरसाता मरुतो हितेधने | परातर्यावाणं रथमिन्द्र सानसिमरिष्यन्तमारुहेमा सवस्तये ||
10.63.e: That which ye guard and grace in battle, O ye Gods, ye Maruts, where the prize is wealth, where heroes win,  That conquering Car, O Indra, that sets forth at dawn, that never breaks, may we ascend for happiness.

10.63.d: सवस्ति नः पथ्यासु धन्वसु सवस्त्यप्सु वर्जने सवर्वति | सवस्ति नः पुत्रक्र्थेषु योनिषु सवस्ति राये मरुतो दधातन ||
10.63.e: Vouchsafe us blessing in our paths and desert tracts, blessing in waters and in battle, for the light;  Blessing upon the wombs that bring male children forth, and blessing, O ye Maruts, for the gain of wealth.

10.63.d: सवस्तिरिद धि परपथे शरेष्ठा रेक्णस्वत्यभि यावाममेति | सा नो अमा सो अरणे नि पातु सवावेशा भवतुदेवगोपा ||
10.63.e: The noblest Svasti with abundant riches, who comes to what is good by distant pathway,—  May she at home and far away preserve us, and dwell with us under the Gods’ protection

10.63.d: एवा पलतेः सूनुरवीव्र्धद वो विश्व आदित्या अदितेमनीषी | ईशानासो नरो अमर्त्येनास्तावि जनो दिव्योगयेन ||
10.63.e: Thus hatb the thoughtful sage, the son of Plati, praised you, O Aditi and all Ādityas,  Men are made rich by those who are Immortal: the Heavenly Folk have been extolled by Gaya.

10.64.d: कथा देवानां कतमस्य यामनि सुमन्तु नाम शर्ण्वताम्मनामहे | को मर्ळाति कतमो नो मयस करत कतम ऊती अभ्या ववर्तति ||
10.64.e: WHAT God, of those who hear, is he whose well-praised name we may record in this our sacrifice; and how?  Who will be gracious? Who of many give us bliss? Who out of all the Host will come to lend us aid?

10.64.d: करतूयन्ति करतवो हर्त्सु धीतयो वेनन्ति वेनाः पतयन्त्या दिशः | न मर्डिता विद्यते अन्य एभ्यो देवेषु मे अधिकामा अयंसत ||
10.64.e: The will and thoughts within my breast exert their power: they yearn with love, and fly to all the regions round.  None other comforter is found save only these: my longings and my hopes are fixt upon the Gods.

10.64.d: नरा वा शंसं पूषणमगोह्यमग्निं देवेद्धमभ्यर्चसे गिरा | सूर्यामासा चन्द्रमसा यमं दिवि तरितंवातमुषसमक्तुमश्विना ||
10.64.e: To Narāśaṁsa and to Pūṣan I sing forth, unconcealable Agni kindied by the Gods.  To Sun and Moon, two Moons, to Yama in the heaven, to Trita, Vāta, Dawn, Night, and the Atvins Twain.

10.64.d: कथा कविस्तुवीरवान कया गिरा बर्हस्पतिर्वाव्र्धतेसुव्र्क्तिभिः | अज एकपात सुहवेभिरकवभिरहिः शर्णोतुबुध्न्यो हवीमनि ||
10.64.e: How is the Sage extolled whom the loud singers praise? What voice, what hymn is used to laud Bṛhaspati?  May Aja-Ekapād with Rkvans swift to hear, and Ahi of the Deep listen unto our call.

10.64.d: दक्षस्य वादिते जन्मनि वरते राजाना मित्रावरुणाविवाससि | अतूर्तपन्थाः पुरुरथो अर्यमा सप्तहोताविषुरूपेषु जन्मसु ||
10.64.e: Aditi, to the birth of Dakṣa and the vow thou summonest the Kings Mitra and Varuṇa.  With course unchecked, with many chariots Aryaman comes with the seven priests to tribes of varied sort.

10.64.d: ते नो अर्वन्तो हवनश्रुतो हवं विश्वे शर्ण्वन्तु वाजिनोमितद्रवः | सहस्रसा मेधसाताविव तमना महो येधनं समिथेषु जभ्रिरे ||
10.64.e: May all those vigorous Coursers listen to our cry, hearers of invocation, speeding on their way;  Winners of thousands where the priestly meed is won, who gather of themselves great wealth in every race.

10.64.d: पर वो वायुं रथयुजं पुरन्धिं सतोमैः कर्णुध्वंसख्याय पूषणम | ते हि देवस्य सवितुः सवीमनिक्रतुं सचन्ते सचितः सचेतसः ||
10.64.e: Bring ye Purandbi, bring Vāyu who yokes his steeds, for friendship bring ye Pūṣan with your songs of praise:  They with one mind, one thought attend the sacrifice, urged by the favouring aid of Savitar the God.

10.64.d: तरिः सप्त सस्रा नद्यो महीरपो वनस्पतीन पर्वतानग्निमूतये | कर्शानुमस्तॄन तिष्यं सधस्थ आ रुद्रंरुद्रेषु रुद्रियं हवामहे ||
10.64.e: The thrice-seven wandering Rivers, yea, the mighty floods, the forest trees, the mountains, Agni to our aid,  Kṛśānu, Tisya, archers to our gathering-place, and Rudra strong amid the Rudras we invoke.

10.64.d: सरस्वती सरयुः सिन्धुरूर्मिभिर्महो महीरवसा यन्तुवक्षणीः | देवीरापो मातरः सूदयित्न्वो घर्तवत पयोमधुमन नो अर्चत ||
10.64.e: Let the great Streams come hither with their mighty help, Sindhu, Sarasvatī, and Sarayu with waves.  Ye Goddess Floods, ye Mothers, animating all, promise us water rich in fatness and in balm.

10.64.d: उत माता बर्हद्दिवा शर्णोतु नस्त्वष्टा देवेभिर्जनिभिःपिता वचः | रभुक्षा वाजो रथस्पतिर्भगो रण्वःशण्सः शशमानस्य पातु नः ||
10.64.e: And let Brhaddiva, the Mother, hear our call, and Tvaṣṭar, Father, with the Goddesses and Dames.  Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja, Bhaga, and Rathaspati, and the sweet speech of him who labours guard us well!

10.64.d: रण्वः सन्द्र्ष्टौ पितुमानिव कषयो भद्रा रुद्राणाम्मरुतामुपस्तुतिः | गोभिः षयाम यशसो जनेष्वा सदादेवास इळया सचेमहि ||
10.64.e: Pleasant to look on as a dwelling rich in food is the blest favour of the Maruts, Rudra's Sons.  May we be famed among the folk for wealth in kine. and ever come to you, ye Gods, with sacred food.

10.64.d: यां मे धियं मरुत इन्द्र देवा अददात वरुण मित्र यूयम | तां पीपयत पयसेव धेनुं कुविद गिरो अधि रथेवहाथ ||
10.64.e: The thought which ye, O Maruts, Indra and ye Gods have given to me, and ye, Mitra and Varuṇa,—  Cause this to grow and swell like a milchcow with milk. Will ye not bear away my songs upon your car?

10.64.d: कुविदङग परति यथा चिदस्य नः सजात्यस्य मरुतोबुबोधथ | नाभा यत्र परथमं संनशामहे तत्रजामित्वमदितिर्दधातु नः ||
10.64.e: O Maruts, do ye never, never recollect and call again to mind this our relationship?  When next we meet together at the central point, even there shall Aditi confirm our brotherhood.

10.64.d: ते हि दयावाप्र्थिवी मातरा मही देवी देवाञ जन्मनायज्ञिये इतः | उभे बिभ्र्त उभयं भरीमभिः पुरूरेतांसि पित्र्भिश्च सिञ्चतः ||
10.64.e: The Mothers, Heaven and Earth, those mighty Goddesses, worthy of sacrifice, ecune with the race of Gods.  These Two with their support uphold both Gods and men, and with the Fathers pour the copious genial stream.

10.64.d: वि षा होत्रा विश्वमश्नोति वार्यं बर्हस्पतिररमतिःपनीयसी | गरावा यत्र मधुषुदुच्यते बर्हदवीवशन्तमतिभिर्मनीषिणः ||
10.64.e: This invocation wins all good that we desire Bṛhaspati, highly-praised Aramati, are here,  Even where the stone that presses meath rings loudly out, and where the sages make their voices heard with hymns.

10.64.d: एवा कविस्तुवीरवान रतज्ञा दरविणस्युर्द्रविणसश्चकानः | उक्थेभिरत्र मतिभिश्च विप्रो.अपीपयद गयोदिव्यानि जन्म ||
10.64.e: Thus hath the sage, skilled in loud singers' duties, desiring riches, yearning after treasure,  Gaya, the priestly singer, with his praises and hymns contented the Celestial people.
Thus hath the thoughtful sage the son of Plati, praised you, O Aaiti and all Ādityas.  Men are made rich by those who are Immortal: the Heavenly Folk have been extolled by Gaya.

10.65.d: अग्निरिन्द्रो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा वायुः पूषा सरस्वतीसजोषसः | आदित्या विष्णुर्मरुतः सवर्ब्र्हत सोमो रुद्रोदितिर्ब्रह्मणस पतिः ||
10.65.e: MAY Agni, Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa consent, Aryaman, Vāyu, Pūṣan, and Sarasvatī,  Ādityas, Maruts, Viṣṇu, Soma, lofty Sky, Rudra and Aditi, and Brahmaṇaspati.

10.65.d: इन्द्राग्नी वर्त्रहत्येषु सत्पती मिथो हिन्वाना तन्वासमोकसा | अन्तरिक्षं मह्या पप्रुरोजसा सोमो घर्तश्रीर्महिमानमीरयन ||
